docs.title: agent-ops — restart resilience for agent work
docs.text: The machine/daemon restarts without warning and kills running workers. This system cannot stop that. It makes restarts survivable: workers checkpoint as they go, and after a restart the supervisor tells the parent agent exactly what died and how to re-spawn it.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File Purpose checkpoint.sh Worker checkpointing CLI (canonical tool) supervisor.sh Post-restart triage: flags stale/dead tasks, prints re-spawn briefs CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL.md The schema + rules workers follow RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md What a re-spawned worker must do, step by step IDEMPOTENCY.md How to write work so re-runs can't duplicate or corrupt it docs/MERGE-IT-YOURSELF-LAW.md Canonical owner law: merge clean green PRs yourself, never leave them for the owner checkpoints/ One JSON per task: <task_id>.json attic/ Deprecated alternate tooling (reference only)

docs.title: For the parent agent
docs.text:
Spawning a worker on a long task — include this in the brief:

Checkpoint your progress with ~/workspace/agent-ops/checkpoint.sh: init first with --goal and --resume-prompt, then beat every ~10 min and step after each unit of work. Read ~/workspace/agent-ops/IDEMPOTENCY.md and follow it.

After a restart — run the supervisor:

~/workspace/agent-ops/supervisor.sh            # stale threshold: 30 min
~/workspace/agent-ops/supervisor.sh --stale-minutes 10

It prints a ready-to-paste re-spawn brief per dead task. Paste each into a fresh subagent. The brief tells the worker to read its checkpoint and the resume template — not to redo completed steps.

docs.title: For workers
docs.text:
1. First action: checkpoint.sh init <task_id> --goal "..." --resume-prompt "...".
  2. Work in units. After each unit: checkpoint.sh step <task_id> "what you did".
  3. Long silent stretches: checkpoint.sh beat <task_id> every ~10 min.
  4. Decisions the next worker must honor: checkpoint.sh decide <task_id> "...".
  5. Blocked: checkpoint.sh block <task_id> "why". Unblocked: unblock.
  6. Done: checkpoint.sh status <task_id> completed.

Write outputs per IDEMPOTENCY.md (deterministic names, done-manifests, temp-then-move, no force-pushes).

docs.title: Honest limits
docs.text:
• Heartbeat staleness is a heuristic. A worker inside one long tool call can look stale while alive; a dead worker can look fresh if it beat right before dying. The supervisor reports; the parent agent decides.
  • Checkpoints live on this machine's disk. If the whole VM is wiped (not just restarted), checkpoints die with it — which is why important work also gets committed to its repo early and often.
  • A re-spawned worker must still verify checkpoint claims against reality (files exist? repo state matches?) before continuing. Trust, then verify.

docs.title: Muse training pack
docs.text: Muse/Ashes and every agent: read the Muse training pack (instructions, pre-flight checklist, real before/after examples, right-way videos) before every job.

docs.title: ANTI-CLOBBER LAWS (owner 2026-10-17 — the DXMMII 54k-file wipe)
docs.text:
On 2026-10-17, commit cd3bf38 ("DXMMII limb system", PR mhvnsnt/western-heart#221) deleted 54,456 files against 105 additions. The commit message said nothing about deletions. Nobody read the deletion list before merging. The repo was 99.996% gone. These laws exist so that never happens again. Every agent, every repo, every commit, every merge.

  1. DELETION CHECK — before every commit, read git status and the diff stat. Every deleted file in the diff must be something your task intended to delete. A deleted file your task did not delete on purpose means STOP: do not commit, do not push, report what you found. The working tree is wrong, not the task.

  2. OWN THE TREE — never git add -A or git commit -a in a working tree you did not fully populate yourself. Before committing, verify the tree is complete: file counts match the remote branch you branched from (your task's own additions and changes aside). A tree missing files you didn't delete is damaged — don't sweep it into history.

  3. CIRCUIT BREAKER — if a commit would delete more than a handful of files outside your task's scope, STOP and report instead of committing. A big deletion count is a hard stop, not a warning to scroll past. Committing unexplained deletions "and letting someone else figure it out" is the failure.

  4. SAY THE DELETIONS — the commit message names every deletion. One deleted file gets one line; many deleted files get a count plus what category went. A commit whose message and diff disagree is a hard failure — don't push it.

  5. MERGE GATE — the merger reads the PR's deletion list against the task description before merging. Unexplained deletions block the merge. "CI is green" does not excuse a deletion list the task never asked for. A red, conflicting, or lossy PR stays open with a comment naming the blocker.

(Co-authored with Aider and Copilot per the ALL-AGENTS-WORKFLOW LAW. Cline's seat stays open — its free-tier API was down during drafting.)

Instructions for every AI agent working in this repo.

docs.title: PRE-MADE PARTS FIRST
docs.text: PRE-MADE PARTS FIRST (Mars, 2026-11-20): Don't hand-build what already exists and works well. Before decoding, decrypting, reverse-engineering, or building anything from scratch, go get the pre-made part from wherever it already exists and work FROM it. Sources: commercial games, open source, closed-source teardowns (study from public sources, rebuild equivalents), the fan translation / ROM hacking scene, the modding community, fan-made tools and docs, decompilations (decomps) and recompilations (recomps), community knowledge (Xentax/ZenHAX, TCRF, wikis, FAQs, archive.org). Like building a machine: you don't build a battery or a cog from scratch, you order the pre-made part and keep building. Spend the work on the innovative parts, not on re-doing what's already well-built. Only build from scratch what nobody has already built.

docs.title: No-data-loss rules (MANDATORY)
docs.text: Read and follow docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md (canonical: mhvnsnt/agent-ops). No force-push, no rebase/amend of pushed work, no history rewrite, no branch/asset deletion without backup + owner approval, PRs only, empty D-filter + gitleaks + green CI before merge, push incrementally, keep WORKLOG, back up and sha256-verify before disk cleanup, never touch other agents' or Muse's work.

docs.title: NO-SPARSE-COMMIT LAW (2026-10-23 — the cape-jones #219 main wipe)
docs.text: NEVER commit or push from a sparse/partial checkout. On 2026-10-23 the overnight pipeline committed PR #219 from a sparse checkout that materialized only docs/ — the merge DELETED the other 21 root entries from cape-jones main. A sparse checkout that looks complete can silently carry deletions. RULE: before any commit from a non-full clone, verify the working tree against the branch's real tree (diff the root listing, or compare tree SHAs). Default recovery path for a bad merge: revert the merge commit (-m 1) and re-add the branch's real payload — nothing lost on either side. When in doubt, build the commit via the Git Data API from verified tree SHAs instead of a local checkout. GOTCHA: gh's -f content=@file does NOT expand @file for the blobs API — base64 the content explicitly or the blob will contain the literal path string.

docs.title: MERGE QUEUE — COMING SOON (owner-ordered briefing, 2026-10-24)
docs.text:
Read this if you work on western-heart or agent-ops. Nothing changes today. This is advance notice only.

What is changing: soon, pull requests will merge one at a time, in a line, instead of every lane merging whenever it wants. Each PR in the line gets checked against the newest main before it goes in. That is called a merge queue.

Why: two lanes merged at almost the same time and one wiped out the other's work. The line stops that happening.

What changes for your lane, once the flip happens: - Merging a PR directly will stop working. GitHub will reject a direct merge. - Instead you add your PR to the queue. GitHub merges it when its turn comes, after re-checking it against the newest main. - If the queue asks you to update your branch (because main moved under you), update it and it goes back in line. Do not force-push. Do not merge main into your branch by hand to get around it. - The merge method stays "merge". Never squash, never rebase. Same as now.

When: NOT YET. The flip happens only after every active lane has confirmed it knows. This briefing is the advance notice — today, merging works exactly the way it always has.

How to confirm: reply "merge-queue briefing confirmed" in your chat, or drop that line as a comment on your PR, or tell the merge coordinator at your next check-in. Confirmations are tracked in mhvnsnt/agent-ops at MERGE-QUEUE-BRIEFING-CONFIRMATIONS-2026-10-24.md.

Status 2026-10-24: the queue plumbing is ready on both repos (western-heart PR #742 and agent-ops PR #39 both merged the merge_group triggers). The flip itself has NOT happened. No branch protection has changed.

docs.title: NO-TEMP-STORAGE LAW (owner 2026-11-21 ~16:33 EST — "why are u storing things in temporary where they can get wiped anyway?")
docs.text: NEVER store work in /tmp or any temporary location that can be wiped. /tmp is a 512 MB tmpfs and a VM restart wipes it to zero — on 2026-11-21 it destroyed the Pyrite checkpoint, worktree, 8 proof shots, capture driver, suite log, and the Colosseum M2 extracts. That loss is the proof: anything stored in temp is already lost, it just doesn't know it yet. 1. EVERYTHING goes straight into the repo or a durable workspace directory the second it exists — checkpoints, captures, scripts, extracts, logs, proofs. Finished work belongs in the repo; nothing finished ever sits only in /tmp or only on local disk. 2. /tmp is for truly disposable scratch ONLY — something that can be regenerated in seconds and whose loss costs nothing. If losing it would cost even one minute of rework, it does not go in /tmp. 3. Any lane caught staging work in /tmp has violated the order — same as staging on local disk. Parents verify: no checkpoint, capture, script, or extract path in any brief points at /tmp. 4. Recovery from a wipe is re-derivation from the repo/release, never a shrug — the work survives because it was pushed, the temp copy is gone and stays gone. Strengthens DIRECT-TO-REPO + CHECKPOINT-AND-SAVE: the repo is the save, temp is not storage.

docs.title: AList Evaluation — TeraBox -> WebDAV -> rclone Bridge
docs.text: Cluster: FRICTION-RESEARCH 2026-10-19 · pull-in 6/6 (owner order 2026-10-19 ~23:33 CDT) Research: [[research-friction-20261019/06-browser-transfer-alternatives]] · Index: [[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX]] Status: EVALUATED 2026-10-20 — DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Nothing installed, nothing deployed. Related: [[BROWSER-TRANSFER-COOKIE-ARIA2-SOP]] (the no-service fallback lane)

docs.title: SERVICE USE ONLY — do NOT deploy without the owner's word
docs.text: AList is AGPL-3.0 and a hosted network service by design. Any deployment (binary, docker, install script) requires the owner's explicit go-ahead first. This doc evaluates; it does not authorize running it. Verdict status stays "queued" until the owner says deploy.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
• AList — a single-binary file-list / WebDAV program (Go, Gin + SolidJS) that mounts dozens of cloud storages behind one web UI, API, and WebDAV endpoint.
  • Upstream: the cluster research cites https://github.com/alist-org/alist; GitHub search this session resolves the live repo as https://github.com/AlistGo/alist (50,316 stars, 2,542 commits, active). Verify the canonical org at deploy time — do not trust either from memory.
  • License: AGPL-3.0 — verified from the repo README ("The AList is open-source software licensed under the AGPL-3.0 license") and the GitHub repo metadata line this session.

docs.title: Why it's the strongest TeraBox find
docs.text:
1. Native TeraBox driver. Source-level docs (DeepWiki, drivers/terabox/): cookie-based auth with jsToken validation and sign generation — the driver extracts a jsToken from the page HTML (drivers/terabox/util.go 49-53) and generates request signatures via a custom sign function (util.go 166-187). That is exactly the browser-session-cookie path — the only path out of TeraBox, since TeraBox publishes no official export tool, no rclone/WebDAV endpoint, and no public OAuth API (per the cluster research).
  2. It also mounts our other lanes: PikPak, BaiduNetdisk, Quark, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3, local disk, and more (README feature list) — one bridge, many sources.
  3. WebDAV out. AList serves mounted storage over WebDAV (README feature: "WebDav (see https://alist.nn.ci/guide/webdav.html for details)"). Community guides address it at http(s)://<alist-host>/dav — the official guide page could not be fetched this session (alist.nn.ci network error), so the /dav path stays to-confirm at deploy time.
  4. rclone has a Tier 1 WebDAV backend (https://rclone.org/webdav/): config keys url, vendor (other for generic servers like AList), user, pass (must be obscured via rclone obscure), bearer_token. CloudDog is already rclone-based, so once AList exists, TeraBox looks like any other rclone remote to the stores pipeline.

docs.title: The bridge architecture
docs.text:
TeraBox (owner account, browser session cookie)
   |  AList terabox driver: cookie auth + jsToken + sign
   v
AList service (single binary or docker, ONE host the owner approves)
   |  serves the TeraBox mount at /dav (WebDAV, user/pass auth)
   v
rclone remote "alist-tb" (type=webdav, vendor=other)
   |  rclone copy / ls / hash-checked pulls
   v
CloudDog stores -> GitHub / TeraBox permanent store
   |  verify hash-identical on store
   v
local copy cleared (one-store rule; disk is a cache)

Proposed rclone wiring — syntax verified against the actual rclone v1.75.2 binary's own --help on this VM (binary at ~/workspace/tools/rclone/rclone, landed by pull-in 1/6; not on PATH, so call it by full path below). End-to-end (AList side) is NOT testable until AList is deployed:

RCLONE=~/workspace/tools/rclone/rclone

# One-time remote setup (deploy lane, after owner approval).
# config create takes key=value pairs; password fields are auto-obscured
# (pass --obscure to be certain, per the command's own help).
"$RCLONE" config create alist-tb webdav \
  url="https://<alist-host>/dav" \
  vendor=other \
  user="<alist-user>" \
  pass="<alist-password>" --obscure

"$RCLONE" lsd alist-tb:/                    # smoke test: list the TeraBox mount
"$RCLONE" copy alist-tb:/<path> /tmp/pull/  # pull
"$RCLONE" check alist-tb:/<path> /tmp/pull/ --download
# check compares sizes + hashes; --download forces byte-level comparison,
# which is the safe mode for WebDAV remotes with weak hash support

docs.title: AGPL-3.0 — what it means for us (honest read)
docs.text:
• Running the unmodified upstream binary/docker as an internal service = the intended "service use" and the only approved mode. No vendoring AList source into any repo of ours, no forks, no patches, no rebranding.
  • AGPL's network clause (section 13) is written for exactly this shape: users interacting with a modified version over a network must be offered its source. Running upstream unmodified, with the upstream source link intact, keeps us on the safe side of that clause. If we ever need a modified build, that's a new owner decision with the source offer planned first.
  • Hosted-service implication: an AList instance holds live cloud cookies (TeraBox, PikPak, etc.). It is a credential-bearing service — bind it to localhost / the tailnet only, never public-internet exposure, credentials via the Secure Vault pattern, never in code or config committed to a repo.
  • This is the same pattern as the repo's other AGPL tools (e.g. FreeMoCap AGPL-3.0, documented-only / runtime-install): use it, don't fork it.

docs.title: Risks and open questions (for the deploy lane, not blockers to this eval)
docs.text:
• Cookie freshness is the operational weakness. TeraBox expires cookies on logout / password change / inactivity — the AList mount will need the same "refresh cookies" step as the SOP lane. Surface it as a named step, not a failure.
  • Upstream breakage risk. The driver depends on TeraBox's web internals (jsToken, sign); TeraBox UI/API changes can break it until upstream patches. Fallback = the cookie->aria2 SOP ([[BROWSER-TRANSFER-COOKIE-ARIA2-SOP]]).
  • WebDAV hash support. rclone WebDAV remotes vary in hash support by server; the end-to-end check (mount -> copy -> hash match) must be proven at deploy before the lane is declared green. Until then, verify pulled bytes with sha256sum locally per the SOP.
  • /dav path and the current docs home (alist.nn.ci vs alistgo.com) need a live confirm at deploy time; the official WebDAV guide failed to fetch this session.
  • What is NOT decided here: deploy host, credentials handling, exposure, version pin. All owner-gated.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
• Evaluation: PASS as documented. AList is the right bridge design for the TeraBox pull problem (native driver + WebDAV + rclone Tier 1), license understood, risks named.
  • Deployment: BLOCKED on owner's word (AGPL + hosted-service implications, per task). Queue #16 stays "queued" in [[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX]] with this doc as its evaluation.
  • Fallback lane already documented: [[BROWSER-TRANSFER-COOKIE-ARIA2-SOP]] needs no service at all — cookies + aria2/curl, works as soon as the lane tools are installed.

Index: [[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX]]

docs.title: The incident
docs.text:
On 2026-10-17, commit cd3bf38 ("DXMMII limb system", branch feat/dxmmii-limb-system, merged via PR mhvnsnt/western-heart#221) deleted 54,456 files against 105 legitimate additions. The agent committed from a working tree that was missing tens of thousands of files; git add -A swept every missing file in as a deletion. The commit message said nothing about deletions. Nobody checked the deletion list before committing or merging.

The 105 additions were the agent's real work (all under tools/limb-system/dxmmii/). Everything deleted was recovered from git history — but it should never have happened.

How a tree gets gutted (any one of these is enough): - Working in a directory that isn't a complete clone (partial checkout, interrupted clone, or files removed to "save disk"). - A cleanup process, VM replacement, or another lane deleting files out from under the working tree. - The agent itself deleting directories it didn't think it needed.

In every case the failure is the same: git add -A turns "files missing from my tree" into "files deleted from the repo", silently.

docs.title: The law
docs.text:
1. Read your deletions before every commit. Run git status and git diff --cached --name-status. Every deleted file must be something your task meant to delete. If you see deletions you can't explain, STOP. Do not commit. Assume your environment is corrupted — do not try to "fix" it by committing.
  2. Never git add -A or git commit -a in a tree you didn't fully populate yourself. If you didn't clone it and watch it finish, verify the tree is complete first — compare file counts against the remote branch. A tree missing files turns every missing file into a deletion the second you stage everything.
  3. Say what you deleted, in the commit message. If you delete files, the message names the directories or file types and why. If the message says one thing and the diff shows 50,000 deletions, that's a hard failure — do not push it.
  4. Deletion circuit breaker. Any deletion outside your task's scope blocks the commit. "My task touches 10 files but the commit deletes 500" is never fine. Stop and report instead of committing.
  5. The merger checks the deletion list. Before merging any PR, read what it deletes and match it against the task. Deletions the task doesn't explain block the merge. A giant diff's deletions are never "probably fine."

docs.title: Co-authors
docs.text: Written with the full agent team per the owner's TEAM RELAY LAW and ALL-AGENTS-WORKFLOW LAW: Aider (rule 1 wording, the "assume your environment is corrupted" framing, and the hallucinated-deletion gap behind rule 3), Copilot (rule 1 name-status inspection, rule 4's clear stop condition). Cline was unresponsive at drafting time (its free-tier API hung); proceeded without it per the workflow law's exception clause.

docs.title: Propagation
docs.text: This law is appended to every mhvnsnt repo's AGENTS.md, each via branch → PR → merge per the MERGE-IT-YOURSELF LAW. This file is the canonical text; repo copies reference it.

1. Nothing goes on local disk that can go straight to TeraBox, Google Drive, a Kaggle dataset, or a GitHub release.
  2. After every turn of work, push outputs to a store; clear local once verified on the store.
  3. Disk is a cache: keep it under 75%. Active work only on disk.
  4. TeraBox has 5TB and is barely used (~27GB) — it is the primary bulk store.

docs.title: Cookie -> aria2/curl Lane SOP (browser-transfer replacement)
docs.text: Cluster: FRICTION-RESEARCH 2026-10-19 · pull-in 6/6 (owner order 2026-10-19 ~23:33 CDT: "Fix it all wire it all in wire it all up pull it all in") Research: [[research-friction-20261019/06-browser-transfer-alternatives]] · Index: [[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX]] Status: SOP DOCUMENTED 2026-10-20 — docs only; queue #17 script (tools/dl/tb-pull.sh) and #15 rclone install still belong to the CloudDog integration lane Related: [[ALIST-TERABOX-WEBDAV-EVALUATION]] (the preferred TeraBox path, owner-gated)

docs.title: Why this SOP exists
docs.text:
TeraBox .blend downloads (794MB + 515MB) failed 10/10 via the browser file-transfer tool — every attempt returned "transfer's outcome is unknown" with zero file references. The browser transfer path is unreliable for large files, and no native rclone TeraBox backend exists (verified across rclone backend lists — the only path out is the browser session cookie). This SOP is the recipe for pulling a file with zero browser-tool involvement after the initial cookie capture: export cookies from a signed-in browser session once, then download from the shell with resume, segmentation, retries, and hash verification.

Every flag below was verified against the real tool docs this session (Ubuntu aria2c manpage, openSUSE yt-dlp manpage, gallery-dl upstream options.md, local curl --help) — no training-data flags.

docs.title: Tool availability on this VM (checked 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
• curl 8.5.0 — INSTALLED (flags verified via curl --help all)
  • rclone v1.75.2 — LANDED as a static binary at ~/workspace/tools/rclone/rclone (SHA256-verified, smoke-tested by pull-in 1/6; not on PATH — call it by full path or set RCLONE_PATH). Its WebDAV backend + config create/copy/check were verified against this binary's own --help for [[ALIST-TERABOX-WEBDAV-EVALUATION]].
  • aria2c, yt-dlp, gallery-dl — NOT installed on this VM. Installing them belongs to the CloudDog integration lane, NOT this doc. All flags below are documented from the tools' real manpages/options, so the SOP is copy-paste ready the moment they land.

docs.title: Step 0 — Get the direct URL and the cookies
docs.text:
1. Direct URL. The browser transfer tool is out of the loop. The download URL comes from the source's own page/API (TeraBox share page, archive.org metadata API, host's "direct link" button), or from a resolver: yt-dlp -g / gallery-dl -g (see section 4), or the AList TeraBox driver ([[ALIST-TERABOX-WEBDAV-EVALUATION]], owner-gated).
  2. Cookies. From the signed-in browser (local-only add-ons only — "Get cookies.txt LOCALLY" for Chrome, "Export Cookies" for Firefox — never remote-export extensions): save as /tmp/cookies-<source>.txt (Netscape/Mozilla format). chmod 600 it. aria2c reads Firefox/Mozilla/Chromium cookie files without modification (aria2c manpage).
  3. Never commit cookies. They live in /tmp or come through the Secure Vault flow. Delete after the lane finishes. Cookies expire on logout / password change / inactivity (TeraBox behavior) — treat "401/403 on first byte" as "refresh cookies", not a tool bug.

docs.title: Step 1 — aria2c (primary: segmented, resume-capable)
docs.text:
--load-cookies, -c, -x, -s, -k, -m, --retry-wait, --dry-run all verified in the aria2c manpage (manpages.ubuntu.com, focal).

# 0. Sanity: is the session still alive? (dry-run checks availability, downloads nothing)
aria2c --dry-run=true --load-cookies=/tmp/cookies-terabox.txt \
  "https://<direct-download-url>"

# 1. The download. 16 conns/server, 16-way split, resume on, retry 10x w/ 5s wait,
#    no splits smaller than 10M, fail fast on HTTP errors handled by -m/--retry-wait.
aria2c \
  -c \
  -x16 -s16 \
  --min-split-size=10M \
  -m 10 --retry-wait=5 \
  --connect-timeout=30 --timeout=120 \
  --load-cookies=/tmp/cookies-terabox.txt \
  -d /tmp/tbpull \
  -o target-name.blend \
  "https://<direct-download-url>"

Behavior notes (all from the manpage):

  • -c/--continue resumes a partially downloaded file; the .aria2 control file tracks byte ranges across runs. It also resumes downloads started by a web browser.
  • -x/--max-connection-per-server (default 1) × -s/--split (default 5): splits only take effect per -k/--min-split-size (default 20M, range 1M-1024M). A 100MB file with -s16 -k10M yields ~10 real segments; don't overshoot -s beyond what -k allows.
  • -m/--max-tries default is 5; 0 = unlimited. --retry-wait applies between retries and triggers on HTTP 503.
  • -d/--dir + -o/--out: -o is always relative to -d.
  • Optional integrity check when you know the hash: --checksum=sha-1=<hexdigest> (the manpage's documented example is sha-1=0192ba11...). Run aria2c -v on the lane to see which hash types the build supports (sha-256 depends on the build).

Discover more: aria2c --help=#http, --help=#cookie, --help=#all (tag system verified).

docs.title: Step 2 — curl fallback (always available on this VM)
docs.text:
Flags verified against local curl --help all (curl 8.5.0):

# Auth probe: headers only, cookies attached, fail fast on HTTP errors
curl -sIL -f -b /tmp/cookies-terabox.txt "https://<direct-download-url>" | head -20

# The download: follow redirects, fail fast, auto-resume partials,
# retry 10x with 5s delay on transient errors
curl -L -f -C - \
  -b /tmp/cookies-terabox.txt \
  --retry 10 --retry-delay 5 --retry-all-errors \
  -o /tmp/tbpull/target-name.blend \
  "https://<direct-download-url>"
  • -C - = auto resume from the existing local file's size. Safe on a fresh start too.
  • -f/--fail fails fast with no output on HTTP errors (4xx/5xx) — without it curl happily saves an error page as your .blend.
  • --retry-all-errors extends retries beyond transient network errors (use with judgment; it will also retry 4xx — for an auth-expired cookie you WANT the fail-fast signal, so watch the first failure's code).

docs.title: Step 3 — Verify bytes, then clear
docs.text:
cd /tmp/tbpull
sha256sum target-name.blend > target-name.blend.sha256   # record what you got
# If the source publishes an expected hash:
echo "<expected-sha256>  target-name.blend" | sha256sum -c -
stat -c '%s %n' target-name.blend                         # size sanity

Delete-as-you-go (owner 2026-10-19): once the blob verifies hash-identical on the store, drop the local copy during upload — disk falls mid-download, not after.

docs.title: Worked example — the TeraBox .blend case that motivated this
docs.text:
export TB=/tmp/tbpull/madelyn-blends && mkdir -p "$TB"
chmod 600 /tmp/cookies-terabox.txt

# One share link, known file name, no browser tool anywhere in the loop:
aria2c -c -x16 -s16 --min-split-size=10M \
  -m 10 --retry-wait=5 \
  --load-cookies=/tmp/cookies-terabox.txt \
  -d "$TB" -o scene_a.blend \
  "https://<terabox-direct-download-url-for-scene_a.blend>"

sha256sum "$TB"/scene_a.blend
# -> push to GitHub release / TeraBox per store law, verify, then clear local
rm -f /tmp/cookies-terabox.txt   # cookies never outlive the lane

If the direct URL is a share page (not a file URL), resolve it first: AList TeraBox driver (owner-gated, [[ALIST-TERABOX-WEBDAV-EVALUATION]]) or a site-specific resolver — then feed the resolved URL into this recipe.

docs.title: 4. yt-dlp and gallery-dl: the direct-link lane standards
docs.text:
Rule of thumb: reach for these BEFORE any browser involvement, for every host that is not TeraBox. Neither covers TeraBox (yt-dlp has no TeraBox extractor — verified in the cluster research).

Tool Reach for it when Don't use it for yt-dlp Video/audio/streaming hosts (1,000+ extractors), HLS/DASH manifests, playlists. -g prints the direct media URL to hand to aria2/curl. TeraBox shares (no extractor). Sites needing JS-heavy auth flows. gallery-dl Image galleries / media collections (boorus, art sites, social galleries). -g dry-runs the direct URLs. Video hosts (yt-dlp's territory), TeraBox.

Verified commands (openSUSE yt-dlp manpage; gallery-dl upstream docs/options.md):

# --- yt-dlp: give me the direct link (no download) ---
yt-dlp --cookies /tmp/cookies-site.txt -g "https://<page-url>"
# -g/--get-url is --print urls; --cookies takes a Netscape-format file;
# --cookies-from-browser BROWSER works too (brave/chrome/chromium/edge/firefox/opera/safari/vivaldi/whale)

# --- yt-dlp: full authenticated pull, aria2c doing the bytes ---
yt-dlp --cookies /tmp/cookies-site.txt \
  -R 10 -N 16 \
  -o "/tmp/dl/%(title)s.%(ext)s" \
  --downloader aria2c \
  --downloader-args "aria2c:-c -x16 -s16" \
  "https://<page-url>"
# -R/--retries (default 10), -N/--concurrent-fragments, -o output template,
# --downloader aria2c (alias: --external-downloader), --downloader-args "NAME:ARGS"

# --- gallery-dl: dry-run the direct URLs ---
gallery-dl -g --cookies /tmp/cookies-site.txt "https://<gallery-url>"
# -g/--get-urls prints URLs instead of downloading; -G/--resolve-urls also
# resolves intermediaries; -C/--cookies is the short form of --cookies

# --- gallery-dl: authenticated gallery pull ---
gallery-dl --cookies /tmp/cookies-site.txt \
  -d /tmp/dl \
  -R 4 --download-archive /tmp/dl/archive.txt \
  "https://<gallery-url>"
# -d/--destination, -R/--retries, --download-archive skips already-grabbed files

Cookie rules from section 0 apply to both tools (local export only, /tmp, chmod 600, delete after). --cookies-from-browser firefox is convenient on a lane VM with a browser profile; on headless lanes prefer the exported cookies.txt.

docs.title: Lane checklist (copy into the runbook)
docs.text:
• [ ] Direct URL resolved (not a share page) — AList / -g dry-run / page source
  • [ ] cookies.txt fresh, chmod 600, in /tmp only
  • [ ] --dry-run / curl -IL auth probe green before the big pull
  • [ ] aria2c: -c -x16 -s16 --load-cookies + retries; or curl: -L -f -C - -b + retries
  • [ ] Hash verified (sha256sum -c), size sane
  • [ ] Stored (GitHub/TeraBox), verified on store, local cleared per one-store rule
  • [ ] Cookies deleted

docs.text: Snapshot: mhvnsnt/western-heart main @ 024df77fb9d9 (2026-10-23T11:20:45Z). Every cell below was verified against main itself: git-trees API enumeration of roster/, game/, docs/, customization/; a direct line-by-line parse of game/js/assets.js MODEL_URLS, game/js/roster-full.js, game/js/movesets.js and game/assets/movesets/index.json; GLB JSON-chunk parses (skins/joints) of all 198 roster+model GLBs; and a payload hunt across all 760 PRs, 759 branches, 89 releases (718 assets), 1,178 checkpoint files, local worktree dirs (5,403 GLBs), and the memory record. A payload counts as landed ONLY if verified on main. Automated claim matches were hand-reviewed line by line; audit narration was discounted wherever it masqueraded as a landing claim.

docs.title: The headline
docs.text:
• 68 fighter rows audited (67 roster dirs merged into canonical fighters, plus the dir-less Nine Souls; wizard-gang is a faction row, not a fighter).
  • Canon: only 4 of 68 fighters have a canon/bio file in their roster dir (buffalo-bill, dorowani [voice only], gyou, zen). BUT the full character bible IS on main — root CANON.md (165,306 bytes) holds complete entries for 43 of the 64 fighters who lack a roster-dir file. It was pushed to the repo root and never split into the per-fighter files. That is the single biggest catch-up item: the text exists, the filing never happened.
  • MODEL_URLS (game/js/assets.js) holds 149 keys on current main; exactly ONE target file is missing: ryuji-rock -> roster/ryuji-rock/attires/attire1/model.glb (CornerStone's Tripo sits archived at roster/ryuji-rock/attires/attire1/source/cornerstone-a1.glb, 18,872,720B, PR #724). An older count of '107 keys, 21 dirs with no key' is superseded — a 2026-10-22 wire-up pass landed most missing keys; the no-key set on current main is 14 fighters.
  • 145 verified gaps total. Payload classes: ON-MAIN-WRONG-PATH 69, DOES-NOT-EXIST 64, LOCAL-ONLY 11, ON-BRANCH 1.
  • The dominant pattern is not missing work. It is work that was pulled, archived, or written and then never wired: Tripo source GLBs sitting in attires/attire1/source/ with no MODEL_URLS key (chordz, kuma/Gashadokuro, panda/Aotsuki, scimitar — all unrigged statics), a moveset file on main that the loader lists never picked up (buffalo-bill), a fighter with model+moveset+loader all present but no roster entry (cain-elias), and 6 wired models that parse with 0 skins (baek A1 attire, blanka, cain-elias A1, dorowani A1, silvertongue A1, slice A1).
  • Genuinely absent (DOES-NOT-EXIST): the SmutBase intake six have no models, movesets, or canon anywhere (intake was blocked; their dirs hold placeholders only); Jin (Eastern Mind) has no base model (owner Tripo still owed) and no moveset file; 12 fighters have no moveset file at all.

docs.text:
• zen — historical-claim: A Zen completion report claimed PRs #470/#471 + merge 0f8a04a6 landed Zen's forms. Verified false in this audit: PR #470 is a DOA4 teardown PR (OPEN) and PR #471 is a playability-fixes PR — neither is a Zen landing, and Zen's real landings are #460 (models), #627 (rig docs), #743 (rigged GLBs). The claimed payload did not exist at claim time; it has since been landed for real. Source: memory/2026-10-22.md (fabrication note) + prs.json titles/states verified 2026-10-23

Note: every other automated candidate for this category was traced to audit narration, gap inventories, or merge logs about other work, and was discounted after reading the source lines. No other fabricated landing claims were found in this pass.

docs.title: Prioritized landing order (for follow-up landing waves — NOT landed by this audit)
docs.text:
1. Filing + wiring fixes (payloads already on main, zero new assets):
  2. Split root CANON.md into roster//CANON.md for the 44 covered fighters.
  3. Point the ryuji-rock key at its archived source (copy source/cornerstone-a1.glb to the wired path).
  4. Add MODEL_URLS keys for chordz, kuma (Gashadokuro), panda (Aotsuki), scimitar from their on-main source GLBs; add a base key + roster entry for buffalo-bill and vainabel.
  5. Add buffalo-bill to the moveset loader lists (his file is already on main).
  6. Add FULL_ROSTER entries for the wired-but-unselectable (cain-elias first — model, moveset file, and loader listing already exist; then blanka, lili, zafina, silvertongue as their pieces complete).
  7. Rigs: rig the 6 unrigged wired models and the archived Tripo statics (cornerstone, chordz, kuma, panda, scimitar, yukihyo sources — every source GLB parsed is an unrigged static) at the shared layer.
  8. Movesets: new files for the 12 fighters with none (jin, kuma, panda, silvertongue, zafina, bonus, and the intake six once models exist).
  9. Canon remainder: land the bios-harvest batch (in flight) for fighters whose canon is recorded in memory but not in root CANON.md (charger, koreshi, kronos, wizard-gang); the DOES-NOT-EXIST canon set (intake six, bonus, kuma, panda) needs the owner's word — nothing exists to land.
  10. Roster entries for intake/new fighters as 1-3 complete for each.

docs.title: Method notes
docs.text:
• MODEL_URLS parsed line-by-line from game/js/assets.js lines 20-375 (block comments and commented-out keys excluded); values resolve against game/ (the page root). 149 keys; 148 targets exist; 1 missing.
  • Rig = GLB JSON chunk contains skins with joints (range-request parse, no full downloads). All 198 GLBs under roster/ + every wired game/assets/models target were parsed: 56 of 62 wired primaries are rigged; the archived Tripo source GLBs are uniformly unrigged statics.
  • Moveset loader-listed = fighter id (any spelling variant) in MOVESET_IDS (game/js/movesets.js) or index.json fighters. FULL_ROSTER moveset: fields name Tekken banks (provenance), not loader keys — an early pass that tested bank ids against the loader lists produced false gaps and was corrected.
  • Canonical merges: sakura dir = Saku-ra's model home; purplerain = Purple Rain; jin-eastern-mind = Jin (Eastern Mind); rave = Kiko Tanaka's roster id; zafina's canon lives under Mariposa (name law).
  • This audit landed NOTHING. It only maps. Landing waves are dispatched separately.

docs.title: Checkpoint Protocol
docs.text:
How workers save progress so a machine/daemon restart doesn't destroy their work. Honest scope: this cannot prevent restarts. It makes every restart survivable: a re-spawned worker reads its checkpoint and continues instead of starting over.

Canonical tool: checkpoint.sh (in this directory). All commands below use it.

docs.title: When to checkpoint
docs.text:
Every worker on a multi-step task must:

  1. init a checkpoint as its first action, with --goal and --resume-prompt.
  2. beat at least every 10 minutes during long runs (cheap heartbeat).
  3. step after each completed unit of work (per card, per model, per batch item).
  4. next whenever the plan changes; decide for anything a future resume must honor.
  5. status completed when done; status failed/stalled with the reason when stuck.

If you only checkpoint at the end, you have no checkpoint.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
checkpoints/<task_id>.json:

Field Type Meaning task_id string Filename-safe id, e.g. judas-cards agent_id string|null Worker agent id (for tracing) repo string|null e.g. mhvnsnt/AshLanev2 branch string Working branch, default main goal string One-line: what the task is trying to achieve status enum running completed failed stalled spawned_at ISO-8601 UTC When the task started last_heartbeat ISO-8601 UTC Last beat/step/next/decide/status steps_completed [{at, step}] Done units. Do not redo these. next_steps [string] Where to continue key_paths [string] Files/dirs the work lives in decisions [{at, decision}] Binding unless the parent overrides blockers [{at, blocker}] What's stopping progress resume_prompt string|null The brief a re-spawned worker should follow

Writes are atomic (temp file + rename). A restart mid-write never leaves a half-written checkpoint.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
checkpoint.sh init TASK_ID --goal "..." [--repo R] [--branch B] [--agent-id ID] [--resume-prompt "..."]
checkpoint.sh beat TASK_ID
checkpoint.sh step TASK_ID "rendered judas-classic.webp"
checkpoint.sh next TASK_ID "render remaining 4 variants"
checkpoint.sh path TASK_ID "~/workspace/judas-cards/"
checkpoint.sh decide TASK_ID "keep all attires, never exclude versions"

docs.title: Reading someone else's checkpoint
docs.text: The supervisor (supervisor.sh) is tolerant of ad-hoc schemas — a worker that writes its own JSON by hand still gets flagged correctly. But workers SHOULD use checkpoint.sh: uniform schema means the re-spawn brief is complete (steps, next, paths, decisions, blockers).

docs.title: The resume contract
docs.text:
A re-spawned worker must read, in order: 1. checkpoints/<task_id>.json 2. RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md 3. IDEMPOTENCY.md

...then verify (does the repo/outputs match what the checkpoint claims?) before continuing. If the checkpoint is missing or unreadable: do not guess — report to the parent agent.

docs.text:

If someone else holds the task or the files, pick another task or coordinate in TAG-TEAM.md. 3. When you're done, set the status to done with a PR link, or released. 4. Temp files must be unique per agent and job, e.g. /tmp/<agent>-<task>-$(date +%s)-body.md. Never use a shared /tmp/body.md. Same for scratch dirs and clones.

docs.title: CROSS-REPO STRANDED-WORK AUDIT — 2026-10-23
docs.text:
Owner question (verbatim): "what else hasn't been pushed or merged or completed"

Scope: every game repo EXCEPT western-heart (112 open / 607 merged PRs — owned by a separate audit lane). Repos audited: wrestling-game, game-reverse-engineering, ConcreteDragon, cape-jones, and Bannon (found during the audit — the Bannon goals live there). Method: live gh API on 2026-10-23 — open-PR mergeable/state, changed-file counts, branch-vs-main containment (compare main...branch), and contents-API spot verification of whether payloads already exist on main. Nothing in this report was merged or closed by the audit; classification only.

docs.title: Headline
docs.text:
• 69 open PRs audited across the 5 repos. Zero are conflicting except 2 in Bannon. The dominant failure class is not conflict — it is MERGEABLE work sitting unmerged:
  • wrestling-game: 11/11 open PRs MERGEABLE, all state UNSTABLE (CI not green — Actions quota outage).
  • game-reverse-engineering: 33/33 MERGEABLE, all UNSTABLE.
  • ConcreteDragon: 4/4 MERGEABLE, all BLOCKED (branch protection on main).
  • cape-jones: 3/3 MERGEABLE and CLEAN — but all 3 are owner-held decisions, not neglect.
  • Bannon: 16/18 MERGEABLE/UNSTABLE, 2 CONFLICTING/DIRTY, 1 empty (0 files).
  • No-PR stranded branches (unique commits not on main, no open PR): wrestling-game 1, game-reverse-engineering 3 (+7 orphan-history branches), ConcreteDragon 8, cape-jones 0 in sample.
  • Local-only work: wrestling move FBX/JSON set in ~/workspace/wrestling-work/ (not a git repo); uncommitted edits in the local agent-ops clone; dirty local cape-jones clone (lane-owned).

Status classes used below: - STRANDED-READY — payload exists nowhere on main; PR/branch is the only copy; land it. - STRANDED-CI — MERGEABLE but checks not green (quota outage); stranded on CI, not on content. - BLOCKED-PROTECTION — MERGEABLE but branch protection blocks merge (ConcreteDragon). - OWNER-HELD — deliberately unmerged per standing owner decision/exclusion. - DUPLICATE — same payload as a twin PR/branch; land one, close the other. - ALREADY-ON-MAIN — branch contained in main (ahead_by=0); hygiene only. - ORPHAN-HISTORY — no common ancestor with main; cannot PR/merge normally. - NEVER-STARTED / DOES-NOT-EXIST — claimed or owed work that exists nowhere.

The residual risk is NOT a hidden program: it is (1) agent-level ad-hoc deletion (the guardian cron and any interactive agent can rm on prompt discipline alone — no code gate exists for that surface), and (2) latent pre-gate code paths that are not scheduled or running but still exist on disk (legacy cmd_reap v1, a dormant pre-gate checkout). docs.title: 4. Notes on the two structural findings
4.1 The guardian is accountable by instruction, not by construction
docs.text: Its log discipline is genuinely good (sampled entries name actor, byte counts, HEADs, stash state, pull-back). But nothing prevents a guardian run from deleting on a mistaken "pushed-clean" judgement — the same failure shape as the historical incidents, one level up. The gate+journal design goal is met for the engine paths the guardian invokes (enforce --apply), not for the guardian's own hands.

docs.title: 4.2 enforce --apply is not the gate module
docs.text: cloud_dog.py contains zero references to delete_gate. Its v2 reap is a parallel implementation of the same invariant (policy front-decider + laws + live verify + audit journal) and fails closed when the policy engine cannot import. It is honestly classed ACCOUNTABLE, not GATED. Unifying it onto check_delete_gate (so the claims leg also binds registry reaps) is the single highest-value hardening left.

docs.text: During this audit, ~/.clouddog/heartbeat.json was briefly overwritten by a pytest daemon instance (roots=/tmp/pytest-of-root/…, pid 4080) — test runs share the production heartbeat path. A keepalive reading that heartbeat could misjudge daemon health. No deletion resulted. Worth a test-isolation fix in the engine repo.

docs.title: 6. wt-verify — unattributed disappearance; what can and cannot be established
docs.text:
Established: - ~/workspace/wt-verify/ (3.9G, parts part-aa..ai downloaded from cape-jones release assets, all DLV-OK per its dl2-progress.log) vanished ~04:06–04:12 CDT 2026-10-20. Directory still absent at this audit. - Zero entries in BOTH CloudDog journals (~/.clouddog/audit.jsonl: 0 matches; ~/workspace/agent-ops/cloud-dog-audit.jsonl: 0 matches), no disk-cleanup-log entry, no surviving checkpoint/process/script attributing the deletion (grep across agent-ops .md/.log, checkpoints, and both daily memory files found only the anomaly reports themselves). - The data is safe: it was download-verified copies of cape-jones release assets; restorable from the releases. No data loss.

Cannot be established: who/what deleted it, or the exact mechanism. The overnight best hypothesis (the verify lane self-cleaned its staging after completion) remains unproven either way. This audit found no new attribution evidence and does not manufacture any.

Which NEW mechanism would have caught a recurrence: - Gate journal — would NOT have caught it if the deleter was an agent shell (gate binds engine code paths only). Would have caught it if any engine path (daemon/reaper/streamer/enforce) had done it: every gated delete now writes an audit event with path + verdict legs. - Claims — a live work-claim on wt-verify would have made the gate BLOCK an engine deletion and would have named the owning lane in the claims table, attributing the work even if a non-engine actor removed the files. - Mirror log — a delete-as-you-go lane deleting its own verified parts writes cleanup-log lines per part (as MIRROR-WW and mirror-one do); a 3.9G self-clean would have left ~35 part lines. Their absence is itself evidence the deleter was none of the accountable lanes. - Net: a recurrence is attributable by construction ONLY if the dir is (a) under a work-claim and (b) deleted by an engine path or an accountable lane. An unclaimed dir deleted by an ad-hoc agent shell remains unattributable — that is residual risk §7.1, and the practical fix is claiming staging dirs at lane start.

docs.title: 7. Residual risk list
docs.text:
1. Agent ad-hoc deletion is ungated by construction. Any agent (guardian included) can rm outside every journal. Mitigations in place: prompt law + cleanup-log discipline (observed working). Not fully closable without an OS-level control.
  2. Legacy cloud_dog.py reap v1 + legacy daemon bypass the gate module (v1 reap: policy+verify only). Not scheduled/running. Fix path: route cmd_reap → cmd_reap_v2 semantics / check_delete_gate, via branch→PR→pytest in the CloudDog repo.
  3. enforce --apply ≠ gate module (§4.2): registry reaps don't consult the claims leg. Unify onto check_delete_gate.
  4. Dormant pre-gate checkout ~/workspace/CloudDog-Muse-Storage-Disc-Assistant @ PR #40. Pull to main or remove before a future lane runs it by mistake.
  5. Daemon --apply is revoked by a comment + flag absence in supervise.sh, not by an engine-enforced trust state. One mistaken edit re-arms it (though the gate would then bind every delete — the invariant holds; only the autonomy posture would change).
  6. Heartbeat path shared with tests (§4.3) — keepalive health judgements can be spoofed by a test run.
  7. Guardian run overlap (timeout 1800s > cadence 600s): two runs can interleave log entries and duplicate relaunch decisions (observed 04:03/04:15 — mirror lane relaunched twice, harmlessly because lanes are idempotent). A run-lock would make attribution cleaner.
  8. sf-tools (and _sf-scratch generally) is unstored: safe today, single-copy. Mirror it before any future disk crunch tempts a hand-clear.

docs.title: Disk Clear Guard — Rules (mandatory, no override)
The incident that made this file
docs.text: 2026-11-17T02:45Z, disk-cleanup ROUND 6 QUIET1 cleared the ENTIRE ~/workspace/_squishyfx-native-20261116/ (833,678,167 B) WHILE the P3 SquishyFX re-render batch was running in it. Renders failed "No such file" at 02:48. The clear verified the STORED payload (PR #205 merged 56/56, 8 blends on release squishyfx-native-20261116, delta release squishyfx-native-20261116-delta, pull-back verified 02:44:18Z) — but the dir also held UNSTORED dev files: web harness + capture + calibration scripts carrying live v2 edits, B1 v1 proof seq frames + metrics. The v1 frames + metrics are unrecoverable from disk (numbers survive in BUILD-REPORT.md in the repo; peak stills + mp4s survive in your_files/). Recovery was verified (8 blends re-downloaded sha256 8/8 OK; delta tar restored the harness with v2 edits intact; v25 GLB recovered from the afro-v25 workdir). Full record: agent-ops/disk-cleanup-log.md:42353 and _proof-quality-upgrade-20261116/p3-squishyfx/CHECKPOINT.md §WORKDIR WIPED.

docs.title: The cause (measured, not assumed)
docs.text:
1. The reaper contract was never called. guard-paths.sh check-tree (the LANE_GUARD.md reaper contract, written 2026-10-20 after a cleanup lane deleted a 93%-complete Tekken 5 ISO) appears 0 times in 42,564 lines of disk-cleanup-log.md. The disk-space-guardian never invoked it.
  2. The registry was empty of lanes. protected-paths.json holds only 6 static Oct-20 entries. _squishyfx-native-20261116 was never registered. Nothing in the lane flow registers ~/workspace/_*-2026* workdirs.
  3. No charter existed. "disk-space-guardian" appears in agent-ops only in old CloudDog-era checkpoint JSONs. Its instructions live in the runtime cron, not in any repo file. No machine-enforced gate existed anywhere in its path.
  4. Judgment flipped. All day Nov 16 the guardian held the dir as SACRED ("in-flight", "active lane"). Once PR #205 merged + the delta release completed, it reclassified the dir as a completed-lane store-then-clear candidate. It protected the P3 workdir (live Blender renders) but cleared the SOURCE workdir the P3 batch was reading/editing from. The guard protected a lane's current workdir, not the dirs the lane depends on.
  5. Payload proof ≠ dir proof. "PR merged + release verified" was accepted as whole-dir proof. No unstored-content inventory was ever taken, no recency check, no open-file check, no dependency check. No .DO_NOT_DELETE marker existed at clear time (written 03:10Z, during recovery — it could not have saved the dir).

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
No cleanup — guardian, reaper, or ad-hoc — deletes, moves, or "tidies" ANY directory without a CLEARABLE verdict from disk-clear-guard.sh first. There is NO override flag, by design. Exit 1 (BLOCKED) or exit 2 (ERROR / UNCERTAIN) means hands off: log the verdict, skip the dir, move on. A blocked dir is never re-evaluated in the same run to get a different answer.

# every candidate, every time, before any delete:
./disk-clear-guard.sh --stored-manifest <manifest> <dir>
# exit 0 = CLEARABLE, 1 = BLOCKED (reasons printed), 2 = ERROR (treat as BLOCKED)
# every verdict is appended to disk-cleanup-log.md by default;
# --no-log is for dry runs and tests only.

docs.title: What the gate checks
docs.text: Check Blocks when [registry] guard-paths.sh check-tree refuses the path (LANE_GUARD contract, now actually called). [marker] A .DO_NOT_DELETE* marker exists at/under the dir, or on an ancestor up to ~/workspace. [recency] Any file under the dir was modified in the last 24 hours. [live-procs] Any process has its cwd inside the dir, or (when lsof exists) an open handle under it. [dependency] A recent (< 7 days) CHECKPOINT*.md / PROGRESS.md under ~/workspace lane workdirs references the dir by path or basename. [git-dirty] The dir is a git repo with uncommitted changes. [manifest] No --stored-manifest supplied, or files in the dir are not listed in it.

docs.title: The manifest rule (the ROUND 6 fix)
docs.text: A whole-directory clear requires a per-file stored manifest: a text file listing, one relative path per line, every file in the directory, each verified byte-identical on a store (GitHub release, TeraBox, or repo) by the pull-back step that produced it. "PR merged" / "release verified" without a file list is not proof — it proves the payload, not the directory. Any file not in the manifest blocks the clear and is named in the verdict. The guard does not verify the store itself; the manifest is the operator's attestation, and the pull-back verification behind it is what makes it true.

docs.title: Lane duty (closes the registry gap)
docs.text:
Every lane registers its workdir the moment it spawns, and unregisters it when it completes:

guard-paths.sh add ~/workspace/_my-lane-20261117 --kind active-scratch --owner <lane-id> --note "<what runs here>"
# ... lane completes, branch pushed ...
guard-paths.sh remove ~/workspace/_my-lane-20261117

Anything that must never be cleared gets a .DO_NOT_DELETE marker file in the dir itself. Both mechanisms are cheap; the guard enforces both.

docs.title: What this gate does NOT do
docs.text:
• It does not verify store contents itself (see the manifest rule).
  • It does not replace the ONE-STORE RULE, the NEVER-KILL-IN-PROGRESS law, or the SAFE-STORAGE-FIRST law — it enforces them mechanically.
  • It does not delete, move, or modify anything. It only reads and returns a verdict. Every verdict is appended to disk-cleanup-log.md by default; --no-log is for dry runs and tests only.

docs.title: Cron update required (parent action)
docs.text: The disk-space-guardian cron's instructions must be updated to call this gate before ANY delete, with the command above and the no-override rule. Until that update lands, the gate is enforced by convention only — the incident proves convention is not enough. The gate script, this charter, and disk-clear-guard-test.sh (10/10 self-test, 2026-11-17) are the deliverable; the cron instruction change is the remaining step.

docs.title: END-OF-SESSION BACKUP (watchdog procedure)
docs.text: Run this when work is wrapping up, or when session/usage is ~90-95% spent (reserve enough budget: roughly 1 tool-minute per dirty clone plus upload time for large files). Follows docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md.

docs.title: 1. Inventory every clone on the box
docs.text:
for g in $(find /workspace /home/box -name .git -maxdepth 6 -prune 2>/dev/null); do d=${g%/.git}
  dirty=$(git -C "$d" status --porcelain -uall | wc -l)
  unpushed=$(git -C "$d" log --oneline @{u}.. 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo NOUPSTREAM)
  echo -e "$d\t$dirty\t$unpushed\t$(git -C "$d" branch --show-current)"; done
Target: every clone 0 dirty / 0 unpushed.

docs.title: 2. Push work to -wip branches (never main, never force)
docs.text:
git switch -c "$(git branch --show-current)-wip-$(date +%Y%m%d)"   # or keep the feature branch
git add -A && git commit -m "wip: end-of-session snapshot" && git push -u origin HEAD
Large binaries (> ~50 MB, or anything git refuses) go to Release assets instead — step 3.

docs.title: 3. Large files -> SHA-verified Release assets in mhvnsnt/box-storage
docs.text: scripts/bk.sh <clone-dir> <name> creates release box-2026-10-14-final-<name> (edit the tag prefix to today's date), uploads every dirty/untracked file, uploads a manifest (path, git status, sha256, asset name), then compares each release asset digest to the local sha256 and prints verified=N bad=M. bad must be 0.

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
• Branches: git ls-remote origin <branch> equals local git rev-parse HEAD; git ls-tree -r origin/<branch> contains the files.
  • Release assets: digest sha256:<x> equals local sha256sum.
  • Re-run the inventory: all 0/0.

docs.title: 5. Only then clean disk
docs.text:
• Delete only items that passed step 4. Log each removed path + where it is backed up + sha256 in WORKLOG / agent-ops/BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md.
  • Anything questionable: back it up again; do not delete.

docs.title: 6. Report
docs.text: Post per clone: dirty/unpushed counts, -wip branch names, release tags, verified/bad counts.

No connector/API credentials, no rclone/terabox CLI on the box (rclone has no official TeraBox backend). - GitHub (branches + SHA-verified box-storage Release assets) stays the PRIMARY, verified backup. TeraBox is SECONDARY only; never delete anything because it is "on TeraBox". - Upload is done through the browser by a desktop agent (one with a box desktop/browser), never by a headless/executor agent and never by signing in again — use the existing session only. - Procedure: (1) after steps 1-4, stage files in /workspace/terabox-out/<date>/ with the sha256 manifest from bk.sh; (2) desktop agent opens terabox.com in the box browser, uploads that folder to /box-backups/<date>/; (3) checks uploaded file count and sizes match the manifest; (4) logs folder path + counts in agent-ops/BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md. - Keep critical sets under the 30 GB permanent quota; anything above it may vanish when Premium+ lapses (~Oct 20, 2026).

docs.title: FRICTION RESEARCH — recurring problems, real fixes
docs.text: Owner order: 2026-10-19 ~23:03 CDT — keep researching what helps with the problems we keep running into; pull open-source/free/industry-standard stuff; whole team working; faster, more optimized, higher quality, fewer stalls and hiccups. Method: six independent researchers, one per problem cluster. Live docs/repos/issues only — nothing from training guesses. All six cluster docs: ~/workspace/agent-ops/research-friction-20261019/01–06-*.md. Index: [[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX]]. Wiring status (honest): all six clusters delivered research + concrete wire-up plans, no PRs opened by researchers — the code targets (CloudDog repo, agent-ops lanes) have a live straight-to-store build lane and running daemons in them tonight; opening code PRs blindly would collide. Findings are entered in the index as queued pull-ins with named owners per the research conventions — the integration lane wires them after check-before-start.

docs.title: 1. Flaky egress proxy — resilient transfer
docs.text:
What we hit: connection refusals, empty responses, transient gh 401s, stream CANCELs. All uploads >485MB failed; 100MB-via-curl proven working; lanes die on flakes instead of riding through.

What research found (01-resilient-transfer.md): - gh CLI does NOT retry transient failures (no --retry flag; go-gh single-attempt client). The whole ecosystem wraps it — so CloudDog's _run_gh is the retry layer and it's too weak (3× fixed 2s, misses connrefused/429). - The backend pushes the wrong size class: github.py splits at 2GiB while our own evidence says >485MB dies and 100MB works. Fix = drop SPLIT_BYTES to 100MB. - aria2's deeper flags were mapped (--retry-wait=10 --max-tries=0 --auto-save-interval=30 --always-resume=true --conditional-get=true); rclone flag bundle (--retries 10 --retries-sleep 30s --low-level-retries 20 --timeout 300s); curl stall-killer template (--retry-all-errors --retry-connrefused --speed-limit/--speed-time → stall becomes exit 28 → retry, not lane death). - Proxy-env hygiene: the no_proxy IPv6-literal quirk in ~/TOOLS.md explains one "empty response" class — a _proxy_env() sanitizer for all subprocess spawns. - Skipped as dependencies: tenacity, backoff, wget, Go retry libs — CloudDog's stdlib-only law stands; port the patterns (new stdlib retry.py: exponential + jitter + transient/permanent classifier + max_elapsed storm bound), not the packages. tus protocol skipped (no tus server on the GitHub side) — but our 100MB+sha256+manifest is the tus shape.

Wire-up plan (W1–W6): stdlib retry.py → beef up _run_gh (8 attempts, exponential+jitter, give-up on true 401) → 100MB SPLIT_BYTES → aria2 flags in _aria2c_fetch → _proxy_env() everywhere → terabox/drive subprocess wrapping → curl template in verify/download paths. Owner / status: queued — CloudDog integration lane (check in-flight lanes first).

docs.title: 2. GitHub API limits — big artifacts
docs.text:
What we hit: blob API 422s above ~10MB; gh release upload silently renames dotfiles; signed URLs expire mid-stream; manifest-less final trees caused the Scooby empty-tree 422.

What research found (02-github-limits.md): - Releases are the right store — GitHub's own docs: <2GiB/asset, up to 1000 assets/release, and "no limit on the total size of a release, nor bandwidth usage." Our 100MB-chunk pattern has no documented ceiling against it. - git-lfs is a hard NO — cost math: 10GiB storage + 10GiB/month bandwidth included, then $5/50GB pack, metered on every download. Our law requires download+hash retrievability proofs — a few dozen 4.8GB proofs burn the free quota; metered forever on reads. Releases are unmetered. Also LFS per-file 2GB cap blocks our biggest ISOs. - gh-large-releases (ading2210) is the industry reference for chunk+manifest+verify — adopt the pattern, not the code (license unverified). - CloudDog's re-resolve-on-403 matches the documented asset-download contract (re-hit API endpoint per fetch, never cache redirect). Validated — keep. - Blob API docs claim 100MB; our lanes 422 above ~10MB — treat our figure as real, docs as aspirational. Skip the blob API for parts. - Rate-limit budget: ~2–3 API calls per 100MB part; 100GB ≈ 3,000 calls fits the 5,000/hr personal budget but the daemon shares the token with other lanes — throttle to ≤8 concurrent uploads, never tight-loop retries.

Wire-up plan: manifest.json as release asset + manifest-first finalization (Scooby lesson into law) → unify 100MB chunk quantum across store()/mirror → bounded-parallel part uploads with chunk-level resume → explicit 403-re-resolution wrapper → adopt gh-large-releases manifest schema → per-part verify shortcut. Owner / status: queued — CloudDog integration lane. Two open questions for parent: (1) 100MB as single standard for both store() and mirror? (2) full re-download verify vs part-manifest shortcut?

docs.title: 3. CI pain — maxed minutes + flakes
docs.text:
What we hit: Actions maxed at 2,000/2,000 min; runner flakiness; one real recurring flake: sqlite "database is locked" in test_concurrent_upserts_are_safe; 75+ PRs stuck.

What research found (03-ci-flakes.md): - Root cause of the sqlite flake (read in the actual code): WAL + busy_timeout=30000 already set — the naive fix is exhausted. Python's sqlite3 starts DEFERRED transactions; a DEFERRED read upgrading to write returns SQLITE_BUSY immediately, bypassing busy_timeout (deadlock avoidance). Plus _open_db() runs schema DDL on every fresh connection — the 20-thread test stampedes DDL. Fix: BEGIN IMMEDIATE on write paths + app-level retry with backoff + serialized schema init. Do NOT add pytest-rerunfailures — the flake mirrors a real daemon race; hiding it hides a production bug. - CI minute diet (zero-risk YAML): concurrency-cancel on PRs, timeout-minutes 15 (default 360 is a billing hazard), path filters, matrix trim to nightly, caching, retention 7d. Pure YAML, staged on highest-burn repos first. - Self-hosted runner: $0/min for private repos (planned $0.002/min postponed, not in effect). Oracle ARM box as host: 2 OCPU/12GB (halved June 2026 — old guides wrong), 200GB block, 10TB egress, free forever — but: card required at signup, idle reclaim (95th-pct CPU+net+mem <20% over 7 days — a mostly-idle CI runner is genuinely at risk), chronic ARM capacity errors, home region locked forever, unexplained signup rejections. Ephemeral-per-job, private-repos-only, kill-switch back to hosted. - Skipped: SourceHut (paid), Cirrus/Codeberg (OSS/FLOSS only), CircleCI (still metered), GitLab/Jenkins/Woodpecker-hosted (migration tax, no win), StarSling (per-minute is the wrong direction), FlakeFighters (minutes-expensive, root cause known).

Wire-up plans: Plan A = CloudDog sqlite flake fix (proof: 20/20 stress-loop green); Plan B = minute-diet YAML via merge-law-ci-watch lane; Plan C = self-hosted runner, blocked on OWNER decision (card required — never auto-signup). Owner / status: A queued — CloudDog integration lane; B queued — merge-law-ci-watch lane; C blocked on owner.

docs.title: 4. Lane resilience — restarts kill work
docs.text:
What we hit: daemon/runtime restarts kill lanes mid-work; stale checkpoints; resume duplicates or misses work; the worker-watchdog can't tell "dead" from "slow."

What research found (04-lane-resilience.md): - Delivery model decision: at-least-once with idempotent units. True exactly-once for agent side-effects isn't achievable without a transactional coordinator spanning every tool; the survivable side is never-lose-work + idempotent units. Write it into CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL.md. - Core gap = liveness is not progress. Fix: progress_seq/last_progress_at checkpoint fields + a STUCK bucket in supervisor.sh (heartbeat fresh, progress frozen) — surface STUCK, re-spawn only DEAD. - Fencing tokens (Kleppmann) — the single highest-value change: monotonic epoch in checkpoints; any write carrying an older epoch is rejected. Kills the paused-agent-wakes-and-overwrites corruption class outright. - systemd user units VERIFIED UNAVAILABLE on this VM ("Failed to connect to bus") — skip; supervisord/s6/runit skipped on cost/benefit (PID-file + keepalive cron already covers the 90% case); Temporal/DBOS skipped (server/DB prerequisites absent — their semantics imported as patterns 1–4). - Dead-man's switch inverted locally: worker-watchdog writes its own ok-ping; the disk guardian alerts if it goes stale. No external hosted monitor (lane metadata never leaves the box).

Wire-up plan (W1–W6): progress fields + STUCK bucket → checkpoint.sh claim with lease + fencing → watchdog claims before spawning → CloudDog daemon health = progress (cycle_seq advancement, not pid-alive) + restart backoff → append-only journal.jsonl per task → fsync hardening. Owner / status: queued — checkpoint infra lane (agent-ops) + CloudDog daemon owner. Open question: claim-registry (cluster 5) and checkpoint claim are the same mechanism from two sides — integrate as ONE claim format.

docs.title: 5. Lane coordination — work claims (the T5 fix)
docs.text:
What we hit: a cleanup lane deleted an in-progress Tekken 5 ISO download. is_inflight() is a 5-min-mtime heuristic — a paused download slips through; .DO_NOT_DELETE markers are static; nothing machine-readable says "lane X owns this path."

What research found (05-lane-coordination.md): - Adopt: flock(2) (kernel auto-release on fd close — no stale locks), Python filelock (public-domain per listing) for the reaper, O_CREAT|O_EXCL + PID-liveness stale-check rules (EPERM = alive), Kleppmann lease + fencing-token model, sqlite WAL as the store. - Skip the tools, keep the models: etcd leases (no etcd in the shop), lockfile-progs (GPL), GitHub Actions/Jenkins/GitLab concurrency (pattern references only).

Wire-up plan — claims table in the EXISTING sqlite v4 registry (no second registry): path PK, owner, action, claim_id (uuid4, fencing anchor), monotonic epoch, claimed_at/heartbeat_at, ttl_s default 600 (heartbeat at TTL/3, etcd practice). API: claim / heartbeat / release / is_claimed (ancestor-prefix coverage) / expire_sweep, all claim_id-guarded. Hard gates: reap_candidates()/cmd_reap in cloud_dog.py, Reaper._try_reap in src/clouddog/reaper.py:193, the straight-to-store mode, plus python -m clouddog.claims check <path> CLI for non-CloudDog sweep lanes. Download lanes claim on start, heartbeat, release on completion. Fail closed if the registry is unreadable. Reapers defer/skip on a live claim — never wait, never delete. Owner / status: queued — CloudDog integration lane. Design is the same claim format cluster 4 needs — integrate once.

docs.title: 6. Browser-transfer alternatives — pulling without the browser
docs.text:
What we hit: TeraBox .blend downloads failed 10/10 via the browser file-transfer tool. Lanes need files FROM TeraBox shares without the browser path.

What research found (06-browser-transfer-alternatives.md): - No native rclone TeraBox backend exists — verified against rclone.org/tiers, pkg.go.dev (v1.64, v1.68.2), Batocera list. TeraBox publishes no OAuth API, no WebDAV, no export tool. Stop looking. - AList is the strongest find (alist-org/alist, AGPL-3.0 — service use OK, never vendored): native TeraBox driver (cookie-based, jsToken validation) + PikPak/BaiduNetdisk/Quark; serves everything as WebDAV → rclone's Tier-1 WebDAV backend. Chain: TeraBox → AList → WebDAV → rclone → CloudDog stores. - rclone PikPak backend exists (added v1.62, MIT): username/password, MD5, multipart, backend addurl for offline-download tasks. The gigaleak loop should document this as the reference pattern. - rclone is NOT installed on this VM — the single highest-leverage quick win. - Cookie-export → aria2 (-c -x16 -s16 --load-cookies=cookies.txt) is the production pattern for large authenticated pulls; cookies live in /tmp or the vault flow, never committed; fail-fast "refresh cookies" on expiry. - yt-dlp (-g) + gallery-dl (-g) become the generic "give me the direct link" lane standard for non-TeraBox hosts — yt-dlp has no TeraBox extractor, honest limit. - terabox-downloader (PyPI, MIT): unofficial scraper, watchlist. terabox-gateway: license unverified, cookie-rotation pattern worth copying. JDownloader2: skip (heavyweight).

Wire-up plan: install rclone ≥1.62 everywhere → AList→WebDAV→rclone bridge (Secure Vault cookies) → cookie→aria2 SOP script (tools/dl/tb-pull.sh) → document the PikPak loop → yt-dlp/gallery-dl as lane standards → delete-as-you-go discipline. docs.title: Problem 1 — GitHub release upload write-timeouts persisting for DAYS
docs.text:
Cost: longtail lane lost 1981.zip–1985.zip repeatedly Oct 20–22 ("FAILED after 4 retries (TimeoutError)" / "Connection aborted / write operation timed out"), one ~400MB whole-file upload at a time, no resume. Guardian offload verify-downloads also failing (FAIL download-back failed), blocking deletes while verify fails.

New finding (not in cluster 01): gh release upload's retry is exactly initial + 3 retries at a constant 200ms backoff, retrying only transport errors/5xx, with no low-speed stall detection (verified in cli/cli trunk pkg/cmd/release/shared/upload.go — the lane's "fails after 4 retries" symptom matches to the attempt). A stalled POST hangs indefinitely. gh also uses 5-way concurrency and --clobber deletes the old asset BEFORE re-uploading. Cluster 01's retry.py was wired into CloudDog only — and CloudDog's local copy was removed by owner order 2026-10-21, so standalone lanes have nothing.

Wired: lanes/resilient-gh-upload.sh + lanes/RESILIENT-GH-UPLOAD-SOP.md + lanes/tests/test-resilient-upload.sh (15/15 stubbed tests green): split-to-exactly-100MB parts (owner standard; RU_PART_SIZE is tests-only), sha256 manifest uploaded LAST (CloudDog-compatible schema), curl direct-POST to uploads.github.com with --speed-limit/--speed-time stall-kill (exit 28 → retry, never a multi-day hang), -T streaming, sequential parts, 8-attempt exponential backoff + jitter, retry only curl 7/28/52/55/56 + HTTP 5xx/429 (abort on 401/403/404/422), idempotent resume (size-matched parts skipped; mismatched parts DELETE-then-reuploaded — worst case re-sends 100MB), per-part size/digest verify + final asset-list check. Pattern adopted from ading2210/gh-large-releases — license verified LGPL-3.0, so the pattern (naming/manifest/delete-then-reupload) is adopted, code is NOT vendored. Stall-kill semantics from curl's documented --speed-limit (exit 28).

Recommendations (not wired): bring the longtail lane onto the 100MB split+manifest convention (its whole-file uploads are the other half of the failure); live-upload smoke test of the script against a scratch release (stubbed tests only so far — no repo artifacts created by this pass).

docs.title: Problem 2 — VM runtime restarts kill lanes AND their watchdogs
docs.text:
Cost: TTT2 pull lane died ~9 times in one night; its own watchdog went absent too; a coordinator died 8 min in with no checkpoint. Cluster 04 assumed the supervisor survives — it doesn't always.

New finding: this VM has no local cron daemon at all (no cron/crond binary, no /etc/crontab, no crond process — checked 2026-10-22), so @reboot crontab entries are not installable without apt/root. The runtime scheduler cron (which runs this task) DOES survive restarts — it is the only restart-resilient loop available. systemd user units already verified unavailable (cluster 04).

Wired (design only — NOT scheduled, NOT installed): lane-autostart/lane-autostart.sh + lanes.manifest + CRONTAB-TEMPLATE.txt + README-lane-autostart.md. flock(1) is the ONLY liveness authority (kernel releases locks on death/reboot — no stale-lock hazard, verified from sources); never kills live lanes; crash-loop guard (max restarts/hour → pause + state/<lane>.ESCALATE); watchdogs supervised too (own lock + heartbeat file — covers the dead-watchdog incident); setsid + env -i + explicit PATH launch discipline; all lanes ship DISABLED. Supervisor alternatives re-checked: supervisord (BSD-style) / circus (Apache-2.0) / honcho (MIT) / overmind (MIT) / s6 (ISC) — all SKIP (bootstrap gap without systemd, or no autorestart, or PID-1 rooting); no new evidence overturns cluster 04. Verified with my own eyes: bash -n clean, single-instance across 4 supervisor runs (1 real lane, "alive (lock held)" logs), crash-loop cap fired at max with ESCALATE written.

Blocked on OWNER APPROVAL (not installed): (1) creating the scheduler cron entry (~5 min) that runs lane-autostart.sh — the recommended wiring; (2) installing a local cron daemon if the @reboot supplement is ever wanted; (3) registering any actual lane (flipping no→yes in the manifest).

Live-tested against mhvnsnt/agent-ops: 17 open PRs listed, real overlaps flagged (CLAIMS.md shared by #9/#10/#11/#24, several already CONFLICTING). Makes the hazard visible; enforcement follows.

Verdicts: GitHub native merge queue — RECOMMEND as pilot ($0 for public org repos; true serialization via merge_group; merge method must be "merge" per owner law; needs branch protection + merge_group CI trigger). Kodiak — SKIP (license verified AGPL-3.0, and it doesn't serialize). bors-ng — SKIP (Apache-2.0, real serialization, setup tax too heavy for 135 repos). Mergify — CONDITIONAL power option (free for public repos, Depends-On cross-repo chains; only after a native pilot proves out). Merge-queue enablement needs OWNER APPROVAL (changes repo behavior).

docs.title: Problem 1 — Deploy blocked: 5,969 MB vs GitHub Pages 1 GB limit
docs.text:
Cost: live site https://mhvnsnt.github.io/western-heart/ frozen on the Oct 24 build; owner decision pending ("what gets cut").

Doc: research-friction-20261025/01-deploy-pages-limit.md.

Verified live (2026-10-25/26): Pages 1 GB published-site cap confirmed from GitHub's own docs (5,969 MB is 5.8× over — the full set can never ship on Pages). GitHub Release assets send NO CORS headers (curl-probed: 302 → release-assets.githubusercontent.com, 200, no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, signed URL ~1 h expiry) — direct in-game fetch() from Releases FAILS, so releases stay the store, not the runtime CDN. jsDelivr serves repo files ≤20 MB with CORS * + correct model/gltf-binary (live probe) and 403s an 86 MB GLB (documented 20 MB/file cap). Repo tree measured via the git-trees API: 176 GLBs >20 MB hold 5,914 MB (73% of GLB bytes); 98 GLBs >25 MiB (4,178 MB). Shell-only floor ≈ 70–170 MB (code ~10 MB + UI/portraits ~7.5 MB + 1 stage + 2 fighters + movesets/music). game/netlify.toml on main verified: publishes game/, proxies /roster/* etc. to Pages (so Netlify currently inherits the Pages problem).

Recommended (1st choice, $0): shell on Pages (~70–170 MB) + all GLBs on Cloudflare R2 free tier (whole set fits 10 GB, $0 egress, CORS-configurable). itch.io HTML5 shell + R2 lazy-load as the money path (shell fits the 500 MB / 1,000-file caps; HTML5 = donations only, selling needs a Downloadable build; payouts Direct to PayPal/Stripe or Collected, $5 min). jsDelivr as the small-file fast path (optional). Cloudflare Pages as shell-only host (unlimited bandwidth) or Netlify free as shell mirror (bandwidth figure uncertain under the 2025 credit system — verify at signup).

Excluded: full set on Pages, releases as runtime CDN, Cloudflare Pages full set (25 MiB/file cap on all plans), Vercel Hobby (non-commercial clause), git LFS / Actions artifacts (already excluded 2026-10-19).

Blocked: owner decision (split hosting vs cutting content — the recommendation makes cutting unnecessary); R2 signup (may ask for a payment method — owner-only per card rules); itch.io account + payout setup (owner phone-only).

docs.title: Problem 2 — Fight goes live +126s after stage confirm (play-verify run 18)
docs.text:
Cost: owner previously called the game unplayable; the 2-min load is part of that. 4 missing assets (404s) in the same run.

Doc: research-friction-20261025/02-load-time-126s.md.

Verified live (2026-10-26 ~04:09 UTC): deploy-manifest.json on the live site is summary-only (7,181 files / 5,647,298,304 B — no per-file list, no hashes), so no manifest check can run until build_pages.py emits a per-file manifest. HTTP Range works on Pages (live 206 + accept-ranges: bytes). Pages serves cache-control: max-age=600 — the browser HTTP cache only holds assets 10 minutes. three.js latest 0.186.1 (MIT); r186 release notes contain zero KTX2/GLTFLoader entries.

Recommended sequence (measure first, then cut): (1) own instrumentation in game/js/loadperf.js + ?loadreport FIRST — the 126s is unmeasured and no three.js load profiler exists to pull (stats-gl, MIT, is a dev-only frame overlay). (2) Kill the 404s: per-file asset-manifest.json from build_pages.py + ~100-line boot verifier (HEAD + size check, named failure, 3× retry); SRI does not apply to fetch()/GLB, and no lib exists for this. (3) If network-bound: KTX2/BasisU via existing gltfpack -tc (ETC1S color / UASTC normal, POT resize, own-eyes compare per fighter) + one shared KTX2Loader in game/js/assets.js; preload next fight during the current fight; Workbox SW + Cache Storage (Apache-2.0; its precache manifest doubles as the §4 verifier). (4) Draco: SKIP — meshopt already wired and decodes faster (1–3 GB/s SIMD). (5) Needle gltf-progressive (MIT): EVALUATE for stages only (17.4 MB → 715 KB first paint is real, but needs LOD-processed assets and buys nothing for fighters).

Correction (parent pass, 2026-10-25): the research doc's first draft said the 4 missing assets were "unnamed in the handoff" — wrong. They are named in the run-18 HTTP log (~/workspace/_playverify-20261025/http8123.log) and in memory: roster/demonio/anatomy/anatomy-layers.json, game-src/js/intro-interactions.js, customization/parts/no-mercy/glb/body_parts/model_1171.glb, customization/eye-library/eye-classic-original.png. game-src/js/... looks like a wrong-path bug (game-src/ vs game/js/) — a game-lane fix. Doc corrected before this PR.

Blocked: nothing above is proven to fix the 126s until the instrumentation runs. Do not start the KTX2 re-encode of all fighters before the measurement. Needle Cloud asset generation is a third-party service step (free tier: 30 optimizations) — owner call before any fighter GLB is uploaded to it.
