docs.title: Bottom line for the TorBox problem
docs.text: Two independent agents, one of which read the credential-broker source, agree: stop putting the surrogate in ?token=. Next step is the 3-step diagnostic in the PR doc (placement print → tb_mylist crash test → Bearer-surrogate requestdl), then Fix A or B depending on whether requestdl accepts Bearer.

docs.title: TorBox Lane 6 — Open-Source Wire-Up + Testing
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-20 (CDT). All TorBox API tests ran through the Secure Vault surrogate flow only (dynamic_credentials, credential custom.torbox); no key was hardcoded, printed, or logged. Surrogates appear below only as <SURR>. CDN URLs are never printed, only their hostnames.

docs.title: HEADLINE FINDING — the BAD_TOKEN wall is endpoint-shaped, not total
docs.text:
The stored TorBox key is dead for Bearer-authenticated endpoints but requestdl works today through the ?token= query flow. Evidence (2026-10-20, torrent 119449922 "Documents", the 350GB cached torrent from CONNECTOR.md):

Call Auth style Result GET /v1/api/torrents/mylist (raw helper bin/tb_mylist.py) ?token=<SURR> appended by helper HTTP 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"} (mylist does not accept query-token auth at all) GET mylist probe Authorization: Bearer <SURR> only HTTP 403 {"success":false,"error":"BAD_TOKEN","detail":"Your token is invalid or has expired..."} GET mylist probe Bearer + ?token= HTTP 403 BAD_TOKEN (same) GET /v1/api/user/me probe Bearer only HTTP 403 BAD_TOKEN GET /v1/api/user/me probe ?token= only HTTP 401 Not authenticated GET /v1/api/torrents/requestdl?torrent_id=119449922&zip_link=true (helper bin/tb_reqdl.py) ?token=<SURR> only HTTP 200 {"success":true,"detail":"Torrent download requested successfully.","data":"<CDN URL>"} Same via torbox-api SDK request_download_link Bearer + ?token= (SDK sends both) 200, success=True, data= requestdl probe Bearer only, no ?token= HTTP 422 missing query token (endpoint requires the query param) requestdl probe ?token=GARBAGE_NOT_A_TOKEN (control) HTTP 403 BAD_TOKEN — so requestdl does validate the token; the surrogate swap delivers a token requestdl accepts

Conclusion: Sentinel swaps the surrogate in the query string too, and the resulting token passes requestdl's validation while failing Bearer validation on mylist/user/me. Whatever the server-side reason (token scope/rotation state), the practical pipeline consequence is:

requestdl → CDN link works NOW. Listing/profile/createtorrent-style Bearer endpoints do not. The pipeline only needs requestdl for torrents already on the account (id known: 119449922), so the range-extract lane is unblocked for that torrent. Adding NEW torrents (createtorrent is Bearer) stays blocked until the owner resets the API token in TorBox settings and the vault credential is re-registered.

docs.title: CONNECTOR.md corrections (noted, not edited — additive-only rule)
docs.text:
• Stored credential placement is actually {"query_param": "token"} (verified from dynamic_credential_entry("custom.torbox")), not bearer_header as the doc states.
  • bin/tb_reqdl.py is NOT broken: it returned 200 + CDN link in this run. The doc's "Untested / broken" section is stale.
  • Existing helpers (tb_mylist.py, tb_export.py, torbox_add_magnet.py) already use url_with_surrogate_query_param; mylist still fails because that endpoint ignores query tokens and wants Bearer (403 BAD_TOKEN).

docs.title: 1. torbox-api Python SDK (PyPI torbox-api 1.0.6, MIT)
docs.text:
Installed into a throwaway venv (pip install torbox-api, 20MB incl. requests; venv lived in /tmp and was wiped by another lane's /tmp cleanup after testing — reinstall is one command).

Source inspection (torbox_api/): - TorboxApi(access_token) fans the token out to 9 services; auth is AccessTokenAuth → Authorization: Bearer <token> on every call. - services/torrents.py::request_download_link is the one difference from raw calls: its serializer attaches the Bearer header AND .add_query("token", token) — dual auth. That matches the API: requestdl requires ?token= (422 without it). - Transport is plain requests.request with no browser User-Agent (default python-requests UA) and no redirect control. It survived Cloudflare here (no 1010), but CONNECTOR.md's browser-UA rule remains the safer default for raw calls. - Error handling drops response bodies: on HTTP ≥400 it raises RequestError with status only — the BAD_TOKEN detail body is lost, which makes debugging worse than the raw helpers. - Base URL default https://api.torbox.app, timeout default 60000ms.

Live tests (surrogate as access_token, output scrubbed): - api.torrents.get_torrent_list(api_version="v1") → RequestError 403 (Bearer BAD_TOKEN, same as raw probe). - api.torrents.request_download_link(api_version="v1", token=<SURR>, torrent_id="119449922", zip_link="true") → RequestDownloadLinkOkResponse(success=True, detail="Torrent download requested successfully.", data=<CDN URL>).

Verdict: SDK does nothing the raw helpers don't, except dual-auth requestdl — and tb_reqdl.py already achieves the same 200 with the query flow alone. Not adopted (extra dependency, worse errors, no UA control). The dual-auth detail is documented here in case a future endpoint wants both.

docs.title: 2. rclone v1.75.2 (genuine, off-PATH)
docs.text:
• Binary: ~/workspace/tools/rclone/rclone (82MB, static, go1.26.9). rclone version → rclone v1.75.2, ubuntu 24.04, linux/amd64. Not on PATH (rclone: command not found in a bare shell).
  • rclone help backends on this build: no torbox, no realdebrid, no alldebrid backend. rclone help backend realdebrid → CRITICAL: didn't find backend called "realdebrid".
  • The one debrid backend present: premiumizeme (premiumize.me, OAuth client_id/secret). Also adjacent: fichier (1Fichier), putio, http, webdav, internetarchive, mega, pikpak.
  • Dummy-config test (--config /tmp/.../rclone-test.conf, no secrets): listremotes works; an http remote against a local server listed and rclone cat streamed a file fine — rclone's http/webdav remotes are the usable glue shapes.
  • Pipeline role: rclone cannot talk to TorBox directly. It can sit downstream of anything that exposes WebDAV/HTTP (Decypharr's WebDAV, TorBox's own WebDAV — existence attested by TorBox Media Center README "use TorBox's WebDAV"; endpoint/credentials NOT verified in this lane), and it is Decypharr's own mount engine (pkg/rclone, RC port 5572). For the single-zip range-extract job it adds nothing over zip_extract.py, which already speaks Range to the CDN directly.

docs.title: 3. Decypharr (sirrobot01/decypharr — 917★, MIT, Go, repo 20.6MB)
docs.text:
Clone into /tmp was attempted and aborted on a transient /tmp-full condition; inspection was done from the GitHub API + raw sources instead (no long service was run, per task).

  • Providers (README + pkg/debrid/providers/): Real-Debrid, TorBox, DebridLink, AllDebrid, Premiumize + direct Usenet/NNTP. Mock qBittorrent/SABnzbd APIs for the *Arr stack; serves via its own DFS VFS, embedded/external rclone mounts, NFSv4/SMB, and built-in WebDAV (docs.decypharr.com: "mounts remote files using DFS, Rclone, or serves via WebDAV").
  • Auth: config debrids[].api_key (config.full.json shape: name/host/api_key/folder/rate_limit/...). Its TorBox provider (pkg/debrid/providers/torbox/torbox.go) sends Authorization: Bearer <api_key> with a custom UA and a built-in 300 req/min limiter (comment cites TorBox's per-key cap). Same BAD_TOKEN wall: its mylist/user-me calls would 403 with the current key exactly like our probes.
  • Download links: fetchDownloadLink makes no API call — it builds the permalink https://api.torbox.app/v1/api/torrents/requestdl?token= <account token>&torrent_id=<id>&file_id=<fid>&redirect=true, i.e. the exact query-token flow proven working above. Its SpeedTest reads Range: bytes=0-1048575 from that link, i.e. Decypharr itself assumes TorBox CDN links honor Range.
  • HTTP Range for zip_extract: Decypharr's WebDAV/VFS is a streaming media layer; feeding a 350GB zip through it to range-extract would add a daemon, a FUSE/WebDAV hop, and an Arr-shaped cache in front of a job zip_extract.py already does directly against the CDN URL. Verdict: real, maintained, production-grade — but not needed for this pipeline, and TorBox-side it is blocked by the same dead Bearer key for everything except the requestdl permalink trick it shares with our helper. Revisit if an *Arr/media-serving need appears or after the token is reset (then it becomes the strongest off-the-shelf TorBox mount: it would give rclone a WebDAV target).

docs.title: 4. JDownloader2 headless — SKIP (feasibility only)
docs.text:
• Headless route is the jlesage/docker-jdownloader-2 image or a bare JVM run: JDOWNLOADER_HEADLESS=1 + -Djava.awt.headless=true, and in headless mode MyJDownloader (cloud account, email+password) is the only control interface.
  • This VM: java: command not found, no /usr/lib/jvm, no Docker on PATH, ~8GB RAM mostly committed, root disk 94–97% full. Installing a JVM + JD2 (+ its self-updating jar churn) to gain a whole-file downloader is negative value: JD2 has no remote-zip Range extraction, no TorBox-specific advantage over the working requestdl→CDN path, and its debrid handling still needs the same account credentials.
  • Skipped with reason: heavy Java stack, extra cloud account, wrong tool shape (full downloads, not range-extract).

docs.title: 5. aria2 1.35.0 (~/workspace/tools/aria2/aria2c wrapper)
docs.text:
Wrapper sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the bundled libs; the bare usr/bin/aria2c fails without it (libaria2.so.0: cannot open shared object file) — always call the wrapper.

  • HTTP(S) multi-connection: works. Local test: aria2c --max-connection-per-server=4 --split=4 http://127.0.0.1:18222/src.txt → status OK, content verified byte-for-byte (lane6-aria2-http-test). Useful as a parallel downloader for plain CDN/HTTP files.
  • Magnet: dead from this VM, re-verified today. aria2c --bt-metadata-only=true 'magnet:?xt=urn:btih:856d0103…&dn=Documents' ran 25s at 0 B/s, stayed INPR [MEMORY][METADATA], fetched no metadata, no peers. Consistent with the 2026-10-17 finding (outbound UDP/DHT blocked; see ~/workspace/hero-parts-pull/swarm_check.py, libtorrent DHT test built for exactly this hash). aria2 magnet only becomes viable via a seedbox/remote node that hands back an HTTP URL — which is precisely what a debrid's requestdl already does.
  • Role: fine as an HTTP download accelerator downstream of a CDN link; zip_extract.py + GitHub streaming upload already cover the actual job with range precision aria2 doesn't offer for zip members.

docs.title: 6. New / notable 2025–2026 open-source TorBox tools (GitHub API search, 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Search torbox: 342 repos; torbox created:>2024-06-01: 316; debrid created:>2024-06-01: 711. Relevant finds (stars as of today):

Repo ★ Auth / shape Fit sirrobot01/decypharr 917 per-provider api_key in config; Bearer for TorBox See §3 TorBox-App/torbox-media-center 284 official TorBox team; TORBOX_API_KEY env; Python, MIT; FUSE/.strm mount, video files only, paid plan required, read-only; explicitly defers to TorBox's own WebDAV Media serving only; same key wall (Bearer mylist); not a zip/range tool jittarao/torbox-app 184 alternative TorBox web UI UI only 93Pd9s8Jt/atba 180 cross-platform TorBox client (Dart, GPL-3.0), streaming Desktop client; API key skjaere/DebriDav 155 Kotlin, MIT; WebDAV bridge for debrids + Arr stack Same family as Decypharr; smaller CasaVargas/DebridDownloader 94 Rust/Tauri desktop, GPL-3.0; RD + TorBox + Premiumize; resumable multi-connection; tokens in OS keychain (the orion01500/DebridDownloader fork shows 0★ — use upstream) Desktop whole-file downloader; no range-extract ArrCee76/magnetar 90 browser extension: send magnets to RD/TorBox/AllDebrid/Premiumize/local client Ingest convenience only Viren070/AIOStreams 2930 Stremio addon aggregator (debrid-backed streaming) Streaming, not extraction g0ldyy/comet 1120 Stremio torrent/debrid addon Streaming, not extraction

None of the 2025–2026 crop changes the auth picture: every TorBox tool authenticates with the account API key (Bearer for API calls, ?token= for requestdl permalinks). No tool bypasses a dead key, and none offers remote-zip range extraction — that remains our zip_extract.py's job, by design.

docs.title: 7. CDN Range verification (the zip_extract contract)
docs.text:
Proven-path evidence already on disk: the earlier successful extraction ran zip_extract.py against a TorBox CDN URL (~/workspace/hero-parts-pull/dlurl.txt, host nexus-088.cnam.tb-cdn.io) — log okko-extract.log: zip size: 350.0 GB, zip64 central dir: 79772 entries, parsed 79772 entries. So TorBox CDN links honor HEAD + Range and the 350GB zip's central directory was already pulled this way.

Fresh-link probe (2026-10-20, new helper bin/tb_cdn_range_probe.py, torrent 119449922, run three times — requestdl succeeded every time): - requestdl success: True | detail: Torrent download requested successfully. - cdn host: store-013.wnam.tb-cdn.io - HEAD -> 200 | len: 350016069757 | accept-ranges: bytes | type: application/zip (350,016,069,757 = the zip_link wrapper; the inner Documents.zip listed in CONNECTOR.md is 350,016,069,428.) - The probe's two small Range GETs did not return within the lane's 125s window (CDN first-byte latency from this VM; no HTTP error was returned — the calls hung, they were not refused). Range support is nonetheless established: Accept-Ranges: bytes on the fresh link, Decypharr's Range-based SpeedTest design, and above all the prior full extraction, which ran entirely on zip_extract.py's assert r.status == 206 Range fetches against a tb-cdn.io link. A patient re-run of the probe (it allows 60s per call) is the way to re-confirm Range reads on a fresh link; nothing about the timeout contradicts the contract.

docs.title: Winners wired
docs.text:
1. Kept/winner: existing pipeline — bin/tb_reqdl.py (query-token requestdl, verified 200 today) → CDN URL → zip_extract.py (Range) → github_upload_stream.py. No new dependency needed.
  2. Added (additive, connector dir): bin/tb_cdn_range_probe.py — one-command health check of the whole contract (requestdl success, CDN host, HEAD length/Accept-Ranges, head+tail Range reads) that prints no URLs or secrets.
  3. Not adopted: torbox-api SDK (§1), Decypharr (§3, revisit after token reset), JDownloader2 (§4), rclone-as-TorBox-client (no such backend, §2), aria2-for-magnets (§5).
  4. Owner action that unblocks everything else: reset the TorBox API token in TorBox settings and re-register the custom.torbox vault credential. Bearer endpoints (mylist, createtorrent, user/me) are 403 BAD_TOKEN until then; requestdl already works.

docs.title: Lane 7 — Free-Trial Seedbox Angle (Seedhost.eu + Pulsed Media + others)
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-20 (researched live this session) Target: Documents.zip — ONE file, 350,016,069,428 B (= 350.0 GB decimal = ~326 GiB) Infohash: 856d01039553693d51c2a98523ca2c9829e8bb63 Actual need: ~125 GB of gap ranges INSIDE the zip. Because the torrent is a single file, qBittorrent/ruTorrent file priorities cannot skip inner zip entries — the only seedbox-side selective paths are (a) hold the whole file, or (b) shell/SSH + a custom client (libtorrent piece priorities) that only fetches the pieces covering the wanted byte ranges.

docs.title: VERDICT: DEAD for this torrent as a free-trial path
docs.text:
No free trial found holds the file, and none holds even the wanted ranges at once. Numbers:

Candidate Free trial (verified) Trial storage SSH/shell on trial? vs 350 GB full vs ~125 GB gaps-at-once Pulsed Media 30-day free, when slots open 50 GiB, 250 MB RAM YES — user-level SSH, full PMSS set FAIL 6.5× (326 GiB needed) FAIL 2.3× (~116 GiB needed) Seedhost.eu NO free trial on current site — 7-day money-back on PAID plans only n/a (old 24 h trial no longer offered; its size was never published) Paid: SSH on all Shared except HD 1 FAIL — nothing free to hold it FAIL Ultra.cc No trials at all (official FAQ) — — FAIL FAIL Whatbox / Feral / Seedboxes.cc / RapidSeedbox No free tier (Pulsed comparison table) — — FAIL FAIL Seedbox.io No free trial — 14-day money-back only — — FAIL FAIL sdbx.moe Free 2-day trial on Discord request Not published, no ≥100 GB evidence Unknown FAIL / unproven, and Discord request = manual work FAIL

docs.text:

You can order any of our account and use it as a test, you can cancel it with the first 7 days and we will refund your money." No current Seedhost page publishes a trial size — there is nothing to verify ≥350 GB against, because there is no trial to size.
  • Paid plans (official, fetched https://www.seedhost.eu/shared-app-hosting/): HD 1 = 1 TB disk / 1 TB traffic / €3/mo (no SSH — FAQ: "Yes, we offer SSH access with all Shared App Hosting accounts, except HD 1"; no root on Shared); HD 2 = 2 TB / 2 TB traffic / €5/mo with SSH, "welcome to install anything locally via SSH in your HOME path." docs.title: 2. Pulsed Media — real free trial, real shell, 7× too small
docs.text:
Official wiki, fetched this session (https://wiki.pulsedmedia.com/wiki/Computer_resource):

  • "A free 30-day trial (50 GiB, 250 MB RAM) is offered when trial slots are open" + 14-day money-back on paid plans. Slot availability is conditional — no guarantee a slot is open today.
  • User access (same page): "SSH — User-level shell access (no root). Run commands, manage files, install user-space software" + web panel with a browser shell console. Free tier is listed on the wiki as "Free Seedbox — full PMSS feature set, evaluation use."
  • Stack (wiki Seedbox page, fetched): torrent clients rTorrent/ruTorrent, Deluge, qBittorrent; file access SSH, SFTP, SCP, FTP, HTTPS downloads, WebDAV; 100+ pre-installed CLI tools incl. Python 3, p7zip/unrar, rclone; rootless Docker on all plans; public trackers allowed.
  • Limits that bite: the media-stack installer "stops on accounts with less than 1000 MiB of memory, so it does not fit the free trial (250 MB)" — irrelevant to torrenting, but it shows how thin the trial slice is.
  • Free page (fetched https://pulsedmedia.com/free-seedbox.php): "You may go beyond your storage limit by 25% for up to 7 days" — even bursting, 50 GiB → 62.5 GiB (~67 GB), still <125 GB and ≪350 GB.

docs.title: The shell / piece-priority path — why it still fails
docs.text:
Pulsed is the one candidate where the (b) path is technically real:

  • SSH + Python/libtorrent (or a custom client) can set piece priorities so only pieces overlapping the wanted zip ranges download, stored as a sparse file — qBittorrent's own UI/API only exposes file priorities, which are useless inside a single-file torrent.
  • But the wanted ranges total ~125 GB and the quota is 50 GiB (53.7 GB). Holding the wanted pieces at once overflows quota by ~2.3×; holding the full file overflows by ~6.5×. Quota enforcement would stall/kill the download long before completion.
  • The only theoretical workaround is a rotating batch loop: fetch a <50 GiB batch of pieces → extract those zip entries locally on the box (p7zip is pre-installed) → offload via SFTP/rclone/HTTPS → delete → repeat. That is unproven custom tooling on a 250 MB RAM trial account, dependent on an open trial slot, with zip central-directory handling and quota behaviour untested. It is a research project, not a backup path — especially when the TorBox direct path already works today.
  • HTTPS Range: files are served by per-user lighttpd over HTTPS, which in principle supports Range requests, but Pulsed does not document a Range guarantee — UNVERIFIED. SFTP (resumable) is documented and would be the reliable pull method.

docs.title: 3. Any other free-trial seedbox ≥100 GB?
docs.text:
None found. Web searches this session (queries on free-trial seedbox storage/SSH, Seedhost/Pulsed/Ultra specifically) surfaced only:

  • Ultra.cc — explicitly no trials. Official docs FAQ (via search): "Does Ultra.cc Offer Trials? No. Ultra.cc does not offer free trials" — new customers only get a 7-day first-order refund policy. Paid entry €4.95/mo / 1 TB would fit, but it is not free.
  • Pulsed comparison table (fetched): Whatbox, Feral Hosting, Seedboxes.cc, RapidSeedbox, Seedhost.eu, Ultra.cc — Free Tier: No for every one; Pulsed is the only "Yes" in the table.
  • Seedbox.io: money-back (14 days) only, no free trial found.
  • sdbx.moe ToS (via search): "A free 2 day trial is available … The request must be made on our Discord server" — 2 days, request-by-Discord (manual step), storage not published, no evidence of ≥100 GB, let alone 350 GB. Fails both the size-evidence and the no-manual-work tests.

No provider anywhere in the sweep offers a free trial with ≥100 GB storage. The largest verified free seedbox storage in existence here is Pulsed's 50 GiB.

Method: gh api recursive tree censuses (blob counts, sizes, extensions), README / PIPELINE / AUDIT reads, last-commit dates, branch / PR / release state. Nothing was merged, pushed, or deleted — catalog only. Verification note (important): two of the four parallel audit lanes returned inflated claims that direct tree censuses contradicted (e.g. reporting catalog/index documents as if the cataloged files were in-repo). Every number in Parts 1, 2 and 4 below was re-verified against a live recursive tree census during compilation; where a claim could not be verified on main it is marked UNVERIFIED or corrected. Part 3 (cn-gigaleak) numbers rest on release-asset evidence plus the pull loop's byte-verified records, and the lane flagged its own census failures honestly. Standing rule for all leaked production files: study / reverse-engineer how the pros built it, owner's own use. Never redistribute, never lift characters / names / logos into Wizard Gang.

EP01 masters are NOT on main's tree (42 entries) despite older docs saying so Archive; masters' location needs a dedicated check — Goodville-Show 2/10 Canon pointer only: 2 files (AGENTS.md, WORKING-METHOD.md). No cutout pipeline, no Blair kits, no sensorium here — see corrections below Near-empty

Headline finding: Wizard Gang does not need a new stack bought or built from zero. Its own cast is ALREADY cut into puppet parts with rig-build scripts (God-Molecule-Show-Studio, rank 1), the how-to paperwork already exists per-character (animation-techniques-archive, rank 3), the pro templates to copy sit loose on releases at zero extraction cost (Foster's Frankie rig .fla + cartoon-vault's Smiling Friends rigs, ranks 2/4; Gumball's rig archive, rank 5), and the finishing software is already vendored (cape-jones, rank 6). Almost all of it is stored-only and was never wired into an episode — the V2 job is wiring, not acquiring.

Corrections to standing assumptions (verified this audit): - Glaxnimate IS in cape-jones — production/tools/glaxnimate/ (full source + GPL-3.0 COPYING + wiring doc), alongside Pencil2D source, COA Tools 2 (Blender cutout addon), and Rhubarb Lip Sync. (An interim version of this audit said the opposite based on a truncated grep — retracted; the directory listing was verified directly on 2026-10-29.) What did NOT check out: Glaxnimate/Krita source trees inside animation-techniques-archive — that repo's tooling is docs + small scripts only. - Goodville-Show holds no South Park cutout pipeline / Preston Blair kits / sensorium. Sensorium material sits in God-Molecule-Show-Studio tools/brain/sensorium/ (7 files) and its production-stage sibling; South Park-style construction paperwork lives in animation-techniques-archive's playbook/starter-kits as DOCUMENTS, not .blend/SVG kits. - God-molecule-production-stage is NOT a Godot-only repo: it carries the same tools/ trunk as God-Molecule-Show-Studio (animation-kit: EbSynth, RIFE, whitebox, grease-pencil probes; brain/knowledge 148 files; ai-qc) minus the wizard-rig-proof. - video-fix-tools V2 and pocket-studio V2 are the ORIGINAL AI pipeline, not a real-animation upgrade. - steal-like-artist-archive is essentially empty on main (5 blobs: README/AGENTS/WORKING-METHOD/NO-DATA-LOSS doc). The actual steal-like-artist material (character-pipeline, show-starter-kits, game-leaks) lives INSIDE animation-techniques-archive's steal-like-artist/ folder (1,305 of its 1,329 tree entries). - wizard-gang-storage main does not hold the EP01 masters tree older docs describe.

docs.text:
How to read this part: holdings live mostly in RELEASES (often draft, often opaque split archives), though several repos hold large browsable art packs ON MAIN (Dexter's, EEnE, Grim, Gym Partner, Space Ghost, Scooby Mystery Inc.). Every figure below was checked against a live tree census or a release asset listing during compilation; where a number comes from a pull-loop manifest/interior census rather than a direct listing, it is marked manifest-level. Byte totals are release-asset sums. All of it is study/template material under the standing sanitize/study rule. Warning carried from the audit lane: almost no .fla/.swf sits loose on any main — the named Flash rigs are the Frankie .fla (fosters-home), the 12 .fla in cartoon-vault, the Gumball S2 rigs zip, and PPG_flas.rar. docs.title: 1. BasicPBC (Paint Bucket Colorization, CVPR 2024)
docs.text:
• Upstream: https://github.com/ykdai/BasicPBC (official implementation, arXiv 2403.18342)
  • Install: git clone --depth 1 → ~/workspace/tools/basicpbc/ (was: directory gone entirely)
  • Pipeline role: colorize hand-drawn line frames by paint-bucket inclusion matching — feed it one colored keyframe (gt) + line frames, it colors the sequence. This is the "color the inbetweens from the key" stage of the cartoon factory.
  • VERDICT: WIRED+PROVEN — venv complete (torch 2.2.2+cpu + all deps import-verified; pin set in constraints.txt — without it timm drags in PyPI's CUDA torch; torch_scatter/matplotlib are imported by the code but missing from its requirements.txt). Both release checkpoints byte-exact: ckpt/basicpbc.pth 105,523,141 B, ckpt/basicpbc_light.pth 50,350,481 B. The seg stage's CLIP-convnext weights (1.41 GB, downloaded by open_clip at first use) are pre-staged in the local HF cache, the .bin blob SHA-256- verified byte-identical to upstream; run with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 so open_clip's safetensors-first lookup falls back to the cached .bin. CPU-portability patches (documented in tools/basicpbc/WIRING.md): map_location="cpu" on three bare torch.loads + conditional .cuda() at inference_line_frames.py:164 and basicsr/models/pbc_model.py:208 — the authors assume CUDA; GPU behavior unchanged. Proof: bundled laughing_girl frames (cv2-resized to 512² — PIL's RGBA resize destroys these frames) colorized end-to-end, 100% in 126 s/it: dataset/test/proof6/proof6/0001.png + color dict assigning the target frame's segments colors from the keyframe's own palette ([151,136,221], [86,16,35]); segmentation separately proven at native 1600² (117 segments, dataset/test/laughing_girl/seg/). Floors learned: <512² collapses segmentation to <2 keypoints (KeyError: 'match_scores'); the one-process native-res run OOMs on this shared 8 GB VM (CLIP ~2 GB + neighbors) — the two-stage --skip_seg split is the low-memory route. Full detail: tools/basicpbc/WIRING.md.

docs.title: 2. FlashXFLParser (XFL/.fla rig-structure parser)
docs.text:
• Upstream: https://github.com/jackisgames/FlashXFLParser (Unity C# project)
  • Install: git clone --depth 1 → ~/workspace/tools/FlashXFLParser/ (was: directory gone)
  • What the code actually is (read in full): the parser core is Assets/XFLParser/display/Symbol.cs — a pure-.NET XmlSerializer data model of an XFL library symbol (DOMSymbolItem → DOMTimeline → DOMLayer → DOMFrame → symbol/bitmap instances with matrices). editor/XFLLibraryEditor.cs is the import loop (deserialize every LIBRARY/*.xml into Symbol). Only Bitmap.cs/XFLLibrary.cs touch UnityEngine (Texture field / ScriptableObject shell). Wire-up = host the project's own parser classes in a .NET console harness with a minimal UnityEngine stub, repo parser files unmodified.
  • ⚠ FORMAT FINDING on the target file: pds3hx.fla (Frankie Foster rig, release frankie-rig-fla-v1, downloaded byte-exact 18,385,408 B) is NOT a ZIP/XFL .fla — file reports OLE2 "Composite Document File V2", i.e. the legacy binary FLA format (pre-CS5). The XFL parser cannot read it as-is; see the Frankie entry below for the decode path taken.
  • Pipeline role: read pro Flash rigs (layers, symbols, parts, tweens) so WG rigs can be built from their structure (USE-PRO-PRODUCTION-FILES-100% law).
  • VERDICT: WIRED+PROVEN — parser built from the project's own code (console host in tools/FlashXFLParser/harness/, .NET SDK 8.0.427) and proven on REAL rigs from cn-gigaleak-cartoon-vault release tv-gigaleak-fla-v1: Pim rig (5 part layers) and Charlie rig (18 symbols / 33 layers / 73 frames, 9-layer master symbol). The Frankie target file is a legacy pre-CS5 OLE binary (parser detects + reports it honestly); its structure was decoded at OLE level — 131 symbols, 466 named parts incl. the full 3/4-view set. Full detail: tools/FlashXFLParser/WIRING.md.

Counts are measured, not quoted: parts = numbered PNGs in parts/ (excl. _-prefixed work files: masks/composites); rig layers = PNGs in rig_layers/ (includes eye-closed + mouth swap layers); params = entries in proofs/rig_parameters.json (== params parsed out of the .inp); textures/animations/physics = parsed out of the .inp binary itself. docs.title: Formats — what opens what
docs.text: Format What it is Opens in .inp (18) nijilive puppet (Inochi2D-family serialization; built headlessly by build_rig.py via the image2live2d toolchain, Apache-2.0) nijigenerate / nijilive editor + Inochi2D runtimes. NOT a DragonBones or Blender format. Honest caveat from RIG_PROOF.md itself: no .inp has ever been opened in the nijigenerate GUI — headless GUI automation hit the first-run setup wizard (synthetic clicks don't register; the setup-wizard-fix/ folder documents the fix attempt). Structural validity is proven; editor-open is not. PNG part packs + rig_layers/ (425 PNGs) The universal asset — cut, stacked, swap-ready (eye-closed, mouth) Krita 6.0.4 (installed above), Tahoma2D 1.6.3 (installed above), Blender via COA Tools 2 / Tiny 2D Rig, any compositor. render_poses.py already renders posed stills from the rig data headlessly (the proofs/ PNGs are deformations of the actual .inp data, not mockups). .blend None for the WG cast. The only .blend in the wider GMSS tools tree is tools/character/Marshead_rigged_v1.blend (a 3D Mars head, not a WG puppet). Blender — not applicable to the cast today; a Blender cast rig would be built FROM the PNG packs (COA Tools 2 / Tiny 2D Rig route). DragonBones No DragonBones-format WG rig exists (no _ske.json/_tex.json anywhere in the puppet tree). tools/animation/DRAGONBONES_WIRING.md names DragonBones as the free skeletal path and claims cloned MIT runtimes at tools/animation/upstream/dragonbones-js/ — that directory is ABSENT from main HEAD (verified in this checkout; tools/animation/ holds only the doc + 7 Python scripts: animate_rig.py, blender_import.py, build_slice.py, fallback_render.py, make_visual_evidence.py, proxy_generator.py, rig_proxy.py). DragonBones is a doc, not a rig source, today.

docs.title: Recommendation — FIRST proof shot
docs.text:
Use the nijilive .inp format, Ashes standard — the only format in which a finished, validated WG rig actually exists.

  • Character/rig: Ashes standard — richest rig in the cast (24 params, 15 textures, 18 animations) and the ONLY standard puppet with a working mouth (ParamMouthOpenY/ParamMouthForm on the grill layer), so the proof can include a line of dialogue with Rhubarb-driven grill movement, not just a silent pose.
  • Exact files:
  • Rig: ~/workspace/_wg-v2-wireup/gmss/tools/puppet/wizard-rig-proof/ashes/Ashes.inp (canonical source: GMSS tools/puppet/wizard-rig-proof/ashes/Ashes.inp)
  • Pose/animation driver: ashes/render_poses.py (already renders true deformations of this rig headlessly — extend it from stills to a PNG sequence: neutral → head-turn (ParamAngleX=30, ParamAngleY=-15) → blink (ParamEyeLOpen/R=0) → mouth-open line (ParamMouthOpenY), on 2s per the mystery-coast doctrine)
  • Ground-truth targets: ashes/proofs/ashes_pose_neutral.png, ashes_pose_head-turn_mouth-open.png, ashes_pose_blink.png, ashes_pose_comparison.png
  • Param map: ashes/proofs/rig_parameters.json; part fallback/QA: ashes/parts/ + ashes/parts/parts_manifest.json, ashes/rig_layers/
  • Validator (fix the one hardcoded path line first): ashes/validate_inp.py
  • Assembly: sequence → ffmpeg; grade with tools/color/presets.sh (vibrant-cartoon); comp/finish in Natron 2.5.0 if a background plate is added.
  • Why this first: zero re-rigging — the rig, its animations, its pose proofs and its validator all exist and passed today; the renderer path (render_poses.py) is the one WG-rig renderer that has demonstrably produced correct output on this VM. The shot proves the actual V2 asset, not a rebuild of it.
  • Why not the alternatives first: DragonBones has no WG rigs (doc only, runtimes absent from HEAD — building there means re-rigging all 18 from PNGs before frame one). A Blender COA/Tiny-2D-Rig rebuild from the PNG packs is the strongest second path (Blender headless is proven on this VM) but is still a re-rig; Tahoma2D is now installed and verified (incl. headless tcomposer) and is the doctrine episode stage, but no WG .tnz scene exists yet — make it shot 2's stage test rather than betting the first proof on two unproven firsts at once. The known open risk on the recommended path is the nijigenerate GUI (never successfully operated headless) — the proof shot deliberately does NOT depend on the GUI; it drives the .inp through the Python renderer. A human/first-GUI open of Ashes.inp in nijigenerate remains an owed check for full editor-based production.

docs.title: Producerbot workflow: how to continue exactly as Producerbot works
docs.text: Written 2026-10-14 so Muse and every other agent can pick up the owner's (mhvnsnt) work with no guessing. Repo-specific notes are at the bottom. When something here conflicts with an owner message, the owner wins: write the new rule here in the same PR.

docs.title: 0. Start of every task
docs.text:
1. Read this file, AGENTS.md, CANON.md (games), and the agent-ops board: mhvnsnt/agent-ops → TAG-TEAM.md (who is on what) and CLAIMS.md.
  2. Claim first. Add one line to CLAIMS.md (<agent> | <repo> | <task> | <date>) on a branch and open a PR with gh. Don't start work someone else claimed. Current owners: creation suite + teardown importers = Repo Co Dev; physics + physics test env = the physics agent; T-pose renders = Muse.
  3. Pull main before you touch shared files (git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main). Another job may be editing the same folder: work only in your files, resolve conflicts by keeping both sides.

docs.title: 1. Clones and disk (box is shared and often near full)
docs.text:
df -h /                                                     # check first; stop if < 3 GB free
git clone --filter=blob:none --depth 1 https://github.com/mhvnsnt/<repo> <dir>      # shallow, blobless
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/mhvnsnt/<repo> <dir> && cd <dir> && git sparse-checkout set <paths...>
- Clone into /workspace/<task>/, not into another agent's folder. - Back up before delete. Never delete anything that is not verified saved. For a clone: git status --porcelain | wc -l must be 0, git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline | wc -l must be 0, and every branch must show in git ls-remote origin. Stashes → push as backup/box-<date>-<name> branches. Uncommitted → commit to a backup/... branch, never main. - Big untracked/ignored files → private mhvnsnt/box-storage as Release assets: sha256sum f > f.sha256; gh release upload <tag> f f.sha256 -R mhvnsnt/box-storage, then download it back and compare SHA-256 before deleting the local copy. - Log every move with links in agent-ops BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md. Keep anything an agent is using right now. - Ports: 8765 and 8791 are often taken by others. Pick a high free port (python3 -m http.server 18437 -b 127.0.0.1 -d game).

docs.title: 2. Git, PRs, merging
docs.text:
• PRs only through the gh CLI from the box, never the connector "create PR" form (the owner refuses to submit forms): git push -u origin <branch> && gh pr create -R mhvnsnt/<repo> --head <branch> --title "..." --body "..."
  • Branch names grok/<repo-short>-<topic>. Small PRs, one piece each. Push each piece as soon as it's done (incremental pushes), never sit on local work.
  • Merge rule (owner, Oct 14 2026): a PR merges into main only if it merges cleanly, its tests/CI pass, and it deletes or breaks nothing on main. Otherwise it stays open. Repos with .github/workflows/pr-clean-merge.yml (money-machine-hq, God Molecule, TRIPPEDD, Bannon) auto-merge when green; it fails any PR that deletes a file on main, and it never auto-merges PRs touching .github/workflows (owner merges those).
  • Check before merging: gh pr checks <n> -R mhvnsnt/<repo> and gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus. If checks are invisible or failing on main too, say so and leave the PR open.
  • Commit identity on the box: git config user.name "Producerbot (Grok Bot)"; git config user.email mhvnsnt@users.noreply.github.com.

docs.title: 3. Media proof standard (never claim without proof)
docs.text: Full gate list: /home/box/agent-data/workflows/media-proof-standard/SKILL.md. Short form: - Reopen the bytes you wrote (PIL verify, ffprobe, full ffmpeg -f null decode, GLB load). - Open the frames/PNGs yourself with an image reader and look: subject present, no blank frames, text spelled right. - SHA-256 every deliverable (sha256sum) into a manifest (parts.json / SHA256SUMS / PROVENANCE.md). - Edits to owner art/models: before/after of the same frame, side by side. - No AI faces. Characters are rendered from the owner's own models or real imports. AI only for non-character plates, labelled AI_PLATE. - Unknown origin = "parts unknown". Never invent canon. Card text comes from CANON.md through a script. - Version, never overwrite: _v2, _a1wip, base_v1. Originals and teardown files are never edited. - Never say "rescanned" for a recolor. Say what was actually done. - You can't hear audio: say so and ask the owner to listen.

docs.title: 4. How the Western Heart UI screens were built (game/ui-wh/, PR #121, #123)
docs.text:
1. Layouts mapped from teardowns, rebuilt not copied: title = TTT2/T6; main menu = Urban Reign/TTT2 list with JP sub-label; mode select = Def Jam/WWE cards; character select = T6/TTT2 (P1 left, P2 right, grid middle, timer); VS = Def Jam/WWE diagonal; HUD = T6 bars + Nine-Soul meter; pause = Urban Reign/Tekken; results = WWE/Def Jam. Table in game/ui-wh/README.md.
  2. Wallpaper transform: python3 game/ui-wh/tools/make_wallpaper.py derives art/wallpaper_wh.png from the owner's game/assets/ui/title-bg.png: 16:9 crop dropping the logo band → heavy blur (source characters become light) → indigo/crimson/gold duotone + crimson sun → Pantera rendered from his GLB as hero → Western Heart Japanese text. Source file untouched.
  3. Portraits from GLBs in Godot (no AI): xvfb-run -a godot --rendering-driver opengl3 --path lab/game -s res://tools/render_ui_portraits.gd -- $(pwd)/game/ui-wh/portraits. Any GLB + recipe: lab/game/tools/render_card.gd (see §5).
  4. Playwright capture + self-review loop: serve game/, then PW_CHROMIUM=/usr/bin/google-chrome WH_PORT=<port> node game/ui-wh/tools/capture.mjs docs/qa/ui-wh (needs a playwright install; on the box ln -s /tmp/gb-pw/node_modules node_modules temporarily, remove before commit). It fails on any page error / 404 / wrong active screen / broken keyboard flow. Then open every PNG, fix what looks wrong, capture again. Repeat until it passes AND looks right.

docs.title: 5. Roster cards and showcases (docs/roster/ROSTER_CARDS.md, PR #125)
docs.text:
python3 game/ui-wh/tools/canon_to_roster.py          # CANON.md -> game/ui-wh/roster_canon.json (never hand-edit)
# real render only if a model fits the canon description; else MODEL PENDING silhouette + full canon text
xvfb-run -a godot --rendering-driver opengl3 --path lab/game -s res://tools/render_card.gd -- $PWD/<glb> /tmp/<id> $PWD/docs/roster/<id>/kitbash_v1.json 20
WH_PORT=<port> PW_CHROMIUM=/usr/bin/google-chrome node game/ui-wh/tools/capture_cards.mjs docs/qa/roster-cards
- Lock state is data: roster.js isUnlocked(); Pantera only by default; ?unlock=all only for promo captures. - Card = render, name, kanji, soul, tier line, quote, Tekken body, element, ORIGIN parts unknown, signature. Flag on the art: ATTIRE 1 / WIP KITBASH / MODEL PENDING. - Kitbash (owner t48u): re-dress existing models with parts from every teardown (TTT2/T6, Def Jam, Urban Reign, WWE) on versioned copies; log every part in docs/roster/<id>/parts.json with source, SHA-256, third_party, pre-sale action. Worked example: docs/roster/zui/ (base T7 Steve Fox import → hide hair, robe recolour, indigo pants, sake gourd, beads, sash → before/after + SHA-256). Honest gap: no extracted head/hair meshes from TTT2/Def Jam/Urban Reign/WWE are on main yet. - Showcase = select (default + unlock all) + every card + promo strip (cards.html#strip?ids=...). Look at every PNG before reporting.

docs.title: 6. Height / scale system (PR #120)
docs.text: lab/game/data/characters/heights.json (cm per fighter) → lab/game/scripts/height_scale.gd scales each fighter at fight load; HUD shows height; tests lab/game/tests/test_height_scale.gd (46 pass). Tekken 6/TTT2 publish no heights; values borrowed from Tekken 7/8 profiles need owner OK (rule check holds it).

docs.title: 7. T-pose and model co-author pipeline
docs.text: T-pose standard: docs/tpose-refs/MUSE_TPOSE_SPEC.md (one-to-one T-pose, pure white, fingertips in frame, flat light, every attire). Flow: T-pose image → Tripo 3D → rig (Tripo/Mixamo) → python3 tools/import_model.py <glb> --character <id> --attire <a> --render (rig map, Tekken segments, P1 retarget map, rig gates, register; docs/MODEL_IMPORT_AUTORIG.md) → co-author in Blender / creation suite (docs/CREATE_A_FIGHTER_SPEC.md, Repo Co Dev) → move-set (docs/MOVESET_EDITOR_SPEC.md). Drive links: AGENT_IMPORT_RUNBOOK in CREATE_A_FIGHTER_SPEC.md. Secondary/jiggle bone names for the physics sandbox: MODEL_IMPORT_AUTORIG.md.

docs.title: 8. Entrance videos
docs.text: Exact method: money-machine-hq/docs/production-bible/ENTRANCE_VIDEO_METHOD.md (also in Bannon, God Molecule, TRIPPEDD): rig repair, animation, ring + lights, name plate and cards, beat-grid edit (every cut on the beat grid), music, post commands, vertical cut. Owner's spelling rules apply (e.g. "STICK UP", no hyphen).

docs.title: 9. Teardown → proprietary rule
docs.text: Build on top, never destroy. Teardown files stay byte-identical; everything new is a derived, versioned file. Transform into the Eastern Mind · Western Heart universe (names, souls, kanji, colours, parts) until it reads as ours. Track every remaining third-party piece (third_party: true + pre-sale action in parts.json / move slots) so it can be replaced before any sale. Tell the owner plainly what is still third-party.

docs.title: 10. Honesty rules
docs.text:
• Report failures, blocks and gaps in the same message as the wins.
  • Never say done, fixed, merged or "looks better" without the proof from §3 and a link.
  • Never claim to have watched/listened. Never invent canon, faces or data.
  • Prefer a smaller true result over a bigger claimed one.

docs.title: Phase 1 — security audit verdicts (owner's hard gate)
docs.text:
Method: full source audit per tool (package.json, Dockerfile, server.json, ALL of src/, scripts/ where present) — postinstall hooks, network egress, env/credential access, remote-code execution, obfuscation, write scope, telemetry. Environment forced the route: git clone is broken VM-wide and tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, so source was read via the GitHub contents API and raw file reads, cross-verified by blob SHA. Zero REJECTs. Universal findings: no preinstall/postinstall/prepare hooks anywhere, no telemetry/analytics anywhere, no ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, Keychain, or browser-profile access by any tool's own code.

Tool Version Verdict greenlight 0.25.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — GitHub tool; opt-in --via-api claim flow talks to the author's hosted API (claim-api-wine.vercel.app) and auth login stores our GitHub token (keychain or 0600 file) BY DESIGN — do not use --via-api/auth login; direct-GitHub mode only. Opt-in Fireworks LLM egress only if FIREWORKS_API_KEY set. sh -c only runs the target repo's own CI/test commands (its ci-prep/verify features — never against untrusted repos) injectcheck 0.1.19 CLEAN — zero egress/env; all credential/curl hits are detection-rule data hookcheck 0.1.18 CLEAN — zero egress/exec/writes in own code; hits are detection patterns actionpin 0.1.8 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — GITHUB_TOKEN sent only to hardcoded api.github.com; fix rewrites our workflow files (its job; has --dry-run) depguard 0.4.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — offline core; npm/PyPI registry only behind --online/--content; tarballs diffed in memory, never installed/executed flowcheck 0.1.2 CLEAN — pure local YAML audit cidiff 0.1.2 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — GITHUB_TOKEN for GitHub API; API base env-overridable only by our own config mcpvet 0.2.1 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — only egress is npm registry metadata; opt-in probe runs a user-supplied local server command mcpaudit 0.1.2 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — zero egress; spawns the target server (its job) with FULL host env copied in — always run it with a scrubbed env against untrusted servers shipcheck 0.2.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — egress only to api.github.com / npm / PyPI / MCP Registry / GHCR (its job); reads only GITHUB_TOKEN, sent only to api.github.com agentsfile 0.1.0 CLEAN — read-only local validation skillcheck 0.1.0 CLEAN — read-only local validation; links resolved on disk, never fetched testdelta 0.1.0 CLEAN — reads only the two user-named result JSONs logdigest 0.1.0 CLEAN — reads only the one user-named log file readmeaudit 0.1.0 CLEAN — read-only local auditor commitcheck 0.1.0 CLEAN — only subprocess is fixed shell-free git log agent-evals 0.1.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — agent URLs are user-supplied (its job); LLM-judge POSTs to api.anthropic.com only when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set prodforge 0.5.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — downloads/installs nothing itself; only GENERATES an npx -y fleet config — fleet packages stand on their own audits (done, this table) muse-farm 0.5.1 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — stdlib Python; wraps muse exec; reads Muse session logs under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions (its supervise job); ntfy.sh POST only when a user topic is configured; self-update is explicit-invocation git-pull + test run muse-marketplace 0.1.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — zero network/subprocess; install = sha256-verified local copy with executable-extension denylist specforge 0.1.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — fixed shell-free command table (git checkout -b, npx prettier/eslint, npm test/audit) in the target project only scenemodel 0.1.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — only egress is the Blender addon socket (BLENDER_HOST:BLENDER_PORT, default localhost:9876); PolyHaven/Hunyuan are forwarded to the addon, not called directly videokit 0.1.0 CLEAN — arg-array execFile ffmpeg/ffprobe; no env/network/shell audioport 0.1.0 CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — only env key is AUDIOPORT_TRANSCRIBER_COMMAND, an operator-chosen local command, execFile no shell imageport 0.1.0 CLEAN — arg-array execFile ImageMagick; no env/network/shell Xod parts (v0.9.23, commit 6e5ebd4) — CLEAN-WITH-NOTES — sentinel core is stdlib-only, zero egress (its review_message() delegates to the host's configured LLM — we use the deterministic core); benchmark localhost-only; scorecard read-only; worktrees' pull_request() pushes to origin (review before use); agent_clis --yolo refusal is real and enforced, BUT its install() helper runs hardcoded vendor curl|sh — that function is EXCLUDED from our pull-in, registry pattern only

docs.title: Honest limits
docs.text:
• The tools are days old, single-author, 0-star. Greenlight is the only battle-tested piece. Everything is pinned to exact versions in tools/cloudcorp/mcp.json so an upstream change never reaches us silently; re-audit before any version bump.
  • npm is broken on the current VM (EPERM on registry writes), so test-runs that needed npm install were run where the environment allowed and are marked honestly in TEST-RUNS.md; anything not run is marked NOT-RUN with the reason, never claimed as working.
  • scenemodel/videokit/audioport/imageport adoption INSIDE western-heart is the next step (western-heart has live lanes; this lane lands config + usage docs in agent-ops only).

docs.title: CloudCorpRecords — RESEARCH / WATCH list (everything not in the top 25)
docs.text: Logged 2026-11-02 per owner order: every CloudCorpRecords repo that was NOT pulled in is recorded here as RESEARCH/WATCH, with what it could help us with. The full per-repo table (name, license, language, last updated, description) is INVENTORY.md in this folder — each repo's description there is its one-line "what it is"; the notes below add "what it could help us with" by group. 355 repos total in the inventory (265 originals + 90 forks), minus xod/internet-of-things, minus the 25 pulled in (see README.md in this folder).

docs.title: Rules for this list
docs.text:
• No-license / NONE / NOASSERTION repos = WATCH / IDEAS ONLY. Never pull code from them. (45 NONE + 15 NOASSERTION in the sweep.)
  • Forks are not CloudCorpRecords code. If a fork looks useful, evaluate and pull from UPSTREAM, never from this account.
  • AGPL/GPL repos (6 AGPL-3.0, 2 GPL-3.0): document-only unless a lane confirms the license fits the destination repo.
  • Anything promoted off this list goes through the same gate as the top 25: source security audit → pinned pull-in → test-run on our own material. No exceptions.

docs.title: Groups and what they could help with
The *-port SaaS wrapper fleet (~120 repos, mostly MIT/TypeScript)
docs.text: Clean-room MCP rebuilds of known services — CRM (crmport HubSpot, crmcloud Salesforce), payments (payport Stripe), comms (channelchat Slack, chatport WhatsApp, mailport Gmail), cloud (deployport Vercel, cloudpanel Azure, clusterport kubectl, containerport Docker), data (databridge-kit SQL, cacheport Redis, pgport Postgres), search (searchport Brave, deepsearch Exa, crawlport Firecrawl). Help potential: LOW for now — we already have official connectors or better routes for nearly all of these (GitHub MCP/gh, Google connectors, Vercel connector, Stripe connector). WATCH for: any service we adopt later that has no official MCP — a *-port wrapper plus a fresh audit is a fast starting point. Subsets are partial (e.g. animeport is 20 of 42 upstream tools), and several depend on hosted/keyed backends rather than being fully local.

docs.title: Original fleet beyond the top 25 (MIT unless noted)
docs.text:
• greenlight-adjacent: claimcheck, gatefile, gapproof, reprocheck, tracewatch, claimcheck — release/claim hygiene; claimcheck is in the index of candidate promotions (it was #26 in spirit; audit before use like everything else).
  • Repo hygiene cluster: contextbudget (token-budget auditor — could help lane context discipline), envdoctor, envdoc, linkrot, lockdrift, installaudit, npmpreflight, tododebt, typosquat, wallcheck, readmeaudit-adjacent tools — cheap deterministic CI checks; promote individually if a lane hits the matching pain.
  • Agent tooling: burnmeter (Claude Code token analytics — could feed Proving Ground cost scoring), thinkstep, termmux, sandboxrun, deskcommand, inboxwatch — WATCH.
  • Media/voice beyond the pulled four: cliqwise (video→vertical clips; finished-episode sources only per CLIP SOURCE LAW), voicegen-port (ElevenLabs MCP — complements our connector), musicport (Spotify MCP), videohub-port (YouTube Data API) — promote when the Wizard Gang / Concrete Dragon clip lanes need them, with audit.
  • Browser/QA: browserdebug (Chrome perf/network/console), browserstage/headlessstage (audited in the sweep as effectively stubs standalone — no browser bundled; executor must be injected) — WATCH, do not rely on them as-is.
  • Hosted-key products (deprioritized by design): taskpilot (api.coderide.ai), cueport (api.cueapi.ai), policyrecall (hosted signed-memory), visualdiff (SnapDiff API) — they need third-party hosted services; specforge (pulled in) covers the local-first equivalent ground.
  • Games in the account: open-city-remake (MIT, GTA-style web slice), strikemobile (MIT, UE5 tactical FPS), test-ai (Godot experiments) — design/reference reading only; neither maps onto western-heart (web fighting) or Bannon (wrestling) without an engine switch.
  • Exotic public-data wrappers: brdata, ashareport, procureport, myopendata, chainlens, lancontrol, nasport, topiclint — no current fit; WATCH only.

docs.title: No-license watch-only (IDEAS ONLY — never pull code)
docs.text:
• ai-handoff — two AIs hand off via one shared docs/AI_HANDOFF.md per repo with MCP tools handoff_read/append/ask/answer. The IDEA fits our TAG-TEAM / no-relay handoff system; implement our own version if wanted.
  • musicboi — MusicGen + local DAW in Electron (3 stars, no license). Idea watch for the music lanes.
  • agent-eval-harness, context-budget-analyzer, browserboi, nightshift-gb10 — prototypes/patterns only (agent-evals, the MIT one, is the pulled-in eval harness).

docs.title: Forks worth knowing (pull from UPSTREAM if ever used)
docs.text:
• squidbrake (Apache-2.0) — "agents propose, people approve" gate with tamper-evident record; matches the Xod approval model — candidate for the agent-ops safety layer.
  • cuga-agent (Apache-2.0, IBM) — enterprise agent harness; Proving Ground benchmark/reference.
  • manim (MIT) — mathematical animation engine; cartoon-factory explainer segments.
  • soundcraft (Apache-2.0) — scriptable DAW in Rust; music/voice production research.
  • SceneDreamer (no license in API) — 3D scene generation; Forge3D research only.
  • activepieces / composio / n8n — automation aggregators; we already have a Composio skill, no new pull needed.
  • ClipForge (MIT) — Chrome video clipping studio; alternative to cliqwise for the pages.
  • Remaining ~80 forks (openclaw, firecrawl, E2B, chroma, nocodb, ToolJet, open-webui, awesome-mcp-servers, etc.) are a curation signal only — the author found them worth forking; no action.

docs.title: Xod and internet-of-things (the two the owner asked about first)
docs.text:
• xod — parts pulled in (tools/xod-parts/); the app itself is NOT adopted (duplicates Muse; Mac-first). WATCH for its fix-round releases — its changelog grading culture is the pattern our Proving Ground harness borrows.
  • internet-of-things — no code, no license, 3 markdown files. Nothing to pull, ever; its scoreboard claims are not publicly verifiable. WATCH only as a catalog pointer to the per-tool repos.

docs.title: Security Audit — actionpin
docs.text:
• Repo / package: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/actionpin — @reneturcios/actionpin
  • Version (pin this): 0.1.8
  • Bin: dist/cli.js (CLI + stdio MCP server)
  • Dependencies: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3 (dev: @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5)
  • License: MIT
  • Method used: git clone and codeload tarballs failed on this VM (clone symref write error; tarballs 0 bytes through the proxy). Source was fetched file-by-file through the GitHub API contents endpoint via the GitHub MCP connector (get_file_contents, the same contents API gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/actionpin/contents/<path> wraps), saved as raw API snapshots in src/actionpin/rawsnap/, and audited in-memory with line-accurate scans; flagged lines were read in context.
  • Coverage: package.json, Dockerfile, server.json, and ALL of src/ (cli.ts, core.ts, index.ts, mcp.ts, types.ts). No bin/ or scripts/ directory exists. test/ not line-audited — not shipped (files: dist, server.json).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: scripts are only build (tsc), dev, test. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Credential access — justified: reads exactly one env key, process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN, at src/core.ts:860 inside ghHeaders(). It is placed only in an Authorization: Bearer header (src/core.ts:861) sent to hardcoded https://api.github.com URLs (src/core.ts:881–884 git-ref/commit lookups; src/core.ts:900–903 annotated-tag dereference). There is no base-URL override anywhere in the tool, so the token cannot be redirected to another host by configuration. Resolving a tag to a commit SHA is impossible without the GitHub API — this is the tool's stated job. The token is optional (requests work unauthenticated at lower rate limits).
  • Network egress: api.github.com only, via an injectable FetchFn (real global fetch passed in at src/cli.ts:98,103 and src/mcp.ts:42; unit tests inject fixtures and never touch the network, src/types.ts:135–146). No other hosts are contacted; github.com / static.modelcontextprotocol.io / registry.npmjs.org appear only as metadata in package.json/server.json.
  • fs writes — feature-scoped: the CLI fix command rewrites the user's own workflow files in place at src/core.ts:1046 (writeFileSync(file, lines.join("\n")) inside applyPinPlan) — that rewrite is the tool's purpose, is user-invoked, and has a --dry-run path. The MCP surface exposes only auditWorkflows / auditOrg / buildPinPlan (src/mcp.ts:7), not the apply/write path.
  • eval / exec: none — no eval, new Function, vm, child_process. No ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, keychain, or browser-profile access.
  • Obfuscation / data collection: none. No telemetry endpoints.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: Notes: (1) GITHUB_TOKEN env read at src/core.ts:860, sent only as a Bearer header to hardcoded api.github.com endpoints to resolve action refs to SHAs — required by its job, no override path. (2) Egress is api.github.com only. (3) The CLI fix command writes the user's workflow files in place (src/core.ts:1046) — the tool's stated purpose; the MCP tools are read/plan-only.

docs.title: Security Audit — agent-evals
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/agent-evals (MIT)
  • Version: 0.1.0 (package.json)
  • npm: name is unscoped agent-evals; no bin entry in package.json — run via the evals script (tsx src/index.ts) / npx agent-evals per README.
  • Dependencies: @anthropic-ai/sdk ^0.30.0, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.0.0, commander ^12.0.0; dev @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5. Note: all three runtime deps appear unused in src/ — the judge calls the Anthropic API with raw fetch, the MCP agent adapter is hand-rolled JSON-RPC over fetch, and argv is parsed manually. Unused deps are a hygiene note, not a security issue. web/ is a separate Next.js leaderboard viewer with its own web/package.json.
  • Method used: git clone is broken VM-wide (“unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted”) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, and tar extraction into the scratch tree hit write-EPERM — so no local src/ copy could be persisted. Primary method per coordinator: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/agent-evals/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file inventory and gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/agent-evals/contents/<path> (base64 content) for source, cross-checked with streamed raw.githubusercontent.com reads: full-file reads of package.json, src/agent.ts, src/index.ts, src/runner.ts, src/scorer.ts, and grep -n scans of the remaining files listed under Coverage. Nothing was installed or run.
  • Coverage: All executable source covered — package.json (+ web/package.json), every file in src/ (agent.ts, index.ts, runner.ts, scorer.ts, types.ts, suites/latency.ts, suites/rag-accuracy.ts, suites/tool-use.ts), plus test/*.ts, web/app/page.tsx, web/app/layout.tsx, README.md, data/rag-corpus.json (scanned). Bundled results/*.json are data outputs (inventoried, not code). No Dockerfile in this repo.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install hooks: Scripts are evals, build, test only. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Network egress — two destinations, both are the tool's job:
  • User-supplied agent endpoint. src/agent.ts httpAgent(baseUrl) does fetch(\${url}/run`, POST {input, tools});mcpAgent(serverUrl)doesfetch(serverUrl, POST JSON-RPC tools/call). The URL comes from the required--agent CLI flag (src/index.tscmdRun`). No default or hardcoded third-party agent endpoint.
  • Hardcoded Anthropic judge endpoint. src/scorer.ts llmJudgeScorer does fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", …) with header x-api-key and default model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. It sends the eval case input, the expected answer, and the agent's output to Anthropic for PASS/FAIL grading. It only runs for cases whose judge is neither exact nor keyword (src/runner.ts scoreCase), and if the key is unset it returns “skipped” without calling out.
  • Credential / env access: Exactly one key in the whole tool: src/scorer.ts reads process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. No other process.env in src/ (test file test/scorer.test.ts:95 deletes it for tests). No ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, Keychain, or browser-profile access.
  • Code execution: No child_process, eval, or new Function anywhere in src/.
  • Filesystem: src/index.ts writes only under a CWD-relative results/ dir, and only with --publish: results/<agent>-<suite>-<timestamp>.json, plus results/leaderboard.json regenerated from results/*.json (also rewritten by the leaderboard command). Reads are results/*.json and the bundled data/rag-corpus.json.
  • Web viewer: web/app/page.tsx reads the results/leaderboard files server-side and renders them; no egress found (grep-verified). Docs reference http://localhost:3000 as an example agent URL.
  • Distinct hosts: api.anthropic.com (hardcoded, judge only), whatever host the user passes to --agent, localhost (docs example). No telemetry/analytics endpoints.
  • Obfuscation / data collection: None. Plain readable TypeScript; bundled results/*.json are the author's mock-run outputs.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: Notes are exactly the egress/env above, both intrinsic to an eval harness: (1) it POSTs eval inputs/outputs to the user-supplied agent URL — its job; (2) the LLM-judge scorer sends case input + expected + agent output to api.anthropic.com using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment, only when an llm-judged case runs and the key is set. No other egress, no other secrets, no install hooks, no subprocesses.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:

Examined and benign: src/core.ts:55 includes the string ".npmrc" in a list of well-known config filenames whose existence in the checked repo is tested with existsSync (src/core.ts:85) — the file's contents are never read, and no credential store (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, keychain, browser profiles, .git-credentials) is touched anywhere.

docs.title: Audit — audioport (@reneturcios/audioport)
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/audioport (MIT)
  • Version: 0.1.0 (package.json, VERSION in src/audioport.ts, server.json 0.1.0)
  • Method: git clone is broken VM-wide (unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy. Primary method used: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/audioport/contents/<path> (base64 content, decoded) and gh api …/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file listing; the transcriber evidence lines (AUDIOPORT_TRANSCRIBER_COMMAND at :41/:223, whitespace-split at :230) were re-verified through this route and match. Core src/audioport.ts also read in full via supplementary raw.githubusercontent.com fetches with identical content/line numbers. src/audioport/package.json persisted under src/ via the file-write tool.
  • Files read: package.json, README.md, Dockerfile, server.json, src/audioport.ts, src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/types.ts, src/index.ts (pattern scan + core full read).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: none in package.json (scripts: build/dev/test only). Lockfile hasInstallScript only on dev-only esbuild/fsevents. Runtime deps: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3 only.
  • Network egress: none in the package. No fetch/http/net imports, no URLs in code (Dockerfile label aside). Explicitly no hosted transcription service and no API key anywhere.
  • Credential/env access — exactly one key: AUDIOPORT_TRANSCRIBER_COMMAND, read at src/audioport.ts:41 (constant) and :223 (process.env[TRANSCRIBER_COMMAND_ENV] in createDefaultTranscriber). No other env keys; no credential files read.
  • Process execution:
  • Audio tools: runExecFile (src/audioport.ts:53) is execFile(command, args, {timeout: 300000, maxBuffer: 16MB}) — argument arrays, no shell. Callers pass the literals "ffmpeg"/"ffprobe" with fixed flag arrays (metadata probe, convert, trim seek, loudnorm normalize).
  • Transcription (the note): when AUDIOPORT_TRANSCRIBER_COMMAND is set by the operator, its value is whitespace-split (commandLine.split(/\s+/), src/audioport.ts in createDefaultTranscriber) and run via the same execFile with the audio file path appended as the last argument; stdout is the transcript. This is an operator-configured local command executed by design (README documents it, e.g. whisper-cli --model base). It is not a shell (no shell parsing/injection surface beyond the operator's own configured words; quoting inside the variable is not supported, by construction), it is never set by the package, and when unset transcribe fails with an error naming the variable — no fallback, no network substitute.
  • eval / new Function: none.
  • fs writes: none by the package itself; ffmpeg writes caller-specified output paths.
  • Telemetry / data collection: none.
  • Obfuscation: none.
  • Dockerfile: two-stage node:20-alpine, npm ci, USER node, no ffmpeg bundled. No curl|sh.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: One env key, AUDIOPORT_TRANSCRIBER_COMMAND, and it names a local command the operator chooses which audioport then runs via arg-array execFile (no shell) with the input path appended — justified and documented; adopters should treat setting that variable as granting that command execution, because it is one. Everything else: no egress, no keys, no shell, no install scripts.

docs.title: Security Audit — commitcheck
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/commitcheck (MIT)
  • Version: 0.1.0 (package.json)
  • npm: @reneturcios/commitcheck · Bin: commitcheck → dist/cli.js
  • Dependencies: runtime @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3; dev @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5
  • Method used: git clone is broken VM-wide (“unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted”) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, and tar extraction into the scratch tree hit write-EPERM — so no local src/ copy could be persisted. Primary method per coordinator: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/commitcheck/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file inventory and gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/commitcheck/contents/<path> (base64 content) for source, cross-checked with streamed raw.githubusercontent.com reads (curl | grep -n for exact line numbers; full-file reads of package.json, src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts, and the src/core.ts git-call context). Nothing was installed or run.
  • Coverage: All executable source covered — package.json, every file in src/ (cli.ts, core.ts, index.ts, mcp.ts, types.ts), plus Dockerfile, server.json, workflows, and test/ (grep-scanned). Test fixtures under test/fixtures/ (plain commit-message .txt files) were covered by tree listing, not full per-fixture download.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install hooks: package.json scripts are only build (tsc), dev, test. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Network egress: None. No fetch, http/https/net/tls, WebSocket, or URL literals in src/ (grep-verified). MCP mode is stdio-only (src/mcp.ts, tool check_commits).
  • Credential / env / secret access: None. No process.env in src/; no ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, Keychain, browser-profile, or token access. It reads commit messages from the target repo's history — that is the tool's stated input, read locally via git.
  • Code execution — one fixed, shell-free subprocess: src/core.ts:19 imports execFileSync from node:child_process; src/core.ts:308 calls execFileSync("git", ["-C", target, "log", "-n", String(MAX_COMMITS), "--format=%H%x00%B%x1e"], { encoding: "utf8", maxBuffer: 32 * 1024 * 1024 }). Argument array, no shell option (so no shell interpretation), fixed subcommand/flags; target is the user-supplied repo path. This is the tool's core function (reading git history). No other subprocess use in src/; exec( hits at src/core.ts:97,109 are RegExp matches. No eval / new Function.
  • Filesystem: No writes in src/ (grep-verified). Tests write git fixtures only under mkdtemp dirs and spawn the tool's own CLI (test/pipe.test.ts:20,29,40,72).
  • Hardcoded hosts (metadata only, never fetched): github.com (repo URL / OCI label, Dockerfile:22), static.modelcontextprotocol.io (server.json $schema), registry.npmjs.org (server.json registryBaseUrl).
  • CI note (not shipped code): .github/workflows/registry-publish.yml:18 downloads the official MCP registry publisher v1.8.1 tarball (curl -L https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/… | tar xz) in the author's publish workflow; publish.yml uses secrets.NPM_TOKEN in CI. Standard fleet template; not install/runtime behaviour.
  • Obfuscation / data collection: None. Plain readable TypeScript; no telemetry/analytics, no minified blobs.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN
docs.text: Local commit-message hygiene checker. Its only subprocess is a fixed, shell-free git log read of the user-supplied repository — exactly its job. No egress, no env/credential access, no install hooks, no writes in shipped source.

docs.title: Security Audit — depguard
docs.text:
• Repo / package: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/depguard — @reneturcios/depguard
  • Version (pin this): 0.4.0
  • Bin: dist/cli.js (CLI + stdio MCP server)
  • Dependencies: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3 (dev: @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5)
  • License: MIT
  • Method used: git clone and codeload tarballs failed on this VM (clone symref write error; tarballs 0 bytes through the proxy). Source was fetched file-by-file through the GitHub API contents endpoint via the GitHub MCP connector (get_file_contents, the same contents API gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/depguard/contents/<path> wraps), saved as raw API snapshots in src/depguard/rawsnap/, and audited in-memory with line-accurate scans; flagged lines were read in context.
  • Coverage: package.json, Dockerfile, server.json, and ALL of src/ (cli.ts, content.ts, core.ts, history.ts, index.ts, mcp.ts, popular.ts, registry.ts). No bin/ or scripts/ directory exists. test/ not line-audited — not shipped (files: dist, server.json).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: scripts are only build (tsc), dev, test. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare. (Fittingly, flagging other packages' install scripts is this tool's job.)
  • Network egress — opt-in only, two registry hosts: the core is offline. Online checks run only behind explicit flags (--online, --content parsed at src/cli.ts:84–96; registry.ts:1–6 header states "These run ONLY behind an explicit online flag"). Endpoints: https://registry.npmjs.org/<name> packuments (src/registry.ts:24, src/content.ts:44, src/history.ts:339) and https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json (src/history.ts:337–339). In content mode it also downloads both versions' tarballs from the packument's own dist.tarball URL (src/content.ts:48–55, byte-capped by MAX_TARBALL_BYTES) and extracts them in memory only (src/content.ts:60–63: "Extracts to an in-memory map only") for static diffing — downloaded code is never written to disk, installed, or executed. No tokens are sent (no auth headers; the tool reads no env vars at all).
  • Credential / env access: none. Zero process.env reads in the entire source; no token of any kind. The .ssh / .aws / process.env-secret hits at src/content.ts:113–123 and the RISKY_SCRIPT_RE at src/core.ts:427 are detection rules applied to scanned packages' files — data, not behavior.
  • child_process — one justified, safe use: execFileSync("git", ["-C", dir, "show",${ref}:${file}], …) at src/core.ts:408 inside loadSnapshotFromGit() — fixed binary, argv array, no shell, so the user-supplied --base <ref> cannot become shell injection. It reads dependency manifests at a git ref, which is the tool's stated function.
  • fs writes: none. No write/append/mkdir calls in src/.
  • eval / obfuscation: no eval, new Function, or vm; no long base64 blobs outside detection patterns. gunzipSync (src/content.ts:21) is used solely for the in-memory tarball reader above.
  • Other hosts in shipped files (metadata only): github.com, static.modelcontextprotocol.io, registry.npmjs.org (server.json/package.json).

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: Notes: (1) Egress to registry.npmjs.org and pypi.org occurs only in explicit --online / --content / history modes; tarballs are fetched from the registry packument's URL, size-capped, and parsed in memory — never installed or executed. (2) One child-process call: execFileSync("git", …) with a fixed binary and argv array at src/core.ts:408 to read manifests at a git ref — its stated job, no shell. (3) No env vars, tokens, or credential stores are read at all.

The two GITHUB_TOKEN hits are advisory prose about the workflows being audited: src/core.ts:567 (explaining that a missing top-level permissions: block leaves the default token permissive) and src/core.ts:742 (a note that a job which never uses the token can run with permissions: {}).
