docs.title: Security Audit — greenlight
docs.text:
• Repo / package: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/greenlight — @reneturcios/greenlight
  • Version (pin this): 0.25.0
  • Bin: dist/cli.js (one bin serves the CLI and the stdio MCP server, src/index.ts)
  • Dependencies: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^4.6.7 (dev: @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5)
  • License: MIT
  • Method used: git clone and codeload tarballs failed on this VM (clone symref write error; tarballs 0 bytes through the proxy). Source was fetched file-by-file through the GitHub API contents endpoint via the GitHub MCP connector (get_file_contents, the same contents API gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/greenlight/contents/<path> wraps), saved as raw API snapshots in src/greenlight/rawsnap/, and audited in-memory with line-accurate scans; every flagged area was read in context.
  • Coverage: package.json, Dockerfile, server.json, action.yml, .mcp.json, ALL 58 files of src/, ALL of scripts/ (llm-claim-smoke.mjs, sync-readme-test-count.sh, trust-index-dry-run.ts), and the shipped integrations/ tree (mcp.json read in full; claude-code/CLAUDE.snippet.md read in full; per-agent subdir listings taken). No bin/ directory exists. Not line-audited: test/, docs/, data/, examples/, protocol/, maintainer/, .github/ — none of these are in the npm package (files: dist, server.json, integrations), so they cannot affect an install.

docs.title: Install scripts
docs.text: package.json scripts: build (tsc), dev, index (tsx src/friction-index.ts — a maintainer script that regenerates the policy-index data file in the author's repo), test, readme:count (bash scripts/sync-readme-test-count.sh). No preinstall / postinstall / prepare — nothing runs at install time.

docs.title: Network egress (complete host list)
docs.text:
All GitHub API traffic goes through apiGet/apiPost in src/github.ts unless noted.

  1. api.github.com — the tool's primary API (issue/PR verdicts, claims, radar, digests). Default base is hardcoded (src/github.ts:19). Override via GREENLIGHT_GITHUB_BASE_URL passes through sanitizeApiBase() (src/github.ts:30–56): http/https only, embedded credentials, query strings and fragments stripped, invalid values fall back to the default.
  2. raw.githubusercontent.com — file-contents fetches (src/github.ts:20, and the best-effort cached contents path at src/github.ts:959).
  3. cloudcorprecords.github.io — the author's own public static files, GET-only, no token or auth headers sent: the Agent Policy Index at …/greenlight/policy.json (src/index-drift.ts:25–26, src/wave.ts:32, fetched at src/index-drift.ts:139 and cached to ~/.greenlight/policy-index-cache.json) and the public Claim Ledger JSONs (default base src/passport.ts:22, GETs at src/passport.ts:110,126; src/claim-import.ts:21).
  4. claim-api-wine.vercel.app — the author's hosted claim-API service, DEFAULT_API_BASE at src/claim-api.ts:39. Used only by the explicit --via-api surface: greenlight auth login, claim --via-api, release --via-api, heartbeat --via-api, and the MCP tools api_status / claim_via_api / heartbeat_via_api (module header, src/claim-api.ts:4–17). Calls are GET status/installation and POST /v1/claims, /v1/claims/release, /v1/claims/heartbeat carrying claim payloads (owner/repo/issue) with the user's token (src/claim-api.ts:586–624). Base resolution order is --api-base flag → GREENLIGHT_API_BASE env → config file → hosted default, and a flag/env-supplied base is cached into ~/.config/greenlight/config.json for later runs (src/claim-api.ts:78–107). If the hosted app path is unavailable it falls back to direct GitHub API comments with a printed notice (src/claim-api.ts:13–17).
  5. api.fireworks.ai — optional LLM claim classification. Enabled only when the user sets FIREWORKS_API_KEY (llmEnabled() is literally Boolean(env.FIREWORKS_API_KEY), src/llm-claims.ts:51–53). POSTs to {base}/chat/completions (src/llm-claims.ts:324); default base https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1 (src/llm-claims.ts:35), overridable via GREENLIGHT_LLM_BASE_URL, model via GREENLIGHT_LLM_MODEL. Data sent: GitHub issue comment bodies truncated to 2,000 chars, at most 25 per call (src/llm-claims.ts:38–41) — i.e., public issue text from repos the user is evaluating, sent to the user's own LLM account.
  6. github.com (OAuth device flow) — greenlight auth login runs GitHub's device flow (src/claim-api.ts:19–23, 46–47) with a baked-in OAuth client id Ov23liv9yM4RTci0UysE (src/claim-api.ts:45 — a public client identifier, not a secret; overridable via GREENLIGHT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID). Resulting scope is public_repo.
  7. 127.0.0.1 (inbound, the proxy subcommand) — a localhost forwarder that attaches the user's token server-side. It binds 127.0.0.1 only (src/proxy.ts:116), forwards to exactly one upstream, https://api.github.com (src/proxy.ts:24, 62–105), strips incoming Authorization headers and attaches only the startup token (src/proxy.ts:75–79); the token is read once from env and never logged or stored (src/proxy.ts:12–18).
  8. Hardening note (not a verdict changer): absolute-form request targets are rejected (src/proxy.ts:66–70), but a protocol-relative target (//other-host/…) is not explicitly rejected, and new URL(target, upstream) at src/proxy.ts:71 would resolve it cross-host — a local process could then use the proxy as a token oracle against another host. Exposure is localhost-only and the token still never leaves in cleartext to the caller, but the check should also reject targets starting with //.

Other hosts appearing in source are metadata or detection data only: github.com, static.modelcontextprotocol.io, registry.npmjs.org, registry.modelcontextprotocol.io (package/server metadata), nodejs.org and cla-assistant.io (help/detection text), api.github.com. (a trailing-dot string in a test-oriented constant). No telemetry / analytics / Sentry / PostHog / Mixpanel anywhere (grep-verified across all 58 src files).

docs.title: Credential / env access
docs.text:
Env keys read (complete list from scan): GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, FIREWORKS_API_KEY, GREENLIGHT_API_TOKEN, GREENLIGHT_API_BASE, GREENLIGHT_GITHUB_BASE_URL, GREENLIGHT_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, GREENLIGHT_LEDGER_URL, GREENLIGHT_LLM_BASE_URL, GREENLIGHT_LLM_MODEL, GREENLIGHT_AGENT_ID, GREENLIGHT_GITHUB_USER, GREENLIGHT_CLAIMS_FILE, GREENLIGHT_CAPABILITIES_PATH, GREENLIGHT_TRUST_FILE, GREENLIGHT_TRUST_MEMORY, GREENLIGHT_CLAIM_DAILY_CAP, GREENLIGHT_CLAIM_MIN_INTERVAL_S, GREENLIGHT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_S.

  • GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN are read at src/github.ts:162–164 and sent only as a Bearer header to the (sanitized) GitHub API base. A GitHub contribution tool reading the standard GitHub token env vars is justified.
  • Token storage (the user's own token, from auth login): OS keychain first — macOS security and Linux secret-tool via fixed-binary execFile/spawn with argv arrays, the token passed over stdin on store (src/claim-api.ts:187–225) — falling back to ~/.greenlight/api-token written with mode 0o600 plus an explicit chmodSync 0600 (src/claim-api.ts:227–247, store selection at 287–295). GREENLIGHT_API_TOKEN / --token are passthrough alternatives (src/claim-api.ts:309–324). In two claim paths the resolved token is temporarily assigned into process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN in-process and restored/deleted afterwards (src/claim-api.ts:1011–1023, 1137–1143).
  • Not touched: no access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gnupg, .git-credentials, browser profiles, or any other application's credentials anywhere in src/ (grep-verified). The only keychain interaction is greenlight storing/retrieving its own token.

docs.title: Code execution
docs.text:
• No eval, new Function, or vm anywhere. Base64 use is decoding GitHub API content payloads (src/github.ts:661, src/guard.ts:744, src/protocol-fetch.ts:168, src/automate.ts:159). No remote code is ever downloaded and executed; no curl|sh.
  • child_process, all accounted for:
  • Fixed-binary git with argv arrays, no shell: src/autopilot-fixes.ts:191, src/ci-prep.ts:474, src/verify.ts:57, plus the keychain helpers above.
  • sh -c in exactly two user-invoked features whose purpose is running the target repo's own commands locally: ci-prep executes the repo's CI step scripts via spawnSync("sh", ["-c", script]) (src/ci-prep.ts:451, env {...process.env, CI: "true"} at :456) and probes for act/docker (src/ci-prep.ts:624–643); verify runs the repo's test command the same way (src/verify.ts:131). The scripts executed come from the repo the user points the tool at — the same trust decision as running npm test in that repo — never from the network.
  • action.yml (the repo's GitHub Action form) only reads its own greenlight-guard.json report with node -e one-liners (action.yml:50, 55, 87).

docs.title: fs writes (all feature-scoped)
docs.text:
• ~/.greenlight/ — the tool's own state: autopilot.json / autopilot-replies.json (src/autopilot.ts:129–133, 187–188, 1038–1039), babysit.json (src/babysit.ts:248, 265), my-claims.json (src/claims-registry.ts:66, 89), capabilities.json (src/capabilities.ts:55, 87), trust.json (src/trust.ts:336, 173), posting-ledger.json (src/posting-ledger.ts:80, 174, 408), api-token (above), policy-index cache.
  • ~/.cache/greenlight/ — best-effort API response cache (src/github.ts:57, cacheSet at :100–106) and the doctor write-probe (src/doctor.ts:54, 106).
  • ~/.config/greenlight/config.json — the cached claim-API base (above).
  • In the user's project: PREP.md prep files (src/automate.ts:885–886), evidence-pack markdown to a user-named output file (src/cli.ts:1634), scout campaign files (src/scout.ts:85), and greenlight init copying agent configs (src/init.ts:178) from the shipped integrations/ snippets.
  • Temp work dirs (mkdtempSync) for autopilot fix application (src/autopilot.ts:68, writes at :882, 894) and verify (src/verify.ts:17).
  • Nothing writes outside the user's home, their project, or temp dirs. The posting ledger stamps entries with GREENLIGHT_AGENT_ID or "<hostname>:<pid>" (src/posting-ledger.ts:68–72) — recorded in that local ledger file.

docs.title: Shipped integrations/
docs.text: integrations/mcp.json and each per-agent .mcp.json are the same 100-byte config registering npx -y @reneturcios/greenlight@0.25.0 mcp — the tool itself. integrations/claude-code/CLAUDE.snippet.md (read in full) is workflow guidance for the user's agent that explicitly requires the human's explicit go-ahead before posting anything to GitHub.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text:
This is a large GitHub contribution tool and its surface matches its stated job; nothing malicious, spying, or unjustified was found. The notes an installer should know:

  1. Hosted claim API: claim/release/heartbeat --via-api and auth login talk to the author's hosted service at claim-api-wine.vercel.app by default (src/claim-api.ts:39), sending claim payloads and the user's token; a custom --api-base/GREENLIGHT_API_BASE is silently cached to ~/.config/greenlight/config.json (src/claim-api.ts:78–107).
  2. Token custody: with auth login, the user's GitHub token (public_repo scope, device flow, client id at src/claim-api.ts:45) is stored in the OS keychain, or in ~/.greenlight/api-token at mode 0600 when no keychain exists (src/claim-api.ts:227–295). Day-to-day operation uses GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN from env (src/github.ts:162–164).
  3. Opt-in LLM egress: only if FIREWORKS_API_KEY is set, issue comment bodies (≤2,000 chars each, ≤25/call) are sent to api.fireworks.ai for claim classification (src/llm-claims.ts:35, 51–53, 324).
  4. Author-hosted public data: the policy index and claim ledger are fetched GET-only, with no token, from cloudcorprecords.github.io (src/index-drift.ts:25–26, src/passport.ts:22).
  5. Local execution features: ci-prep and verify run the target repo's own CI/test commands via sh -c (src/ci-prep.ts:451, src/verify.ts:131) — do not run them against untrusted repos. All other subprocess use is fixed-binary git/keychain tools with argv arrays.
  6. Proxy subcommand: binds 127.0.0.1 only and forwards only to api.github.com (src/proxy.ts:24, 116); minor hardening gap — protocol-relative (//host) targets are not rejected alongside absolute-form ones (src/proxy.ts:66–71).
  7. State writes are confined to ~/.greenlight/, ~/.cache/greenlight/, ~/.config/greenlight/, temp dirs, and user-named/project files (PREP.md, evidence packs, init agent configs).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: scripts are only build (tsc), dev, test. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Network egress: none in the tool's own code. Imports are only node:fs (read-only: existsSync, lstatSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, statSync — src/core.ts:7), node:path, MCP SDK (stdio), zod. Its README claim "no network in the core scan" matches the source.

The only process.env hits are comments describing shapes it detects in scanned code: src/core.ts:1113 (process.env.NODE_ENV given as a non-flagged example), src/core.ts:1200–1201 (env-dump shapes), src/core.ts:1311 (process.env.SECRET in a comment about print disclosure). The tool itself reads no environment variables.
  • Flagged-but-benign (detection DATA, read in context): hookcheck is a hook/persistence auditor, so src/core.ts is full of attack-pattern data: exec-call name list at core.ts:345, curl-pipe-shell rule at core.ts:34, credential-path patterns (~/.ssh, .aws/credentials, .gnupg) at core.ts:956–965, .npmrc write detection at core.ts:1049–1071, fetch/eval flow analysis at core.ts:2394–2532. All are patterns/classifiers applied to scanned repos — the tool never performs these actions.

  • Obfuscation: none; no long base64 blobs outside detection patterns.

  • Hosts in shipped files: github.com, static.modelcontextprotocol.io, registry.npmjs.org (all metadata in package.json/server.json/Dockerfile label); pyenv.run at src/core.ts:2794 is an entry in a KNOWN_INSTALLER_HOSTS allowlist (data — the documented pyenv installer endpoint, core.ts:2800–2803), never contacted.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN

docs.title: Audit — imageport (@reneturcios/imageport)
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/imageport (MIT)
  • Version: 0.1.0 (package.json, VERSION in src/imageport.ts, server.json 0.1.0)
  • Method: git clone is broken VM-wide (unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy. Primary method used: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/imageport/contents/<path> (base64 content, decoded) and gh api …/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file listing; the executor evidence lines were re-verified through this route and match. Core src/imageport.ts also read in full via supplementary raw.githubusercontent.com fetches with identical content/line numbers. src/imageport/package.json persisted under src/ via the file-write tool.
  • Files read: package.json, README.md, Dockerfile, server.json, src/imageport.ts, src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/types.ts, src/index.ts.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: none in package.json (scripts: build/dev/test only). Lockfile hasInstallScript only on dev-only esbuild/fsevents. Runtime deps: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3 only.
  • Network egress: none. No fetch/http/net imports, no URLs in code (Dockerfile label aside). README's "no network call anywhere in this package" is accurate against the source.
  • Credential/env access: none. process.env does not appear in src/.
  • Process execution — its job, done safely: src/imageport.ts:15,42 — one default executor, execFile(command, args, {timeout: 120000, maxBuffer: 16MB}), argument arrays, no shell. All call sites use the literals "identify" / "convert" with fixed arrays:
  • metadata: identify -format "%m|%w|%h|%[colorspace]|%b" <input> (:68)
  • resize: convert <input> -resize <geometry> <output> (:105)
  • convert: convert <input> <effectiveOutput> (:134)
  • crop: convert <input> -crop <WxH+X+Y> +repage <output> (:152)
  • rotate: convert <input> -rotate <angle> <output> (:164) User values enter as single array elements / validated numbers formatted into the geometry string — there is no command-line string for a shell to reinterpret, and no ImageMagick policy/script execution is invoked. Missing binaries surface as honest ENOENT errors.
  • eval / new Function: none.
  • fs writes: none by the package itself; ImageMagick writes caller-specified output paths.
  • Telemetry / data collection: none.
  • Obfuscation: none.
  • Dockerfile: two-stage node:20-alpine, npm ci, USER node; bundles no ImageMagick. No curl|sh.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN
docs.text: No egress, no env/credential access, no shell, no install scripts. The only execution surface is arg-array execFile of the host's ImageMagick convert/identify, which is the package's stated job.

Audit was done by downloading the codeload tarball of main in-memory (Python urllib), scanning every file, and reading src/probe.ts, src/cli.ts etc. in full from memory. No install, no execution of the tool.
  • Stated job: Audit any MCP server: handshake, tool schemas, missing descriptions, error handling — by actually launching the server under test over stdio.

docs.title: Install scripts — none
docs.text: package.json scripts are only build (tsc), dev, test. No preinstall/postinstall/prepare.

docs.title: Network egress — none
docs.text: Zero network code in src/: no fetch, http/https/net/tls, WebSocket, axios, or undici anywhere in src. Remote (HTTP) MCP targets are explicitly refused, not contacted: src/probe.ts:103-107 + remoteUnsupportedError() at src/probe.ts:73-75. Hosts appearing elsewhere are docs/schema identifiers only (github.com, registry.npmjs.org in publish config, static.modelcontextprotocol.io schema URL in server.json, mcp.context7.com / mcp.deepwiki.com as README examples). No telemetry/analytics of any kind.

docs.title: Code execution — spawning the target server is the stated job, and only that
docs.text:
• src/probe.ts:113-119 launches the user-specified server command via the SDK's StdioClientTransport (command + args + cwd exactly as given via CLI args, --config file, --cmdline, or the MCP tool — src/cli.ts:5-9,58-60, src/mcp.ts). It then does initialize, tools/list, prompts/resources counts, one deliberately-bad tools/call (src/probe.ts:216-243, name mcpaudit_nonexistent_tool_zz9), and a liveness ping.
  • No eval / new Function / vm / direct child_process in src; no downloading of code; nothing remote is executed. This is exactly the exception the audit brief grants mcpaudit.

docs.title: Env access — full host env is passed TO the audited server (note)
docs.text:
• src/probe.ts:109-111: the probe builds the child environment by copying every process.env entry, then overlaying user-supplied target.env (src/mcp.ts:26: optional env record param, "Extra environment variables for the server process"; also settable via the audited config file).
  • This env goes only to the locally spawned target process (the SDK transport requires an explicit env map; an MCP client normally inherits env for the server it launches, and servers commonly need API keys this way). mcpaudit itself sends nothing anywhere — it has no network code (above) and no fs writes in src (below).
  • Practical implication, worth a note rather than a rejection: the server being audited receives your full environment (including any API keys in it), because mcpaudit launches it the way a real MCP client would. Audit untrusted servers from a scrubbed environment.

docs.title: fs writes — none in src
docs.text: No writeFile/appendFile/createWriteStream/rm/unlink in src/. Reads: user-specified config/tools-dump files (src/cli.ts:13 readFile). All writes in the repo are in tests creating fixture servers/temp dirs. No base64 blobs ≥200 chars, no obfuscation; sources are plain readable TypeScript.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text:
• Spawning the target MCP server is its stated job; it executes only the exact local command the user supplies, never remote/downloaded code, and refuses HTTP targets.
  • It copies the full host process.env into that target server's environment (src/probe.ts:109-111) — local client-style inheritance needed to launch real servers, not exfiltration (mcpaudit has zero network egress and zero fs writes), but run it against untrusted servers with a scrubbed env.

docs.text:

  • gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/mcpaudit/contents/<path> (base64) — fetched and scanned: package.json, all of src/ (audit, cli, index, mcp, probe, types), server.json, Dockerfile — 9 files. Every contents-API blob SHA matched the tree-listing SHA.
  • Coverage note: no bin/ or scripts/ directory exists in this repo — bin entry dist/cli.js is built from src/cli.ts. Tests/fixtures/docs/workflows/package-lock were covered by the earlier full-tree in-memory scan. The gh-api re-scan reproduced identical findings (NET: 0; ENV: only src/probe.ts:110; EXEC: StdioClientTransport at src/probe.ts:16,113; EVAL/FSWRITE: 0). Verdict unchanged.

docs.title: Audit — mcpvet (@reneturcios/mcpvet)
docs.text:

No preinstall/postinstall/prepare/prepublish. scripts/copy-assets.mjs:8 (build-time only) copies the bundled src/fingerprints.json into dist/. scripts/gen-seeds.ts:61 is a maintainer seed generator that writes a fingerprints JSON in the repo — not shipped (scripts/ not in files), not run at install or runtime.

docs.title: Network egress — one justified host
docs.text:
• src/vet.ts:1045-1046 — vetPackage() does GET https://registry.npmjs.org/<name> with header Accept: application/json only. No auth, no request body, no other data sent. This is the vet-package command / vet_package MCP tool: registry metadata only, tarball never downloaded (also stated in src/mcp.ts:26 and CHANGELOG). Called from src/cli.ts:81 and src/mcp.ts:31 with the global fetch injected.

Remaining hosts in the repo are documentation/badges (github.com, img.shields.io, www.npmjs.com), the server.json schema URL (static.modelcontextprotocol.io, a schema identifier string, not fetched), and *.example.invalid in test fixtures / detection examples.
  • No telemetry/analytics/sentry/posthog/mixpanel anywhere in src. src/known.ts:25,41 contain the strings "server-sentry"/"sentry" — entries in a list of well-known MCP package names used for typosquat distance, i.e. DATA.

docs.title: Credential / env / secret access — none by the tool itself
docs.text:
• src/ reads no process.env keys at all (the only env reads in the repo are in test fixtures: test/fixtures/live/drifting-server.mjs:13,27 reads its own FIXTURE_STATE/DRIFT_MODE).
  • All credential-shaped strings in src/vet.ts and src/known.ts are detection rules (DATA) the scanner applies to target code, e.g. src/known.ts:47 (env-var-name regex), src/known.ts:51 (credential-file-path regex: .ssh, id_rsa, .aws/credentials, .git-credentials, .npmrc…), src/vet.ts:149-175 (network/shell/env capability patterns, DESC-EXFIL pattern), src/vet.ts:280,364,394-419,464-469 (curl|sh and reverse-shell shape detection). mcpvet never opens those paths itself.
  • Test fixtures that do touch credentials are inert test DATA, not shipped: test/fixtures/evil-skill/scripts/helper.sh:3 (cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa — the malicious sample the scanner must catch), test/fixtures/env-harvest-server/claude_desktop_config.json:10-13 (synthetic sk-*/ghp_synthetic placeholder values).

docs.title: Code execution — opt-in live probe of a user-supplied command (its stated live mode)
docs.text:
• Static vetting never executes target code: src/vet.ts:9,71-124 uses only readdirSync/statSync/lstatSync/readFileSync on the user-specified path; src has no fs writes at all.
  • Live mode is separate and opt-in per invocation: mcpvet probe -- <command> [args...] (src/cli.ts:83-100) and the probe_server MCP tool (src/mcp.ts:36-48) spawn the user-supplied local command twice via the SDK's StdioClientTransport (src/probe.ts:49-55), run initialize + tools/list, and diff the two answers. It does not download or execute remote code; the command is exactly what the user typed. The execution is loudly documented in-code (src/live.ts:69: "Live mode EXECUTES the server command (twice…)") and in the README.
  • No eval, new Function, vm, or child_process anywhere in src/ (spawn is via the MCP SDK transport). No curl|sh in src (only as detection regexes, above).

docs.title: Obfuscation — none
docs.text: No base64 strings ≥200 chars anywhere in the repo; src/fingerprints.json is 1,332 bytes of readable JSON; all sources are plain readable TypeScript.

docs.title: CI workflow note (not shipped, not runtime)
docs.text: .github/workflows/registry-publish.yml:22 downloads the official MCP Registry mcp-publisher binary (curl -L https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/download/v1.8.1/… | tar xz) in the maintainer's publish CI only. Not part of the npm package, not run on install or by the tool. Dockerfile is a standard multi-stage npm ci + build with ENTRYPOINT ["node","/app/dist/cli.js"].

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text:
1. Only runtime egress is GET registry.npmjs.org/<package> (metadata, no auth/body) in vet-package — required by its stated job of vetting an npm package before install.
  2. The opt-in probe/probe_server live mode executes a user-supplied local server command twice (SDK stdio transport) — that is its documented live-probe job, equivalent in kind to mcpaudit's stated job; it never fetches or runs remote/downloaded code. Do not point it at a server you would not run anyway. Everything else flagged by pattern scans is detection-rule data or inert test fixtures.

  • gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/mcpvet/contents/<path> (base64) — fetched and scanned: package.json, all of src/ (cli, fingerprints.json/ts, index, known, live, mcp, probe, signals, types, vet), all of scripts/ (copy-assets.mjs, gen-seeds.ts), server.json, Dockerfile — 16 files. Every contents-API blob SHA matched the tree-listing SHA (no mismatches).
  • Coverage note: there is no bin/ directory in the repo — the bin entry dist/cli.js is built from src/cli.ts by the build script. Remaining tree entries (tests, fixtures, README/CHANGELOG, workflows, package-lock) were covered by the earlier full-tree in-memory scan; the gh-api re-scan of all executable source reproduced identical findings (NET: only detection-rule regex at src/vet.ts:149 in the fetched set plus the already-read vet.ts:1045-1046 registry GET; ENV: 0; EXEC: StdioClientTransport at src/probe.ts:14,49; FSWRITE: scripts/gen-seeds.ts only). docs.title: Security Audit — muse-farm
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/muse-farm (MIT)
  • Version: 0.5.1 (farm.py:23 __version__ = "0.5.1")
  • Packaging / bin: None. No pyproject.toml, setup.py, package.json, or console entry point — the entire tool is one stdlib-only Python file, farm.py (57,594 bytes), invoked as python3 farm.py <run|batch|schedule|init|supervise|think|adopt|status|self-update>. Python 3.9+, zero third-party dependencies (imports: argparse, concurrent.futures, json, os, re, shlex, subprocess, sys, time, datetime; urllib.request imported lazily in two functions).
  • Method used: git clone is broken VM-wide (“unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted”) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, and tar extraction into the scratch tree hit write-EPERM — so no local src/ copy could be persisted. Primary method per coordinator: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/muse-farm/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file inventory and gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/muse-farm/contents/<path> (base64 content) for source, cross-checked with streamed raw.githubusercontent.com reads: full read of all of farm.py in four chunks, plus grep -n scans of the files listed under Coverage. Nothing was installed or run.
  • Coverage: Complete — this repo has only 8 files and all were covered: farm.py (the entire tool, read in full), tests/test_farm.py, jobs.example.json, supervise.example.json, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE, .gitignore. There is no src/ dir, no package.json/pyproject.toml, and no .github/ workflows in this repo.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install hooks: None possible — there is no packaging metadata at all. Nothing runs on download/clone.
  • Core execution (its job, as expected): build_exec_cmd() builds an argv list [muse, exec, …flags…, prompt]; cmd_run / cmd_batch run it with subprocess.run(cmd) in argv form. Grep confirms no shell=True anywhere, no eval/exec() of strings, no os.system. --yolo and --trust-workspace are passed through only when the user sets them (CLI flag or jobs-file entry). batch reads a user-supplied jobs JSON and writes one log per job under the runs dir. init runs [muse, init] in the user-named workspace and writes an AGENTS.md stub there if absent.
  • Scheduling / persistence (opt-in): schedule only prints cron/launchd entries by default. With explicit --install it writes a plist to ~/Library/LaunchAgents (farm.py:302) and runs launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>. The baked-in scheduled PATH is ~/.local/bin + system dirs (farm.py:210).
  • supervise / adopt — local access BEYOND spawning muse exec (flagged per audit brief):
  • Reads the user's Muse session data under SESSIONS_ROOT = ~/.local/share/muse/sessions (farm.py:359): session-log (session.jsonl) tails (128 KB default, widening up to the whole file in _scan_mission) to reconstruct each session's mission from runtime.user_intent.accepted text (_mission_from_records), and session tool-outputs/ files (up to 300 files × 32 KB, _collect_mention_text) to infer the session's workspace from path mentions (_inferred_workspace).
  • Inspects processes: ps -eo pid=,args= + lsof to map live muse-bin PIDs → sessions and their working directories (_live_session_pids, _session_cwds, _ps_usage).
  • Acts on stalls by sending nudges via muse session-message send (_send_nudge) and, when the supervise config provides workspace+mission, spawning headless continuations (_continue_exec: muse exec with trust_workspace forced True, yolo from per-session config, capped by max_continues_per_day, default 6). It never kills a process — grep confirms no os.kill / signal use.
  • Writes only supervisor bookkeeping in --state-dir (default <farm>/runs/supervise): state.json, status.json, supervisor.log, continue-<uuid>-<ts>.log.
  • All of the above stays on the local machine except through the two opt-in channels below.
  • Network egress — only two paths, both user-configured:
  • ntfy notifications. _ntfy() (farm.py:547-551) POSTs via urllib.request to {url}/{topic}. Default URL is hardcoded https://ntfy.sh (farm.py:966, overridable in config); the topic has no default — it comes only from --ntfy-topic or the user's supervise config, so no ntfy call happens without user configuration. Bodies sent are minimal metadata only: session <uuid-prefix> is gone and session <uuid-prefix> idle <age> (stall #n), with a Title header. No mission text, no log content, no credentials.
  • think --backend api. _think_via_api() (farm.py:872-880) POSTs {api_base}/chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible) via urllib.request. api_base is user-supplied (config/CLI; the README's https://api.fireworks.ai/inference/v1 is a documentation example only). In supervise mode the prompt sent to that endpoint can include the session's mission text, its done_when, and continuation-log excerpts (≤1,500 chars in the verdict prompt) — i.e. local session-derived content leaves the machine only to the endpoint the user configured. The default think backend is muse (via muse exec, no API call).
  • Credential / env access: Exactly one read: farm.py:869 os.environ.get(key_env) in _think_via_api, where key_env is the name of an env var chosen by the user, defaulting to MUSE_FARM_API_KEY (farm.py:897, :1351); the key is sent as Authorization: Bearer … only to the user-configured api_base. (Deliberate design: --api-key-env help says “never pass the key itself”.) No other os.environ access; no ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, Keychain, or browser-profile access.
  • Self-update (user-invoked remote-code path): cmd_self_update refuses non-git checkouts and dirty trees, then runs git pull --ff-only in the farm checkout (farm.py:1267) and executes the pulled tree's test suite (python -m unittest discover -s tests). This downloads new code from the checkout's git remote and runs part of it — only when the user explicitly runs farm.py self-update. There is no auto-update on any other path.
  • Obfuscation / data collection: None. One plain, heavily commented Python file; no telemetry/analytics; the only hardcoded third-party host is the ntfy.sh default above (plus the Apple plist DTD string at farm.py:224, a template literal that is never fetched).

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: Nothing malicious or covert: no shell execution, no process killing, no credential stores, no author telemetry, and every network destination is user-configured except the ntfy.sh default host. The notes that must travel with any install decision are the breadth of its local remit, all of it the documented supervisor job but beyond “wraps muse exec”: it reads Muse session logs and tool-output files under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions, inspects ps/lsof, can install launchd persistence (schedule --install), can send stall metadata to ntfy.sh once the user sets a topic, can send mission/log-derived prompts to a user-configured OpenAI-compatible API with a key from MUSE_FARM_API_KEY (or a user-named env var), passes through --yolo / --trust-workspace, and its self-update pulls and test-executes remote code on explicit invocation.

docs.title: Security Audit — muse-marketplace
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/muse-marketplace (MIT)
  • Version: 0.1.0 (package.json)
  • npm: @reneturcios/muse-marketplace · Bins: muse-marketplace and mmkt → dist/cli.js
  • Dependencies: runtime @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3; dev @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5
  • Method used: git clone is broken VM-wide (“unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted”) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, and tar extraction into the scratch tree hit write-EPERM — so no local src/ copy could be persisted. Primary method per coordinator: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/muse-marketplace/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file inventory and gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/muse-marketplace/contents/<path> (base64 content) for source, cross-checked with streamed raw.githubusercontent.com reads: full-file reads of package.json, src/cli.ts, src/registry.ts (all but the scaffold tail), and grep -n scans of the remaining files listed under Coverage. Nothing was installed or run.
  • Coverage: All executable source covered — package.json, every file in src/ (cli.ts, index.ts, mcp.ts, registry.ts, types.ts), plus test/*.ts, site/app.js, site/index.html, Dockerfile, server.json, workflows. The registry/** asset tree (SVG assets, listing.json/bundle.json/index.json, persona markdown) and docs/ were covered by full tree inventory + type/size review, not by downloading every asset file — none of them are executable formats, and the registry code rejects executable extensions at validate/install time (see Findings).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install hooks: Scripts are build, dev, test only. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Network egress: none. Grep across all of src/ finds no fetch, no http/https/net/tls, no WebSocket, no child_process, no eval / new Function. The MCP mode is stdio-only. Despite the “marketplace” name, installing a listing downloads nothing (see below).
  • Env access: exactly one variable. src/registry.ts:32 — process.env.MUSE_MARKETPLACE_REGISTRY, a path override for where the registry directory lives (also settable via --root). No other process.env in src/; no credential stores, tokens, ~/.ssh / ~/.aws / Keychain access.
  • What “install” actually does — verified local copy with strong vetting (src/registry.ts installListing()):
  • The registry is the bundled local registry/ tree (or the MUSE_MARKETPLACE_REGISTRY / --root directory). Install is copyFileSync from that local tree to a caller-provided destination (CLI default ./muse-assets, --dest to override); the destination is checked to stay under the provided base dir.
  • Before copying, the listing must pass validateListing(): every file's byte size and sha256 must match listing.json, media types must be on an allowlist (image/*, text/markdown, text/plain, application/json, audio/*), and a blocked-extensions denylist rejects executables and code (.exe .dll .so .sh .bat .ps1 .js .mjs .ts .py .rb .php .jar .msi .bin .run, …). Path-traversal paths (.., absolute, drive-letter) are rejected and each file must resolve inside its listing dir.
  • sha256 is re-verified after the copy, and an install-receipt.json is written into the destination. Invalid/tampered listings are refused.
  • Consistent with that, the bundled registry content is inert: SVG avatar assets, listing.json / bundle.json / index.json, and markdown personas — no executable assets in the tree (per the gh api inventory).
  • Other filesystem writes: rebuilding registry/index.json (index command, src/registry.ts writeIndex), and init scaffolding a new listing (placeholder SVG + listing.json) inside the registry dir. Nothing outside the registry dir / install dest.
  • Static site: site/app.js:111 fetch("data.json") — a same-directory relative fetch of the bundled catalog data for the preview site; innerHTML rendering there uses that bundled local data only.
  • Metadata / CI: server.json carries static.modelcontextprotocol.io (schema), registry.npmjs.org (registryBaseUrl), ghcr.io/cloudcorprecords/muse-marketplace:0.1.0 and github.com manifest strings — never fetched by the tool. Dockerfile is the standard node:20-alpine build. Workflows are the fleet template (registry-publish.yml CI-only curl of mcp-publisher v1.8.1; publish.yml uses secrets.NPM_TOKEN in CI).
  • Obfuscation / data collection: None. Plain readable TypeScript; no telemetry/analytics.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: The single note: it reads one environment variable, MUSE_MARKETPLACE_REGISTRY (src/registry.ts:32), solely as a registry-path override. Everything else is negative in the best way: zero network egress, zero subprocesses, zero credential access, and its install path is a checksum-verified, extension-denylisted local copy of inert media/markdown assets — it cannot fetch or install remote code.

docs.title: Security Audit — prodforge
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/prodforge (MIT)
  • Version: 0.5.0 (package.json, also VERSION in src/cli.ts)
  • npm: @reneturcios/prodforge · Bin: prodforge → dist/cli.js
  • Dependencies: runtime @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3; dev @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5
  • Method used: git clone is broken VM-wide (“unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted”) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, and tar extraction into the scratch tree hit write-EPERM — so no local src/ copy could be persisted. Primary method per coordinator: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/prodforge/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for the file inventory and gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/prodforge/contents/<path> (base64 content) for source, cross-checked with streamed raw.githubusercontent.com reads: full-file reads of package.json and every src/*.ts, and grep -n scans of the remaining files listed under Coverage. Nothing was installed or run.
  • Coverage: All executable source covered — package.json, every file in src/ (catalog.ts, cli.ts, doctor.ts, index.ts, mcp.ts, scaffolds.ts, ship.ts), plus test/*.ts, examples/notes/src/index.ts, examples/taskboard/src/index.ts + example package.jsons, catalog/registry.json, catalog/mcp-servers.json (registry inventoried/scanned), mcp/mcp.json, Dockerfile, server.json, workflows. docs/, playbooks/, stacks/ are markdown (inventoried, not code).

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install hooks: Scripts are build, dev, test only. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Network egress: none in prodforge's own code. Grep across all of src/ finds no fetch, no http/https/net/tls imports, no WebSocket, no hardcoded URLs. The catalog is bundled local JSON, read from disk (src/catalog.ts loadCatalog() / loadMcpServers() via readFileSync of catalog/registry.json / catalog/mcp-servers.json). Catalog data itself lists 27 fleet tools — every repo is https://github.com/CloudCorpRecords/<tool> and every npm is @reneturcios/<tool> (one GHCR-only, npm: null). Data only; prodforge fetches none of it.
  • The fleet-install question (explicitly judged): prodforge does not download packages, fetch package metadata/tarballs, run npm install, or execute anything it downloads — because it downloads nothing.
  • src/catalog.ts mcpConfigFor() only generates config text: { command: "npx", args: ["-y", <npm pkg>, "mcp"] } per MCP tool. prodforge connect prints it or writes it to a user-named --write path (src/cli.ts); the MCP connect_config tool returns it as text. Downstream caveat: if the user loads that generated config into an MCP client, the client will npx -y download and run those fleet packages (including any install scripts they carry). That is prodforge's stated fleet-wiring purpose, executed by the client at the user's direction — it is not behaviour of prodforge itself, and each fleet package needs its own audit (the other batches).
  • prodforge ship executes only already-installed local binaries (see below); absent tools are reported ABSENT, never fetched.
  • Code execution — fixed local invocations, no shell:
  • src/ship.ts runGate(): spawnSync(gate.bin, gate.args, { cwd, timeout: 60000, env: { ...process.env, PATH: pathValue } }) — gate bins/args are a hardcoded table of read-only fleet checks (agentsfile check ., envdoc check ., mcpvet vet ., actionpin audit ., flowcheck audit ., depguard check ., shipcheck check <owner/repo>); bins not on PATH are skipped as ABSENT. Note: children inherit the full process.env (standard spawn inheritance) — the fleet tools it runs receive the user's environment.
  • src/ship.ts resolveShipcheckSlug(): spawnSync("git", ["config", "--get", "remote.origin.url"], …) — reads the local git remote to derive owner/repo; no network.
  • src/doctor.ts run(): execSync of fixed literal strings only — node --version, npm --version, git --version, docker --version, git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree. No user input is interpolated. Doctor checks only the existence of .env.example / .env.sample; it never reads a real .env.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: none. package.json scripts are only build (tsc), dev, test. No preinstall/postinstall/prepare. package-lock.json hasInstallScript appears only on dev-only esbuild 0.28.2 and fsevents 2.3.3 (via tsx, "dev": true) — standard build tooling, not runtime deps. Runtime deps are only @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1 and zod ^3.
  • Network egress — exactly one channel: src/blender.ts:31,56 createConnection({host, port}) from node:net, one TCP socket per command, JSON {type, params} to the Blender addon. Default localhost:9876. That is the documented, expected channel.
  • Host/port are user-configurable via env (below), so the socket can point at a non-localhost Blender (the test at test/blender.test.ts:25 uses 192.168.1.5:9999). It goes only where the operator's env says.
  • No HTTP client anywhere: no fetch, no http/https imports, no URLs in code except the Dockerfile OCI label. PolyHaven (get_polyhaven_categories, search_polyhaven_assets, download_polyhaven_asset) and Hunyuan3D (generate_hunyuan3d_model) are not called by this package — the command names are forwarded over the Blender socket and the Blender addon performs any PolyHaven/Hunyuan traffic. scenemodel itself holds no PolyHaven/Hunyuan endpoint, key, or egress for them.

  • Code execution — by design, noted per brief: executeBlenderCode (src/blender.ts, execute_code command) sends caller-supplied Python over the local Blender socket to be executed inside Blender. docs.text:

  • Dependencies: runtime @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^4; dev @types/node ^20, tsx ^4, typescript ^5

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install hooks: Scripts are build, dev, test only. No preinstall / postinstall / prepare.
  • Network egress in specforge's own code: none directly. No fetch, http/https/net/tls, or WebSocket anywhere in src/ (grep-verified). MCP mode is stdio-only (src/mcp.ts registers the spec/git/quality tools over StdioServerTransport). Indirect egress via the quality tools is itemised below.
  • Env access: exactly one variable. SPECFORGE_ROOT — src/specforge.ts ROOT_ENV / resolveRoot() (src/specforge.ts:47; call sites src/cli.ts:123, src/mcp.ts:305). It only sets the workspace root path (default: CWD). No other process.env reads in src/; no credential stores, tokens, ~/.ssh / ~/.aws / Keychain access.
  • Filesystem writes — confined to the specs tree: all writeFile/appendFile hits (src/specforge.ts:183-525) write inside <root>/specs/<NNN>-<slug>/: spec.md, research.md, constitution.md, plan.md, tasks.md, clarifications.json (+ a contracts/ dir). That is the tool's stated function.
  • Code execution — fixed command table through a shell-free executor: src/specforge.ts:659 defaultExecutor is execFile(command, args, { cwd }, …) — no shell. The only commands ever passed to it are hardcoded in the same file (end of src/specforge.ts):
  • git checkout -b <branch> (gitCreateBranch; branch name validated: non-empty, no whitespace),
  • npx prettier --check . or, with fix, --write (qualityFormat),
  • npx eslint . [--fix] (qualityLint),
  • npm test [-- --coverage] (qualityTest),
  • npm audit [fix] (qualitySecurityAudit). No arbitrary command string from user input, spec files, or config is ever executed; the Executor is injectable only programmatically (tests inject fakes).
  • Consequences of those fixed commands (the notes):
  • npx prettier / npx eslint will download those packages from registry.npmjs.org and run them if they are not already in the target project's node_modules — network egress + execution of downloaded (mainstream, but downloaded) code, triggered only by explicitly invoking the quality_format / quality_lint tools.
  • npm audit sends the project's dependency names/versions to registry.npmjs.org (standard npm audit behaviour), and with fix: true, npm audit fix modifies package.json / lockfile / node_modules. Likewise prettier --write and eslint --fix mutate project files. All fix modes are explicit caller options, not defaults.
  • Metadata / CI: server.json carries static.modelcontextprotocol.io (schema), registry.npmjs.org (registryBaseUrl), ghcr.io image id, github.com repo strings — manifest metadata, not fetched by the tool. Dockerfile is a plain multi-stage node:20-alpine build (npm ci --no-audit --no-fund, no curl). Workflows are the fleet template (registry-publish.yml:17 CI-only curl of mcp-publisher v1.8.1; publish.yml uses secrets.NPM_TOKEN in CI).
  • Obfuscation / data collection: None. Plain readable TypeScript; no telemetry/analytics, no minified blobs.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: Notes: (1) env access is limited to SPECFORGE_ROOT (workspace path); (2) its quality/git tools run a fixed, shell-free command table (git checkout -b, npx prettier, npx eslint, npm test, npm audit) in the target project — of which npx can download and run prettier/eslint from registry.npmjs.org when absent locally, npm audit reports the dependency list to the npm registry, and the opt-in fix modes mutate project files/dependencies.   • Files read: package.json, README.md, Dockerfile, server.json, src/video.ts (full core), src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts, src/types.ts, src/index.ts (pattern scan + spot reads); test/video.test.ts, package-lock.json pattern-scanned.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
• Install scripts: none in package.json (scripts: build/dev/test only). Lockfile hasInstallScript only on dev-only esbuild/fsevents (via tsx). Runtime deps: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1, zod ^3 only.
  • Network egress: none. No fetch, no http/net imports, no URLs in code (only the Dockerfile OCI source label). No sockets at all.
  • Credential/env access: none. process.env does not appear in src/ at all.
  • Process execution — its job, done safely: src/video.ts:14,22 — the only executor is execFile(binary, args, {timeout: 120000, maxBuffer: 16MB}) from node:child_process, where binary is the literal union "ffmpeg" | "ffprobe" and args is a constructed string array (probe: -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>; thumbnail/trim/resize/transcode/frames/audio likewise fixed flag arrays with user values as single array elements). No shell option, no string interpolation into a command line, no exec/spawn string form, no remote code. Missing binaries surface as honest ENOENT tool errors.
  • eval / new Function: none.
  • fs writes: the package itself performs no fs operations; output files are written by ffmpeg to the caller-specified output paths (that is the tool's function).
  • Telemetry / data collection: none.
  • Obfuscation: none.
  • Dockerfile: two-stage node:20-alpine, npm ci, USER node; bundles no ffmpeg (host binaries used). No curl|sh.

docs.title: Verdict: CLEAN
docs.text: No egress, no env/credential access, no shell, no install scripts. The only execution surface is arg-array execFile of the host's ffmpeg/ffprobe, which is the package's stated job.

docs.title: Audit — Xod parts (scoped extraction candidates only)
docs.text:
• Repo: github.com/CloudCorpRecords/xod (MIT). The rest of the Xod app is OUT of scope (already decided: not adopting the app) and was not audited, except where an in-scope file delegates into it — those delegation points are named below.
  • Release version: 0.9.23 — app/version.py: VERSION = "0.9.23"; latest GitHub release v0.9.23 (published 2026-11-02).
  • Git HEAD (main): 6e5ebd4a0113bcf68800b6e034aa3d88e9b1f877 (2026-11-02T11:19:25Z), via gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/xod/commits/main.
  • Method: git clone is broken VM-wide (unable to write symref for HEAD: Operation not permitted) and codeload tarballs return 0 bytes through the proxy, so the re-clone into src/xod/ could not be completed by clone/tarball. Primary method used: gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/xod/contents/<path> (base64 content, decoded) and gh api repos/CloudCorpRecords/xod/git/trees/main?recursive=1 for file listings — slow (~10s/call) but reliable. Key evidence was re-verified through this route after the coordinator's environment update and matches exactly (sentinel.py stdlib-only imports and the llm_service delegation at :256/:265; agent_clis.py UNSAFE_FLAGS at :75, _safe_extra enforcement at :235/:469/:489, create_subprocess_shell install path at :867/:881). Supplementary full-file reads via raw.githubusercontent.com gave identical content/line numbers. Only src/xod/app/version.py (110 bytes) is persisted under src/; treat the per-file reads below as the audit record.
  • Files audited: app/services/sentinel.py (full, 316 lines), tests/smoke/run_sentinel_test.py, scripts/benchmark.py, app/services/scorecard.py (full), app/services/worktrees.py (full), app/services/agent_clis.py (1,105 lines / 60 KB — registry, env, run/session/install/login paths read in context), app/services/harness.py (853 lines — ONLY the crew_start / seat-record surface: tool manifest entries, invoke() dispatch, crew_read field whitelist, plus its _authorize gate).

docs.title: 1. app/services/sentinel.py — CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text:
• Direct egress: NONE — verified. Top-level imports are stdlib only (contextvars, json, logging, re, time, uuid, typing). No urllib/requests/httpx/socket/subprocess, no os.environ/getenv, no eval/exec, no file opens/writes anywhere in the file. The core review() is pure regex classification over in-memory turn state; decisions are kept in an in-memory LOG list capped at 100 entries.
  • curl|sh patterns are detection DATA — confirmed, not malicious: _REMOTE_RUN_RE matches curl|wget|iwr|irm … | sh|bash|iex|python in candidate actions so they get held; _SECRET_RES, _INJECTION_RE, _SAFE_DOMAINS are likewise detector patterns. The module's purpose is holding actions for an approval card.
  • Note 1 — delegated LLM egress in review_message(): this one async function lazy-imports app.services.llm and calls llm_service.chat_completion(..., task="sentinel") with the user's asked text (last 2,000 chars), the pending action's args (2,000 chars) and up to 3,000 chars of untrusted content, asking whether the action follows the person or the page. So sentinel.py itself opens no connection, but adopting review_message means that content goes to whatever LLM provider the host app has configured (the out-of-scope llm_service). Failures are fail-open for this check only (exception → returns None; the regex rules still applied). Extract review()/page_orders() alone and there is zero egress; extract review_message() and you inherit the host's LLM egress.
  • Note 2 — hold() side effects are internal: lazy-imports app.services.mcp_client (mcp_hub.pending[...], in-memory approval queue) and app.services.agent_log; _taildrop_ask_first() lazy-imports app.services.taildrop to read a setting. No network/file activity in sentinel.py itself at these points.

docs.title: 2. tests/smoke/run_sentinel_test.py — CLEAN (test only)
docs.text:
• Sets os.environ only to isolate itself: XOD_SPEECH=off (line 17, "tests never reach the speakers") and XOD_DATA_DIR = a fresh temp dir (line 20). All writes are under that temp dir (ran.txt, Receipts/, keep/).
  • The curl … | sh / iwr … | iex strings at lines 84–87 and the tracker/shady-example URLs are test vectors asserting sentinel holds them (and one asserting the exact user-given command is not held). Example API-key strings are fixtures for the secret rule.
  • It stubs the model: llm_mod.llm_service.chat_completion is replaced with a fake returning scripted verdicts (and restored), capabilities._chat_model and worker.llm_service.deliberate_stream are faked — the test makes no real LLM/web calls of its own. It does execute one real tool flow (computer_run_command) but only after simulating approval, inside the temp dir.

docs.title: 3. scripts/benchmark.py — CLEAN-WITH-NOTES (dev script)
docs.text:
• Egress: its own HTTP is only to the server it spawns: binds a free port on 127.0.0.1, launches uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 via subprocess.Popen (arg list, no shell), polls http://127.0.0.1:{port}/ and POSTs benchmark cases to /api/chat. One check fetches a page from 127.0.0.1:{http_port} it had the agent under test serve. No external hosts in the script.
  • Env: reads LLM_MODEL / LLM_PROVIDER / LLM_BASE_URL (defaults qwen2.5:14b / ollama / http://localhost:11434/v1) and passes the full os.environ plus overrides (XOD_DATA_DIR, XOD_FILES_HOME → temp dirs, XOD_AUTOCONNECT=0, LLM_*) to the spawned server. Consequence by design: benchmark chat content goes to the operator-chosen LLM provider — local Ollama by default, external only if the operator points --base-url/--provider there. (One built-in case, "a live answer" — Tokyo weather — makes the app under test use the web; that is the app, not this script.)
  • Shell note: helper runs(cmd) uses subprocess.run(..., shell=isinstance(cmd, str)). Its only string-form call site is the hardcoded "node index.js" check inside the temp work dir (running the project the benchmarked agent just built there, to verify it). All other call sites pass arg lists. Acceptable for a dev benchmark harness; not a remote-input surface.
  • fs writes: everything case-related lives in tempfile.mkdtemp dirs (work dir removed at the end via shutil.rmtree(W)); it creates a throwaway venv there. Persistent writes are only the results files it exists to produce: docs/reliability.json and docs/RELIABILITY.md in the repo (paths scrubbed of user names/home paths first, scrub()).

docs.title: 4. app/services/scorecard.py — CLEAN
docs.text:
• Read-only aggregation. No imports beyond json, time, typing; no env, no network, no subprocess, no file opens, no writes in this file.
  • It reads (a) the local recorded-events DB via dataset_recorder._conn() with parameterised SELECT-only queries over turns and llm_calls tables, (b) crew job state in memory (crew._load(), crew._jobs), (c) eval suite results via app.services.evals. Its own header is accurate: "Nothing new is recorded for it." (The recording of turns/LLM calls happens in those other services — out of scope here; scorecard itself collects nothing and sends nothing anywhere.)

docs.title: 5. app/services/worktrees.py — CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text:
• Execution: git is only ever run as subprocess.run([git, *args], …, stdin=DEVNULL) — arg arrays, no shell, no string commands (_git(), lines 41–46). Same for the gh call below.
  • Env: _env() inherits the process environment (via agent_clis._env() if importable, else dict(os.environ)) and adds GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GIT_EDITOR=true (never block on a credential prompt/editor). Env is passed to git/gh subprocesses — normal for git operations on the user's own repos.
  • fs writes — where: creates worktrees under DATA_DIR/worktrees/ (ROOT), branch xod/<name>; commits the job's changes there, merges locally, or removes the worktree/branch. That is the file's stated job.
  • Note — commit uses --no-verify: _commit() runs git commit -q --no-verify, i.e. repo git hooks are skipped for these automated job commits. Deliberate in code, worth knowing before adopting.
  • Note — the one egress path: pull_request() runs git push -u origin <branch> and then gh pr create --head … --title … --body … (arg array). That sends the branch + PR title/body to the repo's configured origin (the user's GitHub) — only when pull_request() is explicitly invoked; it refuses if there is no origin remote. No other network activity; merge/changes/remove are purely local git.

docs.title: 6. app/services/agent_clis.py — CLEAN-WITH-NOTES (strong notes on install())
docs.text:
• The --yolo refusal is REAL in code — verified: UNSAFE_FLAGS regex (lines 75–76) covers --dangerously…, --yolo, --yes-always, --full-auto, --bypass…, --no-sandbox, --skip-permissions, --allow-all, -y, --auto-approve, --trust-all. _safe_extra() (lines 208–214) raises CliError if any supplied extra arg matches, and it is enforced on every agent-launch path found: headless run() (line 235: args = […run template…] + _safe_extra(extra)), generic-program sessions via _program_argv() (line 469, when the program is a known agent binary), and session_start() (line 489). The headless run templates themselves (claude -p, muse exec, codex exec, gemini -p, …) contain no unsafe flags. Prompts are substituted into a single argv element, not parsed as flags.
  • Spawning is its job and is arg-array based: run() uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(path, *args, …); sessions use subprocess.Popen(argv, …) (PTY). One exception is install() (below) and search_path() running the user's login shell as [shell, "-lic", "printf %s \"$PATH\""] — a fixed literal string, no injected input.
  • Credential handling — presence only, verified: for each agent, signed_in file paths (e.g. ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.codex/auth.json) are checked with .exists() only — the header comment "only whether the file exists is checked; it's never read" matches the code (signed_in(), lines 164–173). key_env names (META_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, CURSOR_API_KEY, AMP_API_KEY) are checked with os.environ.get(...) for truthiness only; values are never read out, logged, or sent by this file. login() runs the agent's own login command and opens its auth URL in the browser (Popen(["open"|"explorer", url]), line 768) — Xod never handles a password.
  • Env note: _env() (line 128) passes a copy of the full os.environ (with PATH/TERM adjustments) to spawned agent CLIs. That is how those agents get their own API keys — by design — but it means any key in Xod's environment is visible to any agent it launches.
  • STRONG NOTE — install() is a real curl|sh execution path: the AGENTS registry hardcodes vendor install commands, three of them remote-script pipes — Muse: curl -fsSL https://muse.meta.ai/install.sh | bash; Claude Code: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash (Windows: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex); Cursor: curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash — others are npm install -g … / brew install … / pip-based. install() (lines ~867–895) executes the string via asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(...) in $HOME with the full env. Mitigations in evidence: the commands are hardcoded vendor-published installers (not user/remote-supplied, not configurable), and install()'s docstring states it runs "Only after the person's OK (the tool holds it as an approval card first)" — but that gate lives in the calling tool layer (out of scope), not inside install() itself. If this file is extracted, either drop install() or keep an equivalent approval gate in front of it.
  • Other egress: none from this file directly; the agents it launches make their own provider calls once running (their job). find() also returns each agent's install string as data to the UI.

docs.title: 7. app/services/harness.py — crew_start / seat-record surface only — CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text:
• The audited surface: the tool manifest entries (crew_start, kind "write", lines 484–487; crew_status/crew_read descriptions referencing the seat record, lines 489–490, 512–513), the invoke() dispatch for crew_start (lines 772–784), and the seat pass-through in _tool_crew_read (line 655 whitelists "seat" among the returned job fields; line 844 puts out.get("seat") in the envelope's verified block).
  • What it does: crew_start validates a non-empty task, then delegates verbatim to crew.start(task, folder, agent, kind) — with kind="board" requesting a board seat. The seat record itself (model requested / model that actually ran / how that is known) is created inside app.services.crew — out of scope; in harness.py the seat is opaque data that is only carried in and read back out. Within this surface there is no subprocess, no env access, no direct network code, and no file I/O in harness.py.
  • Gate — verified in code: every invoke() call runs _authorize() first (lines 208–228): (1) the beacon's Tailscale whois must say the caller IP is a device on the same account (same_account, else 403), and (2) the caller must present the harness_token setting in the X-Harness-Token header, compared with hmac.compare_digest (401 on mismatch; 503 — port closed — when no token is configured; a configured canary token presentation is logged as a security event and rejected). Work submitted still goes through the app's normal approval-card path; the harness adds no bypass.
  • Out-of-surface warning (same file, NOT audited in depth and NOT part of the seat surface): harness.py as a whole also contains a family-relay tier — _relay() uses httpx to call http://{member-endpoint}:{BEACON_PORT}/… on other family machines' Xod beacons, and task records are persisted to DATA_DIR/harness_tasks.json (capped at 100). Extracting only the crew_start/seat code does not bring these; importing the whole file would. Adopt the surface, not the file.

docs.title: Overall verdict for the Xod parts: CLEAN-WITH-NOTES
docs.text: No file in scope contains telemetry, obfuscation, credential exfiltration, or covert egress. The notes that matter for adoption: sentinel's review_message() delegates content to the host's configured LLM; agent_clis' install() executes hardcoded vendor curl|sh installers through a shell and relies on a caller-side approval gate; worktrees' pull_request() pushes to the user's origin and its commits skip git hooks (--no-verify); benchmark is a localhost-only dev harness whose spawned server talks to the operator-chosen LLM provider.

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Useful — yes, for the vendored part. Standalone, the real Xod sentinel.py passes all 24 pure review checks (S1–S6) and all 8 hold/approve/model checks (S7) with zero failures: unasked deletes, page-injected instructions, page-sourced recipients, download-and-run commands, and a leaked API key are all held with the right rule names, while everything the person actually asked for passes through. That confirms the earlier evaluation's live result and makes sentinel.py adoptable as-is for the provenance/injection gate (with the audit's note: review_message() delegates to the host's configured LLM, and hold() expects an mcp_client-shaped approval queue + agent_log, both trivial to provide, as the stubs here show).

Not proven by this run: S8 (researcher disambiguation — a different Xod component, not in this pull-in) and anything requiring the real Xod app (worker, capabilities, speech). The overall exit code 1 reflects the missing researcher component only, not a sentinel failure.
